<meta>This page is the primary title page of Oswald Croll’s seminal work, appearing after the owner’s personal introductory marks noted on the previous page. It establishes the theoretical and spiritual framework for the chemical and medical knowledge that follows.</meta>

->To God, the Best, Greatest, and Highest<- <note>original Latin: "D. O. M. A.", an abbreviation for *Deo Optimo Maximo Altissimo*, a common dedication in Renaissance texts.</note>

## BY OSWALD CROLL, VETERAN HESSIAN
# THE ROYAL CHEMISTRY
### CONTAINING:

->A philosophical description, confirmed by the experience of<-
->his own labors, and the use of the most select<-
->Chemical Remedies drawn from the<-
->LIGHT OF GRACE and NATURE.<- <note>The "Light of Grace" refers to divine revelation and scripture, while the "Light of Nature" refers to the study of the physical world through observation and alchemy.</note>

->*At the end of the book is added a new Treatise by the*<-
->*same Author on the Internal Signatures of Things.*<- <note>The "Signatures of Things" is the theory that herbs and minerals carry physical "signs" (like shape or color) that reveal their medicinal purpose—for example, a heart-shaped leaf being used for heart ailments.</note>

---

->With the Favor and Privilege of His Holy Imperial Majesty<- <note>Refers to the protection and publishing rights granted by the Holy Roman Emperor, Rudolph II, who was a famous patron of alchemy.</note>
->Published in Frankfurt at the expense of Godefridus Tampachius<-

***

### The Six Masters of the Art

*Top Left:* **HERMES TRISMEGISTOS OF EGYPT**
"That which is above is like that which is below." <note>original: "Quod est Superius, est Sicut id quod est inferius." This is the fundamental law of alchemy, suggesting that the laws of the heavens are reflected in the laws of the earth.</note>

*Top Right:* **GEBER THE ARAB**
"All things exist within the Sun and the Salt of Nature." <note>In <term>alchemy</term>, the "Sun" (Sol) represents the gold or the masculine vital spirit, while "Salt" represents the physical body or the crystalline principle.</note>

*Middle Left:* **MORIENES THE ROMAN**
"Let the hidden be made manifest, and vice versa." <note>Morienes was a legendary hermit-alchemist; this motto refers to the process of extracting the "spirit" from "matter."</note>

*Middle Right:* **ROGER BACON, ENGLISHMAN**
"Through the transformation of the elements, let the purified Trinity become the ONE." <note>original: "MONAS". The "Monas" represents the ultimate unity or the <term>Philosopher's Stone</term>.</note>

*Bottom Left:* **RAYMUND LULL, SPANIARD**
"At last, Water returns into favor with Fire." <note>Lull was a major medieval philosopher; this refers to the reconciliation of opposing elements in the alchemical vessel.</note>

*Bottom Right:* **THEOPHRASTUS PARACELSUS, GERMAN**
"Separate and lead toward maturity." <note>Paracelsus was the founder of <term>iatrochemistry</term> (medical chemistry); his motto refers to purifying substances to find their "essence."</note>

***

### The Two Worlds

**The Celestial Realm (Top Diagram):**
**The Infinite Good from the Light of Grace.**
This circle represents the divine hierarchy. It lists the nine orders of angels: Seraphim, Cherubim, Thrones, Dominions, Powers, Virtues, Principalities, Archangels, and Angels. At the very center is the Holy Trinity: **The Father (God)**, **The Son (Messiah)**, and **Man**, surrounded by the "Unapproachable Light" and the Hebrew name of God <note>The Tetragrammaton (YHWH)</note>.

**The Terrestrial Realm (Bottom Diagram):**
**The Finite Good from the Light of Nature.**
"Pray and work, counting all things vain except loving God and serving Him alone." <note>original: "Ora et Labora...", the famous Benedictine motto emphasizing that spiritual devotion and physical labor must go hand-in-hand.</note>
This diagram links four disciplines: **Theology, Magic, Astronomy,** and **Alchemy**. It shows how the **Soul, Spirit, and Body** are connected to the four elements—**Fire, Air, Water, and Earth**—and the three kingdoms of nature: **Animal, Vegetable, and Mineral.**

<summary>This is the elaborate title page for Oswald Croll's "Basilica Chymica," a foundational 17th-century text that merges Paracelsian chemistry with spiritual philosophy. It frames alchemy not just as a laboratory practice, but as a divine pursuit guided by both God and the study of the natural world.</summary>

<meta>This page serves as the formal dedication of Oswald Croll’s "Basilica Chymica" to Prince Christian I of Anhalt-Bernburg. The text introduces the author’s hesitations in publishing his work during a time of intellectual conflict and criticism.</meta>

### TO THE MOST ILLUSTRIOUS AND WISE PRINCE OF ANHALT

# CHRISTIAN,

## COUNT OF ASCANIA, RULER

### of Zerbst, and Lord of Bernburg, etc. His most
### clement Lord and Patron,

## THE DEDICATORY EPISTLE OF OSWALD CROLL.

<image-desc>Large decorative drop cap 'I' set within a rectangular frame featuring elaborate floral scrollwork and two small faces or figures at the top corners.</image-desc>As I was investigating with the full effort of my mind, most Illustrious and most worthy of all praise PRINCE CHRISTIAN, the greatest Glory of the ANHALT FAMILY, whether in these most deplorable times of ours—in which almost nothing is usually safe from the most petulant and envious slandering of the tongue—I should bring to light this, my <term>Royal Chemistry</term> <note>original: "BASILICAM CHYMICAM", Croll's famous work on Paracelsian medicine and "signatures" in nature</note>, which was compiled through various and long travels, labors, and tireless vigils, at no small expense, and finally by long observation and deliberate study, and written several years ago, and so undergo the perilous sea of public judgment: various obstacles occurred to me as I hesitated at the crossroads of uncertain decision. For those who, with just reason, turn themselves entirely in this most unhappy age of ours to the studies of true Wisdom, and—having left behind the vanities of the Heathens <note>original: "Ethnicis"; Croll refers to the non-Christian Greek and Roman authorities like Aristotle and Galen who dominated university education</note> and having despised the labyrinths of errors and Scholastic <note>The "Scholastics" were traditional academics who relied on logic and ancient texts rather than the "new" experimental chemistry favored by Croll</note> opinions founded upon sand—thereafter

<summary>In this dedication, Oswald Croll presents his major work on "Royal Chemistry" to Prince Christian of Anhalt, expressing his anxiety about releasing his long-researched findings into a judgmental and critical intellectual climate.</summary>
<keywords>Oswald Croll, Christian of Anhalt, Basilica Chymica, dedication, Paracelsianism, Scholasticism, chemical medicine</keywords>

--- Page 12 ---
<meta>This page continues Croll’s dedicatory epistle. Having previously described his hesitations, he now discusses the "iron age" of malice and envy he faces, but explains that his commitment to the "public good" and the "Spagyric Republic" outweighs his fear of critics.</meta>

<header>THE E P I S T L E</header>

<margin>
Search the Scriptures and Nature, in which the Miracles of God are hidden.
</margin>

*...principally* <note>The Latin text begins with the suffix "-ceps", likely completing "præcipue" (principally/foremost) from the previous page.</note> *to bestow their effort happily upon investigating the hidden Mysteries of Nature through diligent inquiry, and upon bringing those same mysteries to light through sagacious labor that conquers all things. And although they have undertaken an arduous, great, and laudable work, they are nevertheless accustomed to experience the diverse and often—without any merit of their own—most unjust judgments of the proud. For such is the fullness of Malice in this iron age of ours* <note>The "Iron Age" is a classical trope, used here to describe a corrupt and difficult historical period compared to a lost "Golden Age."</note>*, most alienated from virtue, that anyone is free to betray their own ignorance, wickedness, and the arrogance of a dishonest mind to the world by carping at the praised labors of others, so that almost nothing remains untouched by the envy of babblers. For while one envies the*

<margin>
The diversity of gifts does not cause strife among the good.
</margin>

*happiness of another’s genius, it happens that he begins to hate the very person he cannot imitate. Furthermore, lazy men entangled in worldly enticements, or burning with the desire for riches, are accustomed to despise those whom they perceive to excel in virtue, and who share the use and fruit of the Talent* <note>A reference to the Biblical Parable of the Talents, where servants are expected to increase the value of what God has entrusted to them.</note> *committed to them for the Praise and glory of* **GOD** *and for the common benefit of their needy neighbor. Nevertheless, having set aside all these hindrances, it was not Private but* **PUBLIC** *Advantage that finally conquered me—not an astral and ambitious desire to write, but a zeal for manifesting and defending Chemical Truth from the masks of impostors. My mind is most desirous of serving all the liberal and Philosophical geniuses of the Spagyric* <term>Spagyric</term> <note>original: "Spagyricæ"; a term used by followers of Paracelsus to describe the art of chemistry, specifically the "separation and recombination" of substances for medicine.</note> *Republic, both of the present and the future age. I am not ignorant*

<margin>
1 Peter 4, section 10.
</margin>

*that men (after the celebration and honor of the Creator) were created for the sake of other men, so that they might cultivate society through mutual studies and duties of friendship; and that they might both be able to help and benefit one another (since "man is a God to man"* <note>original: "homo homini Deus"; a proverb suggesting that humans act divinely when they help one another.</note>*) in the fear of the Most High, and also be bound by the law of the bond of Christian Charity. Therefore, let this offspring* <note>Meaning this book, the "Basilica Chymica."</note> *go forth, by the happy Will of God, under the auspices of the* **NAME OF THE MOST ILLUSTRIOUS ROYAL PRINCE CHRISTIAN...**

<meta>catchword: P I S</meta>

<summary>Croll defends his decision to publish his alchemical work despite the "iron age" of envy and malicious critics, arguing that the duty to share God-given knowledge for the public good and the advancement of chemistry outweighs personal risk.</summary>

--- Page 13 ---
<meta>This page continues the dedication to Prince Christian of Anhalt. The opening word "Prince" completes the sentence from the previous page regarding the responsibility of those who hold great "Talents" to use them for the public good under the protection of a noble patron.</meta>

<header>D E D I C A T O R Y .</header>

<sig>(:) 3</sig>

Prince <note>The Latin text "pis:" completes the word "Principis" (of the Prince) from the previous page.</note>: who, in his singular munificence, has made the labor of bringing this edition to light easy and ready for me. On this account, the entire Medical and Spagyric <term>Spagyric: A term used by Paracelsus and his followers for alchemy, specifically the art of separating and recombining natural substances to create potent medicines.</term> Republic will, after Immortal God, rightly acknowledge along with me that every resulting utility and gathered fruit is owed to Your Highness’s liberality. And so, to the perpetual memory and honor of Your name, even foreign nations shall enjoy it. Moreover, other Magnates <term>Megistanes: A term derived from Greek, referring to great lords or high-ranking officials of a kingdom.</term> will take an example from this, so that with the same incentives and spurs of resources, they might lift the spirits of many geniuses who have been cast down by the indignation of fortune and lie prostrate on the ground. Since they are most loving of virtue, they are gladly at hand for those devoted to virtue; by their kindness, favor, and munificence—imitating the ancient humanity of Princes—they may mercifully assist worthy men who are weighed down by the burden of poverty, yet desire and are able to serve the public good.

<margin>It is the duty of a Prince to promote the study of wisdom and to investigate the secrets of both Nature and Art.</margin>

Since for many centuries now, Illustrious Prince, it has been an established custom that new books be consecrated to Princes—whom it befits above all others to know the greatest mysteries and to be gifted with them—so that, protected by their patronage and favor as if by the aegis <note>original: "Minerva ægide". The aegis was the mythological shield of the goddess Athena (Minerva), symbolizing divine protection and wisdom.</note> of Minerva, they might be more strongly defended from the injury of envious slanderers. Such is the corrupt habit of this filthy world, where one person always envies and attacks the genius of another. For this reason, I did not hesitate to offer these labors of mine, and this gift of my nightly studies ascribed to the merits of Your virtues, to Your most Illustrious Highness, and to choose You as its Maecenas <note>Gaius Maecenas was a famous Roman patron of poets; his name became a universal term for a generous supporter of the arts and sciences.</note> and Patron. Thus, if certain wicked Sophists <term>Sophistæ: In this context, Croll uses the word to describe deceptive or trivial scholars who use clever but false arguments to attack true science.</term>, in the thick madness of envy and slander, wish to gnaw at this work, You may happily protect and defend it as Your own through the sharp-sightedness of Your discretion and the purity of Your judgment. For indeed, following the most praiseworthy example of the most ancient Kings, Princes, and Sages, among the few in this...

<meta>catchword: nostra (our)</meta>

<summary>Croll praises the Prince's financial support of the book's publication and argues that noble patronage is essential to protect scientific works from the "madness" of envious critics and "Sophists."</summary>

<keywords>patronage, Spagyric Republic, alchemy, Prince Christian of Anhalt, Minerva's aegis, Maecenas, defense of science, envy</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the formal dedication to Prince Christian of Anhalt. <header>E P I S T L E</header>

...you stand out as almost preeminent in our time, to whom God has granted such ability and dexterity of mind that he knows how to understand such offerings and weigh them with a correct examination. Regarding this, he can rightly rejoice and congratulate himself that—having known the supreme **TRIUNE GOOD**, the **DIVINE**, namely the **MACRO-** and **MICROCOSM** <term>Macro- and Microcosm: The "Great World" (the universe) and the "Little World" (man), based on the Hermetic belief that the human being is a reflection of the entire cosmos.</term>, as well as the **LIGHT OF NATURE** <term>Light of Nature: A Paracelsian concept referring to the innate wisdom and intuitive knowledge found within the natural world, as opposed to knowledge gained only through books.</term> and of **HIMSELF**—Your Highness can profess your own name in those most recondite sciences, than which there are no others more holy or excellent in this Sublunary world: namely, **Cabala**, **Magic**, and **Voarchadumia** <note>original: "VVoarchadumia"; a technical term used in Renaissance alchemy, specifically referring to the "Gold of Two Fires," a high-level metallurgical and spiritual art.</note>. These are the most chaste handmaidens of the eternal **WISDOM** of our heavenly Father, the only True one. By a singular kindness of Divine Providence, Your Highness is able to govern the State with most prudent scepter and, at the same time, learn in abundance the stupendous mysteries of the Philosophers and Sages.

This fortunate blessedness happens to scarcely one out of six hundred nobles, and is granted to not even one in a thousand of the leaders of the Republic of Letters. Therefore, distant posterity may one day rightly marvel that the traces of venerable antiquity were perceived and seen even in this dark age of ours, in the grandchildren and genuine heirs of that great **Ostanes** <note>Ostanes was a legendary Persian magus and alchemist.</note>, **Osiris**, and **HERMES THRICE-GREAT** <note>original: "TER MAXIMI HERMETIS"; referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the mythical founder of Hermeticism and alchemy.</note>. These are men who were able to see into, search out, contemplate, discern, and judge the most difficult entrances to hidden things. 

But lest I pour out too many words in perhaps an unsuitable place, I return within the boundaries of my purpose. It was therefore fitting by the best right to choose such a Patron and Prince, who, as was just said, could discern the crooked from the straight by himself: who would see with his own eyes, not hear with the ears of another, nor speak with the mouth of another, and to whom malicious men would not dare to say:

---

->White things are black, and black things are white.<-
<note>original: "Candida de nigris, & de candentibus atra"; a classical idiom describing those who lie or distort the truth by claiming opposites are the same.</note>

-># DEDICATION<-

Who moreover excels and abounds in the knowledge of the greatest arts and most secret matters, as even the most learned men, who know Your Highness intimately, admit with admiration. And regarding your admirable and Heroic virtues—like those of an **Armed Pallas** <note>original: "Armatæ Palladis"; Pallas Athena, the Greek goddess of wisdom and war, here used to describe the Prince's blend of intellectual and military prowess.</note>—alongside an invincible greatness of spirit revealed in the French expedition near **Rouen** <note>original: "Rotomagum"; the Latin name for Rouen, France. This refers to the siege of 1591–1592 where Prince Christian of Anhalt led troops in support of Henry IV.</note>, those present who saw with their own eyes <note>original: "oculata fide"; literally "with the faith of the eyes."</note> could never sufficiently praise you for lack of words.

Although, best of Princes, you are worthy of a far more precious gift, and your virtue deserves greater things, Your Highness will not disdain to receive with a serene brow <note>meaning: with favor and kindness</note> this small literary gift from a client (a monument of my humble respect and due gratitude toward you). And since fortune has not yet offered anything better, he will meanwhile value it, in his singular innate clemency, according to the spirit of the giver. Farewell most happily, unique ornament of all Princes of our age, and treasure of the light of grace and nature stored in the field of the Heart...

<margin>
The sacred **Triad** <term>Ternarius: The number three, representing the Trinity or spiritual completion.</term> must be led back through the **Dyad** <term>Binarium: The number two, representing duality or the division between the material and spiritual.</term> into the **Unity** of the author of all consummated Perfection. See John 17, sections 11, 21, 22, 23; 1 Corinthians 6; Psalm 145, section 21; Psalm 150, section 6; Psalm 148.
</margin>

...continue to unearth by most diligent and pious investigation—by asking, seeking, and knocking—the goodness, wisdom, and power of the most holy and ineffable **TRINITY**, to be acknowledged, looked up to, and celebrated. Continue until—once the dark and superfluous point of the **Quaternary** <term>Quaternarius: The number four, often associated in this context with the four elements or the "fallen" material world.</term> is sent away, and the purified, connective point of the **Ternary** is attained and reduced to the simplicity of the **Monad** <term>Monad: The "One," the ultimate source and divine unity in Neoplatonic and alchemical philosophy.</term>—after sufficient contemplation and understanding of the Super-celestial Virtues and Metaphysical Influences, our watch at last being over, we may again become **ONE** in that **ONE** itself, in blessed and immutable Rest, and in whom all things are **ONE**. To this One and Only let all Praise, Honor, Virtue, and Glory be offered and sung by every creature forever, Amen. From my study in Prague, in the year 1608.

--- Page 16 ---
<meta>This page serves as the legal protection for the book, following the personal dedication to the Prince of Anhalt found on the previous pages. It transitions from the author's private respect to the public, legal authority of the Holy Roman Emperor, ensuring the publisher's rights to the work.</meta>

## Imperial Privilege

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut headpiece at the top of the page featuring elaborate foliate and floral scrolls. Below the title, a large ornamental initial 'F' is decorated with intricate leaf-and-vine scrollwork, initiating the text block.</image-desc>

**FERDINAND II**
By the favoring mercy of God, elected Emperor of the Romans, forever August, and King of Germany, Hungary, Bohemia, Dalmatia, Croatia, Slavonia, etc.; Archduke of Austria; Duke of Burgundy, Styria, Carinthia, Carniola, and Württemberg, etc.; Count of Tyrol, etc.

We acknowledge and, by the power of this present Diploma <note>original: "Diplomatis"; a formal legal charter or state document</note>, make it known to all: That whereas Our and the Holy Empire’s faithful and beloved Gottfried Tampach, citizen and bookseller of Frankfurt, has humbly petitioned Us. Several years ago—with the assent and license of Oswald Croll, whom the Emperor **Rudolph [II]** <note>original: "Rudolphus"; the predecessor and cousin of Ferdinand II, famous for his obsessive interest in alchemy and the arts</note>, our most worshipful paternal relative and predecessor of auspicious memory, had graciously protected with a ten-year printing Diploma—the aforementioned publisher released the said author’s ***THE ROYAL CHEMISTRY*** <note>original: "BASILICAM CHYMICAM"; a foundational text of "iatrochemistry," which sought to use alchemical minerals for medicine rather than just making gold</note>. This work is filled with the most excellent experiments for chemical remedies, drawn from the light of Grace and Nature <note>In the philosophy of the time, the "Light of Nature" was the internal wisdom found within the physical world, while "Grace" was divine revelation</note>. In that undertaking, beyond the expense, he experienced no small amount of labor and hardship. Because he now desires to submit this work to the press once more for the sake of public utility, he has asked that We deign to make him secure for another ten years against the frauds of rivals <note>A common 17th-century term for "pirate" publishers who printed unauthorized copies of successful books</note> by granting an Imperial Printing Privilege. We, indeed, following our gracious desire that works timely for the protection of health should benefit the public, and that those who toil for that cause should be kept from loss, were unwilling to deny such humble prayers.

Wherefore, by our Imperial authority, to each and every printer, bookseller, and any others whatsoever involved in the book trade...

<summary>This page contains the official Imperial Privilege granted by Holy Roman Emperor Ferdinand II to the publisher Gottfried Tampach. It grants a ten-year monopoly on the printing of Oswald Croll's influential alchemical-medical work, the Basilica Chymica, to prevent unauthorized reprints.</summary>

<keywords>Ferdinand II, Gottfried Tampach, Oswald Croll, Basilica Chymica, Imperial Privilege, book trade, copyright history, Frankfurt, alchemy, Paracelsian medicine</keywords>

--- Page 17 ---
<meta>This page continues the Imperial Privilege granted by Emperor Ferdinand II. The previous page introduced the publisher Gottfried Tampach's request to renew the legal protection originally granted by Emperor Rudolph II for Oswald Croll’s alchemical masterpiece. This page details the specific prohibitions, the heavy financial penalties for "pirate" printers, and the requirements for legal deposit at the Imperial court.</meta>

<sig>(:)(:)</sig>

...[the craft of printing] practitioners, We seriously command that no one presume to reprint the aforementioned Oswald’s ***THE ROYAL CHEMISTRY*** <note>original: "BASILICAM CHYMICAM"; Croll’s famous work on iatrochemistry, which applied alchemical principles to the creation of medicines</note>, both as written in the Latin tongue and as translated into German, for a period of ten years—to be calculated from the first day of each edition’s publication—within the borders of the **Holy Roman Empire** and our hereditary Kingdoms and Dominions. This prohibition applies to reprinting in a similar or any other typeface or format, whether in whole or in part, as well as giving it to others to be reprinted, or bringing in, selling, or distributing copies printed elsewhere, whether secretly or openly, without the will and consent of the aforementioned **Gottfried Tampach** and his heirs.

If anyone, however, should do otherwise and dare to scorn, neglect, or transgress this Our Imperial Privilege, We decree that he shall not only be deprived of such books (which, being wrongly reprinted and brought in, **Tampach** and his heirs or agents may claim for themselves wherever they are found, whether by their own authority or with the assistance of a local Magistrate), but he shall also be fined the sum of ten marks of pure gold <note>A "mark" was a unit of weight; ten marks of gold was a massive financial penalty intended to be a ruinous deterrent for unauthorized printers</note>. We decree that this fine is to be paid in equal halves to Our Imperial Treasury—as the punisher of fraud—and to the use of the often-mentioned **Tampach** or his heirs, with all hope of pardon removed. 

This is provided, however, that the said ***ROYAL CHEMISTRY*** contains nothing scandalous within itself, nothing adverse to the **Orthodox Catholic Religion** or the Constitutions of the **Holy Roman Empire**, and nothing contrary to good morals, whether in the preface, the text, or elsewhere. Furthermore, the said **Tampach** must send at least three copies, at his own expense, as soon as possible to Our Imperial Chancery <note>The administrative office of the Emperor; this was an early form of "legal deposit," ensuring the state had a record of all protected works</note>. 

We therefore command all and singular Our and the Holy Empire’s subjects and beloved faithful within Our hereditary kingdoms and dominions, of whatever status, grade, order, condition, dignity, or preeminence they may be—both ecclesiastical and secular—but especially those established in the Magistracy who exercise the administration of law and justice in their own name or that of their superiors: that they do not permit anyone to rashly and with impunity transgress, violate, or scorn this Our Imperial Privilege. Rather, they should ensure that the stubborn, if any are found, are punished with the prescribed penalty and coerced by other suitable means, insofar as they wish to avoid the same fine and not incur Our gravest indignation.

*—and [I pray that] my pen (which is at least far lesser than all His mercies and bestowed benefits, and I both desire and hope for this in this publication) [may bring] praise and glory: also for the benefit and growth of my neighbor or rather the entire **Chemical Republic** <note>original: *Reipub. Chymicæ*; the international community of alchemists and physicians</note>, I bring forth here to you from the deepest chest of my heart most excellent **Spagyric Secrets** <note>original: *Arcana Spagyrica*; "Spagyric" refers to the alchemical process of separating and recombining substances to create medicine</note> (all of which have first been confirmed by me through my own manual experience, after many errors of expense, time, and labor).* <margin>Through my voluntary communication, some of these were even prepared by others for our Emperor **Rudolph** <note>Rudolph II (1552–1612), Holy Roman Emperor and famous patron of alchemy and the occult</note>.</margin> *I have neither been able to hear, nor to understand from the monuments of the ancients, that such things have come forth together and at once into the public light until this day. It has always been foreign to me to burden the reader with trifles and lies, of which our age (the dregs and sediment of the world) is quite fertile: much less to fill a huge volume (of which many lie hidden by me, collected through long-lasting labors) with the formulas of most tedious **Recipes** <note>original: *Receptarum*</note>,* <margin>Generally, the larger the Recipes, the smaller their virtues <note>A common alchemical critique: complex medicines with dozens of ingredients were often thought less effective than "pure" distilled essences</note>.</margin> *with which patchwork collections I now see students of Medicine overwhelmed and so entangled that they almost collapse and die under such a heavy weight of Recipes. However, what I have acquired with indefatigable diligence and curious exploration through nearly twenty years in my hardships and the laborious wanderings of various fortune through **France, Italy, Germany, Hungary, Poland, and Bohemia** from **Chymiatrists** <note>Chemical-physicians or iatrochemists who followed the teachings of Paracelsus</note>—men of the greatest experience and learning—partly by prayers, partly by price and exchange (to say nothing of my own discoveries found by the will of God through my own study in medical practice, and those not a few); preferring the common utility to private advantage, and moved moreover by Christian charity for the misery and necessity of the sick, in accordance with my fidelity to the medical Republic, I wished first to see and handle [these things] with "eye-witness hands," so to speak, having most thoroughly tested them by the **benefit of Vulcan** <note>original: *Vulcani beneficio*; Vulcan was the Roman god of fire; here it refers to the alchemist's furnace</note>, before they were gifted by me for the public benefit. In this way, the "sons of doctrine" <note>An alchemical term for students or initiates of the "Art"</note>, seekers and lovers of truth, may now obtain in a most excellent summary what I learned to my own great cost—namely, not deceptive opinions (as they have complained of until now in such a fertility of impostures), but the long-desired truth explored by many experiments.* <margin>It is a gracious thing, as **Pliny** <note>Pliny the Elder, Roman naturalist</note> testifies in his Letter to **Vespasian**, and full of noble modesty, to acknowledge those through whom we have made progress.</margin> *And thus also, once the course of a **Platonic Year** <note>original: *magni anni Platonici*; historically a vast cycle of time, here used metaphorically to mean a long period of refinement and return</note> has been completed, some things will return for free to their own people, whole and clothed in far more splendid attire than when I formerly received them from their authors half-ruined and at a price. For among some, to whom the rumor of many hidden **Secrets** <note>original: *Arcanorum*</note> had enticed me through tedious difficulties and expenses of journeys, their actual presence (as often happens) diminished their fame: so that they seemed to me either commonplace, which they were flaunting as secrets, or mutilated and defective, whose lack had to be filled by me from many descriptions reduced into one, confirming*

# ADMONITORY PREFACE.
### A 3
<meta>catchword: order</meta>

—nevertheless first proving the same by the test of my own fire: also through an exchange not harmful to them (according to that common Chemical custom, <note>original: καὶ Δὸς τί, καὶ λάβε τί</note> "Give something, and take something") often comparing my studies with theirs, they received an egg for a nut in mutual conversation; which nut being broken by long, laborious, and vain efforts, I finally found a rotten kernel, or obtained husks and pods instead of a kernel. From this it has happened that without Nature’s **Vulcan** <note>The Roman god of fire, here representing the alchemist's furnace and the essential practical labor of the laboratory</note>, the truest inventor and teacher of arts and mysteries celebrated by the poets, the greatest part of those (I say this saving the peace of such great men) who in our age have written about the more secret **Spagyric** <term>Alchemical preparations involving the separation and recombination of "pure" essences</term> preparations from the reports of others, rather than from their own manual experience, have brought this "fruit" to students of Chemistry: that for the most part, after great expenses placed in vain, they have finally given them the cause of both lost labor and a very long stretch of time.

Those who, not being satisfied with my example and the loss of others, prefer to examine such things thereafter by the service of **Pyrotechnia** <term>The art of using fire for chemical transformations</term> and Chemistry, and to become more cautious by their own peril, will willingly admit with me that the matter stands thus. And just as there are many things in words which are not found in deeds, so many things fall between Theory and Practice. He who desires to make another's danger his own and be deceived by those who were themselves deceived by others, will find this out by experience.

<margin>
Learn to be cautious by the warnings of others, lest you repent of the effort spent.
</margin>

Therefore, in this study, let no further faith be held in anyone than what each has found proven by his own experience—touching and seeing—through the proper test of fire, which judges the false from the true. And because, according to **Aeschylus** <note>The Greek tragedian (c. 525–456 BC)</note>, he alone is considered wise <note>original: ὁ χρήσιμα, ἐχ ὁ πολλ' εἰδώς</note> "who knows useful things, not he who knows many things," I have preferred to offer fewer and more select things, repeatedly turning over in my mind that saying of **Damascenus** <note>Likely referring to Johannes Damascenus, an influential 8th-century scholar</note>: *You must keep few **Medicaments**, whose powers and operations you have experienced many times.*

<margin>
See Anaxagoras in his little book *On the Wisdom of Nature* <note>original: περὶ της σοφῶν φυσικῶν; likely referring to a pseudo-Anaxagorean alchemical text</note>.
</margin>

Nevertheless, in this small number, I can confidently assert to you that in the majesty and pantry of all Nature (if you except that universal and most celebrated Medicine possessed by the most ancient wise Philosophers from the founding of the world, and celebrated even unto a miracle for its legitimate heirs), there are scarcely any more select or effective things lying hidden than these principal Secrets of the more hidden medicine here offered: <note>original: ὁ γὰρ ἐν τῷ μεγάλῳ τὸ εὖ, ἀλλὰ ἐν τῷ εὖ τὸ μέγα</note> "For the Good is not in the Great, but the Great is in the Good."

<margin>
The fruit and greatest utility will more than sufficiently compensate for the labor spent by the craftsman.
</margin>

He who, by devoting himself more sincerely to Philosophy, duly approaches the innermost sanctuaries of Nature with a pious assiduity of preparation joined with a diligent contemplation of natural causes—and who, moreover, does not shrink from the labors and difficulties of experience—will, from this revealed bosom of Nature and by the skill of manual operation (if the grace of the favor of the Most High has been poured into him), bring forth far greater things than they seem to promise at first glance. However, although the powers to each in order—

<summary>Croll argues that true alchemical knowledge comes only through "Vulcan" (the fire of the laboratory) rather than book learning. He warns against "rotten" theories and insists that a few well-tested remedies are superior to a vast collection of unverified recipes.</summary>

<meta>catchword: prisons</meta>

<margin>
*He who, because of the laziness of his intellect, does not obtain his desire, should attribute the fault of his ignorance and lack of skill not to a defect of nature, nor to me, but to himself.*
</margin>

*...assigned in their proper order, I, by whom the medicine is made, have not personally tried every single application, even though I have performed the preparations themselves in actual work. Nevertheless, because I have found the most important part to be true through medical use, I address those **Spagyrists** <term>Alchemists who practice the "Spagyric" art—the separation of components to extract pure essences and their subsequent recombination</term> who are advanced and practiced in **Chemical** labors—namely, the "sons of the art." These men are skilled in its terms and have drunk from the fountains of true Philosophy; they can, even at a glance, render a fair judgment of these things and reach a conclusion by easy conjecture. (For these preparations—having nothing in common with the common rabble of Alchemists—require an artisan who is not stiff-necked or of dull wit, lest through a most shameful slander <term>he should think the faults of the craftsman belong to the craft</term> <note>original: τὰ τεχνίτου σφάλματα, τῆς τέχνης εἶναι νομίζῃ</note>). To those practical and <term>hands-on</term> <note>original: ἐγχειρητικοῖς (enchiiritikois) — referring to manual or laboratory skill</note> artisans, I say, there will be no doubt that the remaining powers—having been proven by the most expert **Chymiatrists** <term>Physicians who used chemical and alchemical medicines, a movement led by Paracelsus</term> through long use and certain experiment, and now published in this one work—will undoubtedly satisfy the vow and eager expectation by providing the desired effect. Therefore, true and more profound Physicians—inspired by a divine spirit and moved by **Samaritan mercy** <note>A reference to the biblical parable of the Good Samaritan, emphasizing compassionate care for the sick regardless of their status</note> toward their suffering neighbor of whatever lot or condition—who, in the fear of GOD and by a suitable and skillful method, legitimately use these things by their own labor (unless they wish to be cheated of the desired effect by using things prepared by others, which is often done sophistically and fraudulently), will learn by experience even far greater efficacies and virtues during the process of healing. This is especially true if the medicines are offered according to the nature of the sick person and the judgment of the physician present, which I could not and should not assign here; as **Truth, the daughter of Time**, will teach by the will of GOD.*

<margin>
*Ignorance is the inseparable companion of Pride and Wickedness.*
I.
</margin>

*But into what waves do I now throw myself with this public service? What, I ask, should be done in this gamble and diversity of judgments? What is to be done in such a crop of detractors who gnaw at even the best things in the worst way? I shall intrepidly hold out a shield to protect myself—namely, the shield of my sincerity and my zeal for serving the **Spagyric Republic**. This shield will not fear the proud judgments of the unskilled, and it will easily blunt all the foreseen arrows of my adversaries: namely, Wrath, Slander, Envy, and supercilious contempt, which is the truest witness of Ignorance.*

*First, the more secretive **Hermetic Philosophers** <term>Followers of the mystical and alchemical traditions attributed to Hermes Trismegistus</term> will rise up against me and be gravely angered; these higher secrets were previously understood by them in part. They will complain that an injury is being done to them if those things—which were sought out with the greatest study over long intervals of time and have been suppressed until now in deep silence—should so suddenly see the light and be communicated to the common crowd of men. They will call me a breaker of the Chemical seal, because, not having been initiated into the mystical **Pythagorean silence** <note>The silence required of followers of Pythagoras; here meaning the tradition of keeping alchemical secrets hidden from the uninitiated</note> and being unmindful of the **Hippocratic law** <note>The medical oath or tradition of "holy things for the holy" (τὰ ἱερὰ ἱεροῖς)</note>, I bring the Chemical Truth out of the prisons of shadows and Envy...*

<summary>Croll defends his decision to publish secret "Spagyric" medical preparations, arguing that while he hasn't seen every clinical result, the formulas are verified by practice. He anticipates backlash from elite alchemists who believe these "holy" secrets should never be shared with the public.</summary>

...hitherto held back, I have liberated; and having freed it from its chains and opened the doors, I have kindly communicated it to posterity. Truly, because these men are the heirs of Wisdom and citizens of the Philosophical Kingdom, they have closed the window of Envy and are (or at least ought to be) always lovers of **GOD** and neighbor. With heads held high and Cabalistic eyes, they will not be unaware that in the true **Cabala** <term>A mystical Jewish tradition often adapted by Christian alchemists to find hidden meanings in scripture and nature</term>, **Magic**, and **Voarchadumia** <term>original: *VVoarchadumia* — a technical term for the art of refining gold and a deeper mystical alchemy</term>, far more powerful treasures have been set aside for them. Through untiring labors and vigils, by the Light of **GRACE** and **NATURE**, these things shall at last, in the progress of Time, be manifested to all without distinction. This will occur once the **BLOODY JUDGMENT OF THE SON** has passed, and the **WATERY JUDGMENT OF THE FATHER** has undoubtedly followed, until finally, in the **THIRD** age—the century of the **HOLY SPIRIT** (which is to be renewed by **FIRE**, for the sake of manifesting what is hidden)—**ELIAS the Artist, the Restorer** <term>original: *HELIAS Artista Reparator* — a legendary figure in alchemy predicted by Paracelsus who would reveal all secrets of the art at the end of time</term> of all things shall arrive. For one may clearly gather that a specific age is destined for each Person of the Trinity from the twelve articles of the tripartite Apostolic Creed, which correspond appropriately to the twelve hours of this great and unique Day of the enduring World. 

And so, to a grateful posterity, experienced in the Natural Light of Chemistry and incited by **GOD** toward these preparations (the beloved heirs, that is, of Science and Wisdom), they will in no way begrudge me these present crumbs. For these **Chemical Secrets** <note>original: *Arcana hæc Chymica*</note> will remain well untouched by unpracticed, lazy, or ignorant despisers due to their lack of skill in manual operation. Likewise, there will be no danger of comprehension or perception by the profane, the wicked, and the unworthy regarding the theological mysteries mixed in at the appropriate place (in speech that is brief but sufficient for those who are meant to understand), because they lack the spirit of Wisdom and possess a slowness of wit.

<margin>Such men seek praise for their intelligence through theft and the slander of their benefactors.</margin>
The spurious and bastard **Theophrasteans** <term>Followers of Theophrastus Paracelsus; here Croll refers to those who claim his authority without his virtue or skill</term> (the most wicked race of men) will not cease to most furiously accuse my sincerity. They take it very badly that they can no longer peddle their deceitful impostures—sold for great sums through feigned experience, fictional friendship, painted piety, and various vain promises—to those who have minds least prepared for caution and deception. Nor is the crafty cunning of certain men easily revealed by their face or clothing; while catching opinions from the gatherings and conversations of others, they subsequently suppress the names of their benefactors to hunt for a reputation of learning, wisdom, and prudence among the great nobles. These things, which they have obtained from other good men through a multitude of tricks—namely, through their own fallacies and chameleon-like cunning...

But since*

<margin>
4. Alchemy is twofold: Natural, held in great value by the sons of Art; and Sophistical, which is utterly detested by those same men.
</margin>

*But the more coarse and foul faction—those who have abandoned the truth and taken error as their companion—being entirely unrefined and lacking in all human kindness and true philosophical learning, will most of all harass my goodwill toward the Commonwealth with their haughty mockery. Indeed, since according to the Comic writer <note>A reference to the Roman playwright Terence, who wrote that nothing is more unjust than an ignorant man</note> nothing is more unjust than these cursed Chemical-haters <term>original: *Misochymicis*; from Greek *misos* (hate) and *chymia* (chemistry)</term> and Wisdom-haters <term>original: *Misosophis*; from Greek *misos* (hate) and *sophia* (wisdom)</term> buried in their own ignorance, it is no surprise that the minds of these men, submerged in the mud and dust of the schools, can perceive nothing sublime. On the contrary, they prefer to die in the old path and their own thick ignorance rather than be considered disciples of those over whom they have arrogated the power to teach.*

*Let it seem a wonder to no one if these insolent and manifest despisers of Nature's secrets—bristling at the mere mention of the Name of Chemistry—have not feared to mock this most divine art until now without any shame. With a certain foolish and barbaric arrogance, they impudently tear it apart with every kind of insult. Like dogs barking at things they do not know, they angrily pursue and unworthily mangle an art which they have never even greeted from the threshold.*

*This is partly because they lack Divine Wisdom due to the foolish ignorance of their minds and their ambitious stupidity; they have no other weapons with which to fight against the Truth and trample the scattered pearls than those supplied to them by their leader, that **Binary Calumniator** <note>original: *Binarius ille Calumniator*; in Pythagorean and Hermetic thought, the "Binary" or number two represents division, falling away from unity, and is often associated with the devil or the source of all error</note>. It is also because they have no other cause for their "Cyclopean" anger or madness—which ought to be deported to Anticyra <note>An ancient Greek city famous for hellebore, a plant used in antiquity to treat madness and melancholy</note>—than their own ignorance of legitimate chemical preparation, as they themselves confess both publicly and privately.*

*But since there is no desire for what is unknown, and to pass judgment on unknown things as if they were correctly understood is not only foolish but borderline disgraceful, how, I ask, do such scholastic Doctors dare—or how can they legally be allowed—to condemn the uncommon studies of uncommon men? For due to their poverty of intellect, they have never even entered the Sanctuary of Nature. And why do they unjustly usurp the titles and honors of Philosophy and Medicine, and receive public salaries for their names, if those noble works in which the entire power of Nature flourishes are viewed by them—when they are finally confronted by the truth—with the same ignorant wonder that common people feel for "magic" miracles?*

*Nor do they cease to despise many of the most famous physicians of our age—men who should be compared to the most learned of scholars—who have spent their entire lives engaged in the practical works of the art and are most skilled in the Secrets of Nature. They despise them because (although these physicians are sufficiently instructed in both the old and new Medicine, as much from reading the most approved authors as from the experience of the "Light of Nature" <note>A Paracelsian concept referring to the innate wisdom and divine guidance found within the natural world</note> itself, which is entirely unknown to common physicians) they reject those most vain honors of the world, and "Doctorates" as they call them, and those authorities and titles by which*

# ADMONITORY [PREFACE]
<sig>B 2</sig>

<margin>
The world is ruled by opinions.
</margin>
<margin>
God is the first book for eternal life; for from God comes the Rule of life.
</margin>
<margin>
The Firmament or Heaven with all it contains is the second Natural book for mortal life: for physical science is to be drawn from the Stars.
</margin>
<margin>
The happiness of the present life consists in the knowledge of Nature; therefore, after eternal things, the highest pursuit in temporal matters is the investigation of the secrets of Nature.
</margin>
<margin>
A physician of this kind, as an eminent master of Earthly Light, feels no regret.
</margin>
<margin>
See Agrippa <note>Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa (1486–1535), a famous polymath and occult writer.</note>, Book 6, Epistle 6.
</margin>
<margin>
Worldly doctors do everything out of a desire for money and their own honor...
</margin>

...and they would not blush at the wretched recognition and confession of errors, follies, and foolish persuasions—having applied a healthy repentance and first laid aside the obstacles to the sciences, namely Opinion and Pride—as if returning from exile, even in old age (for it is a beautiful thing for an old man to study Wisdom, and like Diogenes <note>Diogenes the Cynic, an ancient Greek philosopher who valued practice over theory.</note> in the stadium, not to slacken his pace while running) to shed old age in imitation of the wise serpent, and having assumed a new skin, to become disciples of this Chemical art. They should consume their future days with the Secrets both in GOD and in Nature; and alongside the great book of GRACE (from which comes the eternal salvation of our Soul), they should also more exquisitely scrutinize the other book which deals with the secrets of NATURE, looking toward the health of the body. They must not leave untouched the chief treasures of Nature, in which the medicines for the most serious diseases have been placed by the Most High. 

Lest they should mourn and be buried in an unhappy error among the dead shadows of surfaces or external <term>Galenic Qualities</term> <note>The traditional medical system based on the four humors (blood, phlegm, black bile, yellow bile) and their qualities (hot, cold, moist, dry).</note>, they have built for their old age a *place of labor* <note>original: πονηθεῖον (*ponetheion*)</note> and a Temple of Nature, like a most honored monument. From this, alongside a clearer knowledge of the Creator (which they reached as much through the diligent searching and admiration of the works of GOD as through the laborious examination and <term>Philosophical separation</term> <note>The alchemical process of breaking down substances to find their pure essences.</note> of Creatures or Natural things), they have also obtained this extraordinary fruit of their labors, vigils, time, and expenses: so that when they are subsequently called to the bedsides of the sick as physicians confirmed by much experience—where it is not the *garrulousness* <note>original: πολυγλωττία (*polyglottia*), literally "many-tongues" or excessive talking.</note> of a physician for debating, but rather his *practical skill* <note>original: πολυπραξία (*polypraxia*), meaning effective action or experience.</note> for healing that is required—there was no longer a need to attempt things in the art which he desires to patch up with external allurements. 

That is to say, they no longer need to seek excuses through a numerous multitude of duties and defend their ignorance by softening their speech, as the supercilious crowd of physicians is accustomed to do. These common doctors court at least the wealthier patients for the sake of infamous gain, while neglecting the "little rustics" of narrower fortune, as they call them, being terrified by the difficulty of the first and foremost duties. From this same "bran" or "chaff" of the common crowd, there is such perversity and malice in some that the medical inventions and secrets of the <term>Chemists</term> <note>original: *Carbonariorum*, literally "charcoal-burners," a derogatory name used by university doctors for alchemists which Croll here reclaims.</note>—which they secretly snatched up with a deceitful desire to learn and which they notice they can use with success and profit—they then annihilate, reject, and condemn with swelling words, and prohibit to the public as if they were poisons. Meanwhile, they claim the due praises of the author for themselves, and by a lying and inverted theft, they strip the inventors and benefactors of the arts of their earned honors, so that they might more conveniently and with greater ostentation [sell] these medicines acquired through these tricks as their own...

<margin>Medicine is wonderfully inscribed by God, the illuminator, in the Book of Nature—that is, in Heaven and Earth—to be read and investigated there through Chiromancy <note>Usually palm-reading, but here meaning the study of the "lines" and features of the natural world</note> and Physiognomy <note>Judging the inner nature of a thing by its outer appearance</note>.</margin>

For Philosophy teaches the powers and properties of Earth and Water, just as Astronomy teaches those of the Firmament and Air. Philosophy and Astronomy create an internal and perfect Philosopher, not only regarding the Macrocosm <note>The Great World; the Universe</note>, but also the Microcosm <note>The Little World; Man</note>. It is therefore necessary to adapt the disposition of the Macrocosm, as if it were a parent, to the Microcosm, which is its son—namely, Man—and to properly compare the World’s Anatomy with the Anatomy of the Microcosm. The external world is the Theoretical Anatomy, a mirror in which the lesser world, Man, is seen; for from Man himself, the wonder and excellence of his structure and creation cannot be fully grasped by a physician as much as is necessary.*

<margin>Without knowledge of the Light of Nature <note>The innate wisdom or intelligence found within the natural world, put there by God</note> or the greater World, no physician can have an exact knowledge of diseases and the Microcosm. The Macrocosm is the Theory and the mirror of the Microcosm, Man. The end goal of Philosophy and Astronomy is Man.</margin>

*Moreover, they correspond not in external form or bodily substance, but in all powers and virtues. Just as the great world is, so also is the small; in essence and internal form they are clearly one and the same; only the external form distinguishes the World and Man. This is made most evidently clear to us by the Light of Nature, which is nothing other than a certain divine analogy of that visible world with the microcosmic body. For whatever lies hidden invisibly in Man is manifested in the visible Anatomy of the entire universe, because the microcosmic Nature within Man is invisible and beyond comprehension. Therefore, in the visible and comprehensible Anatomy of the great world—as if in its parent—all things are manifested. The parents of Man are Heaven and Earth, from which Man was ultimately created; and he who knows and anatomizes the parents has attained a true knowledge of the son, Man—that most perfect creature—in all his properties. This is because all things of the entire universe flow together in him as if into a Center; and his Anatomy in his own Nature is the Anatomy of the entire universe. The external world is the figure of Man, and Man is a hidden world, because the things that are visible in the world are invisible in him; and when they become visible in him, then there are diseases, not health, since he is a microcosm, not the world. The Platonic Rings and the Homeric Chain are nothing other than the Order and Series of Things serving Divine Providence, a graduated and linked Sympathy of Things.
</margin>

*The things of the Earth and of the Water have conspired into one Republic, citizens of the same Anatomy; therefore, they mutually cherish each other through society and a pleasing exchange of actions. This is the oft-celebrated Golden Chain* <note>original: "Aurea Catena"; a classical and Neoplatonic concept where all levels of existence are linked from the lowest matter to the highest divinity</note>, *the society of visible and invisible Nature, this marriage of Heaven and Earth* <note>original: "Cœli Opisq;"; Ops was the Roman goddess of the earth and fertility</note>, *these Rings of Plato, this philosophy hidden in the innermost sanctuaries of Nature, for the sake of obtaining which we know that Democritus, Pythagoras, Plato, and Apollonius traveled to the Brahmans* <note>original: "Brachmannes"; ancient Indian philosophers/priests</note> *and the Gymnosophists* <note>original: "Gymnosophistas"; meaning "naked philosophers," a term used by Greeks for certain Indian ascetics</note>, *and likewise to the columns of Hermes in Egypt. This, therefore, was the study of the most Ancient Philosophers, understood by them from the Light of Nature by the singular inspiration of GOD, in which the admirable and infinite power of our Creator and His incomprehensible Wisdom shines forth, so that we cannot sufficiently admire and proclaim His inestimable Goodness in his creatures and the Infinity of his ineffable mysteries.*

*Nor should this be passed over in silence: that there are THREE Principles of all things, which are found in any compound. For it is very well known that those things into which natural bodies are resolved* <note>broken down through chemical processes</note> *are also the very parts of which they consisted from the beginning of their composition: No body composed by Nature can be divided by the art of dissolution into more or fewer than Three: <term>Mercury</term> (or liquor), <term>Sulfur</term> (or oil), and <term>Salt</term>. In these three, every created thing is generated and preserved: For the Holy TRInity, through its TRI-une spoken word FIAT* <note>original: "Let it be done"</note>, *created all things as a TRI-UNE <term>Spagyric</term> <note>Spagyric analysis refers to the alchemical practice of separating a substance into its components and then recombining them in a purified state</note> analysis witnesses: God through the word FIAT produced the first matter, which by reason of the three Principles contained within is first triple, and afterwards these three species were separated into four different bodies or Elements, not otherwise than if a skilled craftsman makes Red Lead* <note>minium</note>, *White Lead* <note>ceruse</note>, *Glass, and the Spirit of Saturn* <note>lead acetate</note> *from Lead. Thus the World with all created bodies is nothing other than coagulated smoke, from three substances, namely Sulfur, Salt, and Mercury: for these three are the matter from which all bodily things are created. This can be demonstrated by the Spagyrics* <note>alchemists</note> *through visible experience and undeniable certainty: In green wood, three types of moisture also exist: The first is watery, corresponding to fugitive Mercury, which preserves the wood from burning; the second is quite fatty and oily, which provides the cause of inflammation and burning like Sulfur; and these two are consumed by fire. The third, however, is unctuous and small in quantity, and remains in the ash (namely Salt); it is subtle and permanent. In the same way, the cause of the material human body is Earth...*

Genesis, chapter 1.

No Element can exist without the others; instead, a mixture of the four Elements is always found in the generation of all things.

Paracelsus, in his *Paramirum* regarding the "Being of the Stars" <note>original: "de Ente Astrorum"; one of the five influences Paracelsus believed governed health</note>, says that Air was created before all other creatures.

For the Air, the fruits proceed from the Center to the circumference; there they achieve their coagulation and perfection. The seeds of the Water give birth in the bosom of the Earth, then tend toward the surface. The Earth, however, leads its fruits out into this circumference in which we live and thrive: for grain produced in the Earth is gathered in the Air above the Earth. In this way, the offspring of all the Elements hasten with a voluntary impulse toward the Human Province, as if toward a desired goal, and with a kind irrigation, they cherish all parts of Nature. So also we see this happen by the immutable decree of eternal law: that Water produces no more than the Earth can nourish, the Air can cherish, and the Fire can consume. Likewise, Air is twofold: it also has its own Element within itself, as if it were an inhabitant. It is the Balsam* <note>original: "Balsamum"; a vital, life-preserving internal fluid or force</note> *of all created things and the life of the remaining three Elements; no subtler Element was created by God, for it lives by itself and gives life to all. Without it, neither the Firmament, nor Water, nor Earth could produce their fruits; indeed, Fire could not burn without air, much less could the "Coals of Heaven"—that is, the Fire of Growth—shine. Similarly, the Firmament or Fire is also twofold: and it has its own Element within itself as an inhabitant, and that Element contains all the Stars and seeds within it. Just as fire increases itself in wood, or in any suitable material, one Fire always arises from another. Angels cannot multiply themselves because they have no body; Man can multiply himself by means of the body. All growing things—herbs, trees, fish, birds, animals—can multiply themselves by the benefit of the body in this way (for a Seed or Star can do nothing without a body). As soon as the Seed or Star dies and putrefies <note>original: "putrescit"; refers to the alchemical stage of *putrefaction*, where matter breaks down to be transformed.</note> in its matrix, then the Star moves forward into a new body and multiplies itself. Christ himself uses this likeness and example from Nature when he speaks of the grain of wheat which, cast into the Earth, dies by putrefaction and finally bears much fruit or many grains, which have the same power as those from which they descended. Putrefaction consumes and separates the old Nature and brings forth the new fruit. Therefore, eternal Life cannot exist in any body unless it has first died, because death is the cause of the body's glorification in eternal Life, just as corruption is the cause of a new generation of Divine substance. The first life of herbs and medicines must necessarily die so that, through the **Putrefaction** and **Regeneration** performed by the work of the **Chemist** <note>original: "Chymicus"; a practitioner of alchemy and laboratory medicine.</note>, a *second life* may be obtained. # P R E F A C E

<meta>catchword: because</meta>

<margin>The anatomy of bodily diseases must be sought from the internal Stars, or from the impressions that cause them; this is more necessary for the physician than the local anatomy of corpses.</margin>

*...Therefore, once the external World is known, the **Philosophical Physician** <note>original: "Philosophicus Medicus"; a doctor who understands the hidden chemical and spiritual laws of nature, not just physical symptoms.</note> also understands the Physical Body of Man, which takes its nourishment from the Earth and its life from the stars of the Firmament. He sees that the Physical Body is nothing other than **Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury** <note>original: "Sulphur, Sal, & Mercurium"; the "Three Primes" (Tria Prima), which Paracelsian alchemy held as the fundamental components of all matter.</note>—for all bodily things, as said a little before, are contained in these three. He sees that growing things arise not from the four visible Bodies <note>the four elements: Earth, Water, Air, and Fire.</note>, nor from the four humors, but from an invisible **Seed**, just as a herb or a tree grows from a seed. It is not the **Local Anatomy** <note>original: "Anatomia Localis"; the dissection of physical organs in a corpse.</note> of the microcosm and of corpses, but the **Essential and Elemental Anatomy** <note>original: "Anatomia Essata & Elementata"; the study of the spiritual and chemical essences that form the "blueprint" of the body.</note> of the world and the microcosm that reveals both diseases and their Prescriptions. The members of the great world (the macrocosm) are the Remedies for the members of the microcosm, by bringing the external and internal Anatomy into harmony, not by pitting "degree against degree" <note>A critique of Galenic medicine, which treated "hot" diseases with "cold" remedies; Paracelsus argued for treatment by similarity.</note>. Just as there is one Anatomy for man and woman, so there is one Anatomy for diseases and medicines. Just as there is a "Man of disease" within a human, so there is a "Man of medicine" within the Remedy. And although the hidden virtues of Herbs or the stars of the Physician's Heaven may be known to us, the physician must especially strive to know the **Concordance of Nature**—namely, how the Star of Medicine or of the magical Heaven is to be harmonized with the internal Star and Olympus of Man. Because of this similar Anatomy, **Mummy** <note>original: "Mumia"; a medicinal preparation made from human remains, believed to contain a "vital balsam" that could stop bleeding.</note> stops human blood. The nightingale, subject to diseases from spiders, is restored by eating them: for the External leads to the Internal; as it is in the great world, so it is in the small:*

<margin>The foundation of true physicians: the Anatomy of Diseases and of Things.</margin>
<margin>The cause and subject of diseases.</margin>
*Therefore, he who knows the growth and fruits of the Earth, herbs, and trees—realizing that they all proceed from a seed or from the stars—simultaneously knows that various diseases lie hidden in the Physical Body. These diseases do not arise from four fictitious humors or qualities, but rather, through the Analogy of the greater and lesser worlds, they arise in various ways from a seed. Once the diseases of the macrocosm are known, the diseases of the microcosm (man) are no longer unknown:*

<margin>Many diseases arise from the minerals of the microcosm (which the Illiadus contains within itself).</margin>
*As many species of minerals as there are in the World, there are just as many in Man. For there are as many kinds of diseases as there are species, bodies, and seeds of growing things. The number of diseases cannot be known unless one knows the number of all growing things. For in the Elements that are compatible with Human Nature, seeds are fostered, as are the celestial, Aerial, Aquatic, and Terrestrial stars, which—at their digested and appointed times—produce the fruits of health or the heralds of disease:*

<margin>The origin of diseases is from the three first principles upon which the Stars can impress something, just as Fire acts on wood or straw, or saffron on Water.</margin>
*Thus, the **Three Primes** <note>original: "tria prima"; Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury.</note> are the cause of all diseases. In whatever body these three agree through a state of union, that body can be judged truly healthy. But where they do not (since Health consists in a balanced Temperament), it must be clearly established that disease and the first root of death have entered. Hereditary diseases produced from the seed or the Stars are partly called Elemental,*

Specifically, from the Fire of the Firmament come all arts, crafts, languages, and faculties. Just as a magnet, by attracting iron, draws out the spirit of Mars <note>In alchemy, Mars is the planetary correspondence for iron.</note> and leaves behind the rust, so Man has a double Magnet by reason of his body. For on one hand, he draws the <term>Stars</term> to himself, and just as bees draw honey from flowers and herbs, so he draws his food from them—namely, worldly Wisdom, the senses, and thoughts. On the other hand, by his own attractive power, he draws daily nourishment for his flesh and blood from the Elements. And just as the Elemental body attracts elemental bodies through hunger and thirst, so the star-like spirit of Man attracts all arts, sciences, and faculties, and all human Wisdom, from the rays of the higher stars. For the Firmament is the **Light of Nature** <note>original: "Lumen Naturæ"; the divine spark within nature that allows humans to understand the world through reason and observation.</note> which flows all natural things into Man. 

Furthermore, the <term>Stars</term> or Elements (which are spirits) are <term>without qualities</term> <note>original Greek: "ἄποια" (apoia); meaning they possess no inherent physical properties like heat or moisture in their pure, spiritual state.</note>, being neither hot nor cold, nor dry nor moist; but the things produced from them are endowed with qualities. For from the Earth come the Poppy, Opium, and cold Darnel; while the Spearwort and Water-pepper are hot. Indeed, contrary things grow from the same Elements. From Fire grow Snow, Rain, Dew, the Rainbow, Winds, Thunder, Hail, Lightning, and all similar atmospheric impressions, produced from the three first principles <note>Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury.</note> by the <term>Archaeus of the Firmament</term> <note>original: "Archæo Firmamenti"; the "internal chemist" or governing spirit of the heavens that directs the formation of weather and celestial phenomena.</note>. These are the fruits and "excretions," as <term>Paracelsus</term> says, of the stars of the Firmament; indeed, they are the fruits of the invisible Stars which exist within the visible stars, making the invisible visible. For the Stars, like earthly trees, provide their own fruits. 

From this it is clearly evident that diseases are not cured by opposites—as if heat ought to drive out cold, or as if the Elements themselves should be expelled from Man. Rather, they are cured through secret essences or <term>Stars</term> which the physician, by the benefit of <term>Alchemy</term> <note>original: "Chymiæ"; the art of chemical transformation.</note>, can reduce from the "final matter" back into the "first matter." These secret essences are neither cold nor hot in their action; they remove all diseases just as an axe cuts down a tree, even though the axe itself is neither cold nor hot. Of this kind also are <term>Quintessences</term> <note>original: "Quintæ Essentiæ"; the "fifth element," a highly purified and potent alchemical extract.</note>, <term>Magisteries</term> <note>original: "Magisteria"; medicinal preparations where the core essence of a substance is extracted while preserving its full power.</note>, and the like.

There are, however, two spirits in Man: one is the sidereal spirit from the <term>Firmament</term> <note>The sphere of the stars.</note>, and the other comes from the breath of life; from the mouth of the Most High comes the intellectual Soul inspired by God. For just as the World was hidden in the invisible Waters above the Abyss, so Adam lay hidden in the world. The First Matter became the world, and the Great World became Man. 

Just as a Tree grows from a seed—the seed being both the Beginning and the End of the Tree, because in every grain or seed of the Tree another Tree is again hidden—so the First Matter (which Paracelsus calls the <term>Limbus</term>, the "Earth" of which was the WORD of the Lord) was the seed of all things to be created. Man was the last among all, like a perfect seed, which can again produce from itself another Man such as he is. And although Man is not one seed and then another, he nevertheless has the power to emit seed from himself, from which a similar Man is produced, just as he is. And as Adam carries the whole world and all created things in himself and is preserved by the world, so everyone born from him carries the same things he carried—namely, the whole world—and is also carried and preserved by it just as Adam was. All Men are one Man, from flesh, blood, and spirit.

It follows that three Worlds or Heavens are also found in Man, and that he is governed by three Worlds—or rather, he is every World, and the most thoroughly examined Model of the entire universe. For this reason, he is called by some the **Fourth World**, in which all those things are found which are in the other three, and for that reason, he is judged worthy of the name "Every Creature." For he has his Spirit or Mind from **GOD**. For what is the Spirit of Man inspired by the Most High other than God himself dwelling in us? Now the Stars (for I do not speak of the seven visible "Coals of Heaven," that is, the physical bodies of the Stars, but of the invisible and insensible body of all Things, or the Astral Spirit) are nothing other than the virtues of the Angels: but the Angels (feeding themselves only on the sight of GOD) are the created wisdom of GOD. From this it follows that he who knows God also has knowledge of the Stars; and once the Stars are known, the World cannot be unknown, and thus subsequently the world’s offspring, Man. The Stars form and produce all corporeal things from themselves, and in producing these bodies they also multiply themselves: just as the seed of Grain or Wheat is a Star—namely, an invisible body—which, when cast into the Earth, produces from itself a visible body and generates many other Stars from itself. So it happens in other growing and living things. A Star is nothing else than an insensible, invisible body, or a living Spirit, yet without Reason in growing things; but in those possessing life, such as Man, it is with reason, and is diverse, just as the forms of different Things are diverse. Bodies, however, are nothing more than the **Excrement of the Stars**, produced into corporeal existence by their operation. Any Star can, through itself—as by imagining or forming—produce through operation another Star enclosed in a body. For no body exists without a Star, just as, conversely, no Star exists without a visible body. Since the Imagination of Man is not one but all Stars, it certainly produces not one, but many operations: And although Imagination is incorporeal and invisible, when it is exalted and joined to a most firm Natural or Innate Faith, like the **Gate of Miracles**, it is the source and beginning of all Magical operations, and without detriment or diminishment to the Astral and sidereal Spirit—*

To this end, the Poet <note>likely referring to Horace</note> said that nothing is blessed in every part; thus Man, though a partaker of Divine Nature and Master of all living things, must endure his own "shades" and the furies that torment him.

<margin>God's rigid justice is disease and poison in all things: On the contrary, God's Mercy in Nature and in all things is medicine.</margin>
Roger Bacon, the English Philosopher, says that God, who creates Darkness and Light, placed a great Medicine therein for His **MERCY**; yet in that same place, by the power of His incomprehensible justice, He joined **POISON** as a guardian—namely, the briars and thorns of the rose—as the inseparable companions and avengers of our transgressions. Good cannot be known without evil, and once the enemy is recognized, damage can be avoided. So too writes the most ancient theologian, Holy Hermes <note>Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</term>, along with the author of Ecclesiasticus in the *Key*: all sublunary things must consist of opposition and contrariety. Because of the generation and corruption of things, it is otherwise among the impossible things <note>original: "τῶν ἀδυνάτων"</note>.

<margin>
Wisdom 18, verses 15–16.
Sirach 39, verse 36.
Ecclesiasticus 33, verses 15–16.
Ecclesiastes 3, verse 14.
Ecclesiastes 7, verse 15.
Sirach 42, verse 25.
</margin>
For all things act against the laws when they have nothing to fear; nor can Man reach the highest summit unless, with a hand always active, he establishes himself for his own salvation through the course of the struggle.

<margin>The cause of sympathy and antipathy.</margin>
For God, through His wisdom, has so ordained that there is antipathy <note>original: "ἀντιπάθεια"; a natural aversion or "feeling against"</note> just as much as there is sympathy <note>original: "συμπάθεια"; a natural affinity or "feeling with"</note>. Nature wished to move mortals to contemplate and unearth her secrets through this spectacle, so that if one thing dreads another, the Hated thing might repair or heal the defects of the things you envy. For this reason, Heraclitus says Nature was born from War, and Homer calls it "contention." Man is his own enemy; the cause of our dissolution and death is this "Kingdom divided against itself," namely an internal duel. In the microcosmic body <term>microcosmico: the human body viewed as a "little world" that mirrors the macrocosm of the universe</term>, because of the joining of adverse things, a perpetual struggle lies hidden, acting as both the preserver and the destroyer of health. For this reason, the Saints called the mortal body "Hell" and "Purgatory," in which one must always wage war.

<margin>Sirach 38, verse 15.</margin>
Therefore, since the Anatomy of Death has found a home in the Republic of Life, Nature has commanded that physicians be ministers and separators <term>separatores: alchemical practitioners who use fire to separate pure medicine from impure dross</term>, not masters or composers. Remedies require preparations, separations, and exaltations before they can unfold their hidden and bound virtues. Just as all things are tested by Fire, so too must the examination of the science of medicine be conducted in the fire. Medicine and...
