# TO THE ADMONITIONS

<sig>G</sig>

Chemistry and Medicine cannot be separated: for Chemistry—not that kind which impostors use for their **Whitenings** and **Reddenings** <note>original: "Dealbationes & Rubefactiones," terms for alchemical processes often associated with fraudulent attempts to make silver or gold</note>—reveals not only true simple substances, great wonders <note>original: "Magnalia"</note>, secrets, mysteries, virtues, and powers concerning healing, but it also teaches us to imitate the **Archeus of the Stomach** <term>Archeus of the Stomach: the "internal chemist" or spiritual force believed to govern digestion and the separation of nutrients from waste</term> or the **Innate Natural Chemist**. It teaches how to set apart every mystery into its own reservoir and to deliver medicines, which are covered in "unfortunate garments," by a proper separation from impurities and the corruptible, foul mixing of superficial and external elements. This is done so that the pure and crystalline matter, or Nature in its simple form, may be offered to our bodies. But to deliver this matter from its prisons and captivity: **This is the task, this the toil** <note>original: "Hoc opus, hic labor est," a famous quotation from Virgil's Aeneid regarding the difficulty of returning from the underworld</note>.

It is a province worthy for all physicians to grow old in, and one full of practice; for indeed, without Alchemical Philosophy, all Medicine is dead. Without the knowledge of Alchemy, Medicine can be neither theoretical nor practical. He who, terrified by its difficulty, refuses it, searches for the locations of diseases in vain. In this regard, we must not imitate our common physicians, who seek protection for their own laziness from the late-night vigils and discovered labors of others. They are accustomed to committing the preparation of medicines to Pharmacists who are, for the most part, negligent and greedy—I do not speak here of those conscientious ones who serve the Commonwealth with faithful diligence like the Alchemical Vulcan <note>Vulcan was the Roman god of fire and the forge; here used to describe the hard-working chemist at his furnace</note>—to the great disadvantage of the sick.

For through this artful resolution <note>meaning the "breaking down" or analysis</note> of bodies, those properties will come into view which were previously hidden by the power of their composition. Furthermore, as if by an artificial **guiding star** <note>original: "cynosuram," referring to the North Star</note>, Alchemical Physicians have set their sails not only toward all the shores of Nature, but even toward the admiration, contemplation, and perception of the entire Creation itself, and of its most hidden virtues. They have attained distinguished knowledge in many things, and not without merit. Therefore, in this true analysis of bodies and **vital Anatomy**, it is necessary for the physician to be practiced (as was said above), because there is no constant property of any body which is not found in either the **Salt**, the **Mercury**, or the **Sulphur** <term>Tria Prima: the "Three Primes" of Paracelsian alchemy—Salt (stability/body), Mercury (fluidity/spirit), and Sulphur (flammability/soul)—which were thought to be the fundamental components of all matter</term> of that same body.

<margin>Vegetables include plants, trees, and zoophytes <term>zoophytes: organisms like coral or sponges once thought to be intermediates between plants and animals</term>. Animals include beasts, ordered as Reptiles, Swimmers, Flyers, and Quadrupeds.</margin>

First, however, all composite bodies of the lower globe are to be distributed into three orders or choirs: into **Animals**, **Vegetables**, and **Minerals**. Then, the individuals of all these must be diligently examined, as well as the parts of those individuals. Thus we shall find in each order the illustrious differences of the Three Primes: for in the workshop of Nature there is animal, vegetable, and mineral **Salt**; there is animal, vegetable, and mineral **Sulphur**; and likewise vegetable, animal, and mineral **Mercury**. The first face of things was pure and whole...

# PREFACE

...perfect without corruption and death: For God, the highest Maker of all things, by His own will and for His infinite glory, created all things good, so that all might glorify Him and live holily and incorruptibly according to the prescribed order.

<margin>
Sirach chapter 38, section 15.
</margin>
Man was first created healthy (for diseases take their first origin not from the man but from the woman <note>This reflects the common 17th-century theological view that Eve's role in the Fall brought mortality and sickness into the world</note>); but once he entered the world, he gave birth to an opening for death. Because two opposites appeared—the external corruptible part and the internal whole part—they could not remain together for long without corruption following.

<margin>
By the calamity and arrival of diseases, a **Transplantation of the Creature** occurred; after the fall, mortals carry an enemy in their own breast—both by reason of their creation and their propagation—causing diseases and death through their innate contrariety and corruption.
</margin>
Therefore, after the transgression and the falling away from unity into "otherness" <note>The move from divine simplicity to the divided, conflicted state of material existence</note>, new Tinctures (an **iliad of woes** <note>original Greek: "ἰλιὰς κακῶν," a proverb meaning a vast number of troubles</note>) arrived through the Divine curse. By their mixing into a disastrous fate, the beauty of the whole Creation was transplanted together with the world’s calamitous companion [Man]: Impurity was joined to pure roots, and that was the predestination of diseases. For the roots of diseases do not exist separately in uncertain individuals or species, but are implanted and mixed with the pure and primary seeds of things. Truly, the nutrients of natural things are the fruits of seeds flourishing in the four matrices or Elements. Nature, therefore, as it now is, has given us nothing pure in this sublunary realm, but has mixed all things with mingled impurities. This was done so that she might instill in us this **Chemical science** <note>Referring to Alchemy as the necessary tool for purifying nature</note>, to be learned from infancy as if by a certain prod of necessity, so that while we are expelled from Paradise into the outskirts of this world,

<margin>
He who learns to know God and himself has cultivated the Earth well.
</margin>
we might cultivate the EARTH—that is, the whole machine of the world—in admiration, investigation, and knowledge of both the **Visible and Invisible Mud** <note>original: "Limi Visibilis & invisibilis." This refers to the "slime" or "dust" from which man was formed, both his physical body and his spiritual essence</note>. And in preparing food and other things necessary to sustain this present life, we should be occupied like laborers of Nature, not in the shade but in the **sweat of our brow** <note>A reference to the curse of Adam in Genesis 3:19</note>. In this way, He [God] might rouse our industry in this **EARTH OF LABOR** through the imposition of the Cross, which must be borne patiently, to obtain the fruits of Earthly and Heavenly Wisdom. This ensures we might not waste away, sluggish, in idle and most foul laziness, or (being more prone to all vices and sins) learn to do evil by doing nothing.

<margin>
Through excessive license, men become worse or similar to beasts.
</margin>
<margin>
Through labor, **Idleness—the pillow of Satan**—is driven away.
</margin>
And this is the true Purpose of Man’s Creation: that in the Fear of GOD and love of neighbor, he should labor upon the Earth to recover what was lost—not to be idle, but by walking in the **Light of Nature** <term>Light of Nature: a Paracelsian concept referring to the innate wisdom or divine intuition through which humans understand the natural world</term>, not according to his own will but the Creator’s. Thus he remains an Instrument, a Dwelling, and a Tabernacle of GOD. To avoid evil and idle thoughts, he should walk in the Ways of the Lord; that is, in his own works, through the observation of things Temporal and the consideration of things Celestial, he should investigate the miracles of GOD through Nature, and make manifest the Invisible works of GOD, celebrating with admiration the infinite Wisdom, Power, and unceasing [goodness] toward the hu[man race]...

Sirach 39:39-40.

...to the human race in the unveiling of His wonderful works, wonders, and mysteries, to His goodness. But leaving aside food, we must now come to medicines, in which no one is so stiff-necked—unless he prefers to find his harvest and yet still eat acorns or husks with their shells like the people of a prior, more primitive age—who will disapprove of this **Separatory Art**. This art teaches us how to rightly discern and separate the Good from the Evil, the Useful from the Useless, the <term>Narcotic</term> <note>The "deadly" or "numbing" properties</note> from the Fire, the mineral spirit from the <term>Anthos</term> <note>original: "Anthos," Greek for flower; here referring to the most delicate and potent floral essence</note>, the homogeneous from the heterogeneous, and poisons from medicines and healthy balsams. It separates Light from Darkness, Life from Death, Day from Night, the Visible from the Invisible, and the pure, heavenly kernel and marrow from the impure, earthly husks, membranes, coverings, shells, pods, and dross. It teaches how to separate the "garments" and "dwellings" of medicines—which are often hostile to human bodies—from the "Inhabitant," the Soul, the <term>superelemental mystery</term> <note>A spiritual force residing within matter that transcends the four basic elements</note>, and the Quintessence. This is clearly the internal <term>Balsam</term> <note>The inherent healing power or preservative force within a substance</note> of our own bodies, and by separating it properly, we find it to be suitable, friendly, and harmonious. Thus, that life-giving essence alone is collected; once its bonds are loosened, its power rises higher and displays itself more readily, putting forth much greater and more effective strength for healing bodies than before.

For even all poisonous things possess a Balsam agreeable to Human Nature. There is no poisonous animal that does not contain within itself an <term>Antipharmacum</term> <note>original: "Antipharmacum," an antidote or counter-medicine</note> for its own poison; in its own kind, the animal is good. While it may be poison to a Human, it is often familiar food to another animal: thus spiders benefit hens and sparrows, toads benefit serpents, and serpents benefit deer and storks. These extracted "Forms" of medicines perform more work than when they are submerged in raw matter, which usually hinders and breaks the power and operation of the <term>Arcanum</term> <note>The "secret" or vital core of a medicine</note>. Indeed, the Soul or specific "Form" of any thing has many more and more excellent virtues and operations than either the body or the raw matter of that same thing. Since every thing has its "being" from its Form, the more of the Form one has, the more one has of its true Essence. This is a fact that even those who hate <term>Chemistry</term> <note>original: "Chymiæ"</note> cannot deny, being forced by their own consciences and convicted by ocular demonstration.

<margin>
Reasons why <term>Spagyric</term> <note>A term for alchemical medicine, derived from the Greek words for "separating" and "recombining"</note> medicines, when properly prepared, are to be preferred over many of the <term>irregular</term> <note>original: "Heteroclitis," meaning anomalous or disorganized</note> mixtures of the apothecary shops.
</margin>

And from this, many advantages follow. **First**, because of the smaller quantity of the medicine, the sick may take it much more easily and freely. Many patients are often so difficult that they would rather exchange life for death than swallow full cups of those thick and muddy potions which corrupt the constitution of the human body—potions which even the Physician prescribing them and the Apothecary mixing them would, in a similar case, refuse to drink out of horror. **Second**, that by the use of these [Spagyric medicines], even if repeated, the stomach is not harmed, since nothing stands in the way...

# P R E F A C E

<margin>
Poison transformed into a <term>Secret Remedy</term> <note>original: "Arcanum"; in alchemical medicine, this refers to the pure, celestial essence of a substance stripped of its physical dross</note> is no longer poison, but proves to be a superior medicine. In this way, the **Terrestrial Planets** <note>Alchemical shorthand for the metals: Lead (Saturn), Tin (Jupiter), Iron (Mars), Copper (Venus), Quicksilver (Mercury), and Silver (Moon)</note> are cleansed of their **Leprosy** <note>A term used by alchemists to describe the impurities, corrosion, or "immaturity" found in base metals</note>, and the most offensive odors are turned into a sweet fragrance through **digestion** <note>The process of using gentle, consistent heat to break down and mature a substance</note>.
</margin>

...[performing] their action less efficiently. For when substances are separated <note>referring to the chemical extraction of medicinal spirits from the raw plant or mineral bulk</note>, they are carried by the stomach's natural drive to their familiar destinations without any obstructive side-stops. They affect the body very quickly and are, in turn, affected by it. Thus, their harsh and earthy parts, which might otherwise cling to the internal organs and cause sores, cannot make regular users chronically ill—as often happens with the frequent use of common, unrefined drugs. 

Thirdly, in these essences, every harmful quality (if it cannot be entirely removed during the initial preparation) is either completely taken away or at least more easily dulled by being mixed with other highly refined substances. 

Indeed, we cannot deny that this **Spagyric Art** <note>The "art of separation and recombination," a term coined by Paracelsus to distinguish medical alchemy from gold-making</note> is so essential that physicians cannot do without it without great risk. For in a single simple substance, the components are often dissimilar and marked by contrary properties: one may be harmful while the rest are healing. This is evident in **opium** and honey, which cannot be truly understood or discerned without the aid of this art and the separation of their substances. 

Even the **Galenists** <note>Traditional doctors who followed the ancient Greek theories of Galen, often relying on herbs and the "four humors" rather than chemical extractions</note> can only defend their own core principles by the benefit of this art. They claim that all bitter things are "hot" in nature, yet Opium—despite being extremely bitter—is famous for its power to numb or stupefy <note>Properties usually associated with "cold" substances in Galenic theory</note>. Likewise, Roses and Chicory, though bitter, are typically used for cooling. The knot of this contradiction must be cut by the **Anatomical Knife of Fire** <note>A poetic term for the alchemist's furnace, which "dissects" a substance into its elemental parts</note>. Thus, by performing a separation of substances, we can discern the true Nature <note>original: "Temperaturam"</note> of simple medicines. In Opium, we will find a sweet Narcotic **Sulfur** <note>The oily, soul-like component of a substance</note> and a hot, bitter **Salt** <note>The physical, crystalline body of a substance</note> which, through subtle refinement, moves the sweat without any numbing power.

What is truly wondrous—as skilled doctors know, who understand how to draw benefits and usefulness out of disadvantages—is that metallic poisons, though most deadly, can be so corrected and improved through the service of this art and the **Judgment of Fire** that they can be safely ingested into the body. Arsenic is a clear example of this: its unbridled malice can be fixed and tamed by the benefit of **Vulcan** <note>The Roman god of fire; here used to mean the alchemical furnace</note> using saltpetre <note>original: "salem petræ"</note>. 

For minerals, whose spirits surpass our own in subtlety, and precious stones should not be excluded from the list of medicines. When rightly prepared, they are far superior to plants <note>original: "Vegetabilibus"</note> in curing diseases. First, because such great power and strong actions could not be imprinted upon softer matter, such as that of plants and animals, since they seem barely able to hold them. Furthermore, it would be impossible for plants—which are themselves prone to decay—to rescue the human body from corruption in the same way that the spirits of perfect metals do, as they are subject to no corruption.

Secondly, it is clear that minerals and "imperfect" metals <note>Metals like iron or lead, which were seen as "sick" versions of gold</note> are endowed with great medicinal virtues, as is seen in surgical medicines, where hardly any...

Thirdly, because Nature—wishing to create Animals and Plants fit not for just one action, but for many virtues and functions—was least able to balance the mixture of those bodies in such a way that they might attain those admirable powers and admit the solid and stable **Nature of a Balsam** <note>original: "Balsami Naturam"; in alchemy, this refers to a preservative, life-extending essence inherent in a substance</note>. All things are from one principle, and tend toward one: in the "Night" of Orpheus and the "Hades" <note>original: "Orco"; the underworld or hidden state of matter</note> of Hippocrates, all things are one, as even the Anaxagorean **panspermia** <note>Greek: πανσπερμίᾳ; the theory that "seeds" of all things are present in all matter</note> testifies—though it was poorly understood and unfairly accused by Aristotle. But after that single Nature, Essence, and Matter of all things enters onto this worldly stage, according to the will of **GOD**, which is the **Specification** <note>the defining characteristic that makes a thing what it is</note> of every Creature, it puts on various bodies of manifold distinction and wonder along the way, according to the disposition and variety of the Place and Receptacle: and also according to the agitation and operation of the **universal spirit**. Here grow the Vegetables, there the Minerals arise, in another place the Animals are generated, and one always yields to the nourishment of another. For this order is prescribed for the sublunary economy: that Minerals provide food for Vegetables, these for beasts, and beasts for humans—which could not happen unless the nature of one participated by affinity in the nature of another, and this by the proximity and closeness of the first genus from which all things proceeded.*

<margin>Book 1, chapter 19. The three first principles of Milk are Whey, Butter, and Coagulated Cheese; for all earthiness is Salt.</margin>
*Furthermore, the Chemical method of refining, extracting, and separating* was lacking in **Galen’s** <note>Galen of Pergamon (129–216 AD), a Greek physician whose theories dominated Western medicine for over a millennium.</note> time and was not much in use (for they were not able to separate the husks and barks from the kernel). This method was utterly unknown to [Galen] himself, though he desired it with great longing without knowing it: as can be understood from his own words when, [writing] about the powers of simple medicines and the need to distinguish between the hot and cold parts of vinegar, he said he would undergo all dangers if he could find some machine <note>original: "machinam"; here meaning a device or technical method</note> for the separation of contrary parts—in vinegar as it is in milk. If he had been skilled in the art of distillation, he could easily have obtained his wish in this matter. Nor indeed should it be imputed as a disgrace or reproach to **Hippocrates** <note>The "Father of Medicine" (c. 460 – c. 370 BC).</note> or **Galen** that they were ignorant of these things: for **GOD** and **Nature** (which is the order and series of Divine works, and obeys the power of **GOD** and His words and commands, and borrows its strength from Him), doing nothing in vain, do not pour out all things to the human race at one and the same time. Instead, they successively communicate particular gifts to certain ages; they do not bestow all things on one person, but distribute a particular gift to each. From this it appears how different the judgment of many Ancients was. If there was something they themselves did not know, but which they heard was known by others even in distant regions, they underwent every danger of sea and land for the sake of learning it thoroughly. Undoubtedly, if **Galen’s** age had fallen in the time of **Paracelsus**, he would have venerated his erudition without envy, and he would not have been ashamed of the **Coals** <note>A reference to the charcoal used in alchemical furnaces; critics often mocked alchemists as "sooty charcoal-burners."</note>. As greedy as he was for learning, he would not have refused to serve **Theophrastus** <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim, known as Paracelsus (1493–1541), the Swiss physician who pioneered the use of chemicals and minerals in medicine.</note> himself for free for several years to learn the separation of the "three firsts" <note>The *Tria Prima*: Salt, Sulfur, and Mercury—the three fundamental components of matter in Paracelsian philosophy.</note> in vinegar, as well as the preparations of higher **Magisteries** <note>technical term: *Magisterium*, a medicine prepared by a "masterly" process that retains the full power of the source material.</note> and **Elixirs**. Finally, he would not have refused to take the place of a Bellows-blower, a Clay-mixer, or a Night-watchman; he would have accepted any condition that would help him learn this excellent science. This is despite the vain anger of those "Philerastic" <note>original: "Philerastis"; likely used here as a derogatory term for physicians who are more lovers of their own cliques or traditional "friendships" than of truth.</note> physicians, both Choleric and Melancholic, who, since they were scarcely **Beginners** <note>original: "Alphabetarii," literally those still learning their ABCs.</note> in **Spagyric Medicine** <note>term: *Spagyrica*, a branch of alchemy focused on separating and recombining the medicinal virtues of plants and minerals.</note>, and knew nothing of the Creation and Composition of the **Internal Astral Man** <note>The "Astral Man" is the spiritual or celestial body that Paracelsus believed governed the physical body and linked it to the stars.</note>, much less of the **Mechanical Spirits** of diseases, yet do not blush to rashly and presumptuously leap over the barriers of shame. They do this by attacking the never-sufficiently praised **Paracelsus**, the immortal glory of **Germany**, who is a thousand times better than his adversaries (and who, beyond what can be believed, [mastered] all divine sciences)...

### ADMONITIONS ###

...[of things] Divine and Human, he possessed absolute knowledge. Not understanding him, to their own disgrace, they maliciously attempt to suppress him with vain effort. They have pursued the conduct of his life with viper-like hatred, exaggerating his human vices; and so, with great rashness, they establish an unjust law for themselves: "No one lives without vices; he is best who is burdened by the least." <note>A reference to the Roman poet Horace: "nam vitiis nemo sine nascitur; optimus ille est, qui minimis urgetur."</note> They do not see the travel-pouches that hang behind their backs <note>This refers to the ancient fable that every person carries two bags: one in front containing the faults of others, and one behind containing their own.</note>, as if they themselves were not also men, subject to those very vices which they attack—or perhaps subject to even greater ones, or having been so once, or remaining liable to become so. They should have endured his human imperfections (which are approved by no one) with the same spirit of mercy with which they pardoned the Galenic impiety that mocked the school of Moses and Christ. ->P R E F A C E.<-

<margin>
4. The Pillars of Medicine: Philosophy, Alchemy, Astronomy, and Physics (which is also Virtue, or Medicine).
</margin>
...judgment, Truth and lies are treated as equals by this malicious world. Almost everyone, inflamed by the pursuit of gold-making <note>original: *Chrysopoeia*; the alchemical art of transmuting base metals into gold</note>, neglects the proper preparation of medicines. The sole cause of this is that they do not understand the True Philosophy of Paracelsus or his Metaphysics. Nor do they first diligently study those great books pointed out by Theophrastus <note>Theophrastus von Hohenheim, the birth name of Paracelsus</note> in his *Labyrinth of Physicians* before they approach the preparations, separations, and true analysis of natural things. I also see many Chemists who commit themselves to royal courts being led away from the truth by the splendor of courtly business and deceived by vain courtly flatteries, so that they either neglect those great works of God or, rather, become unfit for such stupendous miracles of God. I have observed for many years now that many begin well, but, deceived by these trifles, end badly. For this reason, this Divine *Spagyria* <note>original: *Spagyria*; a term for alchemical medicine involving the separation and recombination of natural elements</note>—an admirable and proven art—is slandered without cause by the unrefined masses (as usually happens to the best of things). Despite being a proven science, it lies despised alongside higher branches of knowledge even among those intent on this business, and it is looked down upon as if it were not a means of earning one's daily bread. What is said regarding abuse, imposture, and evil arts are not reasons why a thing otherwise good can or should be condemned. For what thing, if you abuse it, cannot be turned to a man’s destruction? Indeed, the better a thing is, the more destructive its abuse becomes. And who dares to oppose those "Athenian Thrasos" <note>Thraso is a stock character from Roman comedy representing a "braggart soldier"; here used to describe arrogant academic rivals</note> who contend that light is darkness and darkness is light? They have almost the entire unclean world as a defender of their most vain vanities; for the world does not seek the Truth, but its own honor. Therefore, God gives us over to a reprobate mind <note>A reference to the biblical passage Romans 1:28</note>, so that we may persecute one another with hatred and envy, and we ourselves become the cause of the imminent destruction of our own Kingdom. O fountain of truth and wisdom, look upon our affairs and the hearts of those who, with pious desire and burning prayers, struggle day and night against this looming metamorphosis. But the Most High will also give an end to these things in His time. And I hope, with the heavens favoring us, that God will soon stir up some great minds to bring the Truth in sciences and faculties into the light (for the discovery of the arts has not yet reached its final end), to root out the weeds <note>original: *zizaniam*; a reference to the biblical "tares" or weeds sown among wheat</note> of the sciences, and refute the deceptions and errors of the scholastics <note>Traditional university philosophers and physicians who relied on ancient texts rather than experimentation</note>—not with words, but with deeds; not with logic-puzzles, but with reality itself. For when Perfection comes, as the time of Renewal and Regeneration approaches, all that is imperfect must necessarily fall. For where there is Pride with titles, degrees, and famous names, there is no Humility,

# IV. BY WHAT POWER, AND IN WHAT MANNER,
## Medicine Acts upon the Human Body,
### and expels diseases.

<margin>In the book *On Winds* <note>original: *De flatibus*; a treatise in the Hippocratic Corpus.</note>.</margin>
Because physicians commonly clash over whether remedies are "contraries for contraries" <note>original: *Contraria Contrariorum*</note> according to the oracle of Hippocrates, or "likes for likes" <note>original: *Similia Similium*</note> according to Paracelsus, it must be observed that the phrasing of these two axioms—though they appear different in form and seem to conflict—are both accepted within the Anatomy of Nature. Thus, many fail to grasp the mind of the Philosophers because they do not understand that what seems to be a discord among them is actually a beautiful concord, if the disagreement is reconciled by a timely and harmonious interpretation. For medicine is nothing other than the application of those things which are desired—namely, the restoration of powers and the Balsam <note>original: *Balsamus*; a vital, life-preserving force or fluid believed to exist in all living things.</note>—and the removal of those things which are redundant—namely, morbid impurities. Therefore, Paracelsus does not oppose Hippocrates when he asserts that hunger is cured by food, thirst by drink, fullness by evacuation, emptiness by restoration, labor by rest, and rest by labor; and that, in general, "contraries are the remedies for contraries." But he clearly opposes Galen <note>A 2nd-century Greek physician whose theories of "humors" dominated medicine for centuries.</note>, who improperly adapts Hippocratic "contrariety" to those bare qualities condemned by Hippocrates; for Galen, through an unfortunate error, traces the primary and chief ideas of cures to cooling, heating, moistening, and drying, and their associated qualities.

Only the *Natures* of remedies, as mentioned above, or *powers* <note>original: *δυνάμεις* (dynameis); the active, inherent virtues of a substance.</note>, are the Hippocratic healers of diseases; the Physician is truly the servant. And this same Nature—namely our Life, and the Balsam or Balsamic Mummy <note>original: *Mumia Balsamica*; a Paracelsian term for the innate preservative power within a living body that prevents decay.</note> which defends the body from any corruption through the medium of the Saline liquor (that is, the inferior Balsam born from the superior in the lower parts)—this same Nature of ours (which sometimes performs miracles when the help of physicians has been implored in vain, those who, to the great shame of their Name and the disgrace of the medical Art, have too hastily declared the patient lost and abandoned them to their Prognostics) is the human body's own physician, who from the outsid— <note>original: *ab extrinse-* (catchword for next page: *ab extrinseco*)</note>

<summary>This page argues that the medical theories of Hippocrates and Paracelsus are complementary rather than contradictory, asserting that "Nature" and the body's internal "Balsam" are the true healers, while the physician merely assists.</summary>

P R Æ F A T I O

<margin>
Nature cures by like things.
<note>original: *Natura similibus curat*</note>
</margin>

...internal physician requires nothing else besides restoration or—as they say in common speech—fortification, applied through an external medicine that is highly purified and similar to the afflicted part of Nature, not alien to it. And thus the Medicinal Balsam <note>A healing substance or elixir.</note> aids the Balsam of Life—also called the Radical and Natural Balsam—because of their shared sympathy and common nature, acting like a coworker and fellow initiate. From this, the weakened Natural powers regain their strength; once recovered, Nature is powerful enough on her own—like an internal and inborn Antidote—to drive all her enemies out of her Kingdom <note>original: *Monarchia*; the sovereign rule of the life force over the body.</note> by the sole power of the Vital faculties.

For to wish to cure sick bodies with contrary qualities is nothing other than to stir up an internal war leading to total ruin for a Nature already sufficiently weakened by civil strife. Furthermore, contraries do not accept one another; and if they do not accept one another, they neither act upon each other nor receive any influence from each other. Where there is no true action and passion <note>In the philosophical sense, "action" is doing something, and "passion" is having something done to you.</note>, no true Natural effect follows. 

Therefore, medicines cannot be contrary to the affected area; instead, they must be most closely related to it. Because of the harmony between the Great World <term>Macrocosm: the universe or environment around us</term> and the Little World <term>Microcosm: the human being, seen as a reflection of the universe</term>, the External Nature of the medicine must be the same as the Internal Nature of the affected place, so that its failing Internal Nature may be comforted and assisted by the abundance of that External Nature. 

Man is called a **Microcosm** for this reason: because the whole world preserves, nourishes, and cures him. For when the fruits of Earth, Air, Water, and Fire within the Microcosm fall ill, they must be restored by similar fruits from the Macrocosm. In this way, Nature comforts and assists her own nature. Once Nature is comforted and aided by her own nature, she forcefully expels every enemy, since by nature every Nature is most inclined toward its own preservation. 

Thus, we have Nature not only as an ally, but as a friend and dutiful helper, since she alone is the genuine healer of all diseases—as Galen <note>A famous Greek physician whose theories dominated Western medicine for centuries.</note> also testifies in the thirteenth book of his *Method of Healing*. She is the "first mover" of every cure, for without her strength or vigor, all medicine is useless and in vain. Nature, when preserved in her proper Balance <note>original: *Temperatura*</note>, is a medicine unto herself and heals her own infirmities through her inborn **Mummy** <note>original: *Mumia*; in Paracelsian medicine, this refers to a vital life-force or "balsam" inherent in the living body that heals wounds and resists decay.</note>. Where the Internal Nature herself refuses to be the medicine, there all diseases are fatal. 

For it is very well known that every thing desires, by a certain natural instinct, to be perfected and preserved; conversely, it most vehemently shrinks from its own destruction and avoids it as much as possible. The parts of our body, when injured by a sword or in any other way, prove this to us by daily experience: for the injured parts feel the immediate and tireless help of Nature rushing to them, as if she will not rest until...

<summary>This page argues for the principle of "like cures like," claiming that the human body (microcosm) is healed by corresponding elements in the universe (macrocosm) that strengthen the body's own innate healing power, or "Mumia." It challenges the traditional Galenic idea of "curing by contraries," suggesting that introducing opposing qualities only creates internal conflict within a weakened patient.</summary>

### ADMONITORY PREFACE

...once a hideous wound has been closed, Nature restores the injured parts to their original integrity. Now, as for what some say—that ***Contraries are cured by contraries***—they speak well, provided they are not looking at physical **qualities** <note>In traditional Galenic medicine, these were Hot, Cold, Moist, and Dry.</note> but rather at the **contrary powers of Nature**. For there are as many adverse or "evil" powers of **Nature** as there are healthful or "good" powers. The goodness of the latter is always occupied with and consists in the preservation of **Nature**, just as the malice of the former is always occupied with the destruction of **Nature**. Therefore, if those evil powers seek to destroy, the good powers are given as a reinforcement to a struggling **Nature**, so that by their own goodness they may preserve the twofold goodness of **Nature**, while expelling and overcoming that malice. 

In this way, the "evil" adverse or contrary powers of **Nature** are rightly expelled and conquered by "good" adverse and contrary powers of **Nature**. However, contrary qualities are not removed by contrary qualities; rather, both are further irritated and provoked to a fight. From this battle follows a greater weakening of **Nature** rather than a **Confirmation** <note>A strengthening or stabilization.</note>, because **Nature** is not a **Quality** but a **Power** <term>Virtus: The essential, active strength or "virtue" of a substance</term>. She wishes to be helped by **Powers**, not by **Qualities**, if she is to prevail and fight happily against her evil enemy. For it is not the physician who puts the disease to flight, but **Nature** herself—which is the **Internal Mummy** <note>original: *Interna Mumia*; a Paracelsian term for the vital life-force or healing essence inherent in living bodies</note> or **Internal Balsam**. She expels every evil set against her if, when her own **Internal** forces fail, she is supported by **External** forces provided by the physician, who is her servant.

<margin>When the Natural physician <note>The human doctor.</note> stops, the Internal physician begins.</margin>

Indeed, the best medicine is often to apply no medicine at all, and to commit the operation solely to the **Archaeus** <term>Archaeus: The "internal chemist" or vital force that governs the body's functions</term> or the Craft of **Nature**. For the **Nature** of the internal body expels more diseases than the physician does with his medicine. 

For this reason, if a cure is sometimes achieved in a burning plague by using very cold opium, it is not accomplished because of the coldness of the opium, but because of the specific poisonous power of the opium. This power is greater in its degree of poison than the hidden poisonous force of that plague; thus, **Nature kills Poison with Poison**, and compels a lesser evil by means of a stronger evil. In this way, she fights against the enemy with weapons both good and harmful so that she may keep her own domain safe, putting the enemy to flight from her territory by any means necessary. 

Just as winter does not "remove" summer, and summer does not "drive out" winter, but one merely succeeds the other, so a quality never "removes" a quality. Without power, a quality is dead and entirely accidental; consequently, it can provide no life or substance—which is exactly what a medicine must do if it is to help Nature. It is also worth noting here that the **Roots of diseases** in the human body are neither hot nor cold; but since nothing can exist without heat, a disease is *said* to be hot or cold, even though those accidents and discharges are merely the signs of the disease, not the **disease**

*...internal to himself. These spirits even build their own house and external habitation, just as snails and shellfish do. These builders of diseases and these Invisible Stars were unknown to the ancients. Medicine is spirit (not body), and the sun is its visible image. Therefore, in simples <note>Medicinal plants or substances used on their own, rather than in complex mixtures.</note>, the body or Earth must be left behind, and the virtue, Heaven, or Star must be received. For in the Microcosm <note>The "little world" of the human body, which reflects the "Macrocosm" of the universe.</note> and in medicine, once the impure body is set aside, it is necessary for pure life to act upon life, and spirit upon spirit—just as the intangible sun makes snow vanish by liquefying it. For such is the Nature of all Arcana <term>Arcanum: An incorporeal, hidden healing virtue or "secret" essence within a substance.</term>, that they perform their operations without matter or body, since diseases themselves are also not bodies. And this is true and living Anatomy.*

<margin>In the first Treatise of the second book of the *Great Surgery*. Degrees and Complexions in diseases are not considered.</margin>

*This Mechanic and Builder of diseases must be overcome and removed at its Root and Origin, just as a whole tree can be destroyed in the Seed, but not in the Branch. Thus the Mechanic Craftsman, or the principle of a pear's generation, has his dwelling in the Root, not in the Branch. In the same way, weeds, while they are green, are prevented from growing through the corruption of the Earth, not by plucking them out. Where the Center, Root, and Seed of diseases are uprooted and healed, then all is well accomplished. It is not the smoke rising from the fire, but the fire itself that must be extinguished. For the physician who heals based on complexion <note>The balance of the four humors (sanguine, phlegmatic, etc.) in a person’s temperament.</note> is like one who wishes to extinguish the harmless flame of a fire while leaving behind the burning ember or glowing coal. That which is born from the seed is not to be judged as the disease; rather, the Root of the seed, which encompasses all powers, must be attacked in the cure.*

<margin>In the booklet *On Ancient Medicine*.</margin>

*Now, while Paracelsus affirms that like is preserved by like and destroyed by contraries, he does not look to the primary or secondary qualities <note>The Galenic qualities of Hot, Cold, Moist, and Dry.</note>, which he always calls "Relollacean" <term>Relollaceas: A term coined by Paracelsus to describe things that are useless, invalid, or devoid of true power.</term> or invalid. Instead, he looks only to the substance—the CHERIONIUM <note>original: *CHERIONIUM*; likely referring to a specific curative power or essence</note>, the Hippocratic powers <note>original: δυνάμεις (*dynameis*)</note>, and Virtues—as can be seen in the 18th chapter of the first Treatise of the second part of the *Great Surgery*, and in other places. Remedies are called "similars" to diseases because they are said to be of the same Anatomy of Nature—because they contain similar Signatures <note>The physical signs or "stamps" on plants and minerals that reveal their medicinal use.</note>, Properties, and Roots. But they are called "contraries" because they repair deficiencies and desires; because, through a friendly saturation of the spirit, they soothe compatible impurities, and they bring about resolutions, consumptions, and silent removals.*

<margin>For every disease must be cured by its own specific appropriated remedy.</margin>

*He understands that "like is preserved by like" in this way: namely, the Salt, Sulphur, and Mercury <note>The three primary alchemical principles (Tria Prima) thought to compose all matter.</note> of the microcosm are preserved by the Salt, Sulphur, and Mercury of the macrocosm that correspond by analogy. And just as in the microcosm there are various Sulphurs (one of the head, another of the heart, etc.), so too the Mer-*

...just as there are various Mercuries and various Salts, so too in the macrocosm <note>The "great world" or the universe.</note> a corresponding variety of Sulphur, Salt, and Mercury will appear in herbs and minerals. The service of fire is what usually reveals their compatibility, conflict, and distinction. Because Paracelsus classifies all physical diseases according to those three substances—from which our bodies are composed—and according to the waste-like excesses resulting from food and drink, he describes them as follows:

Diseases arising from "ignited" Sulphur (since Sulphur is destroyed and intensified in four ways, namely by the four elements) he calls **Sulphurous** in the human body; these include all **Inflammations** and **Fevers**.

Those arising from the "liquor" <note>The fluid, metallic principle of Mercury.</note> he calls **Mercurial**. For Mercury is raised above its natural state in three ways: by the accidental heat of the digestive power, by the heat of physical exercise, or by heat arising from the Stars. By the heat of digestion, it is distilled and causes **Apoplexy** and its various types. By the heat of exercise, it is refined <note>original: "sublimatur"</note> and causes **Mania** and **Phrensy** <note>Severe delirium or mental agitation.</note>. By the heat of the Stars, it is precipitated; when combined with food and drink that are rich in **Tartar** <term>Tartar: A stony or calcified byproduct within the body, which Paracelsus believed caused blockages and pain.</term>, it causes **Gout of the feet** <note>original: "Podagram"</note>, **Gout of the hands** <note>original: "Chiragram"</note>, and **Joint Pain** <note>original: "Artheticam"</note>.

Those provoked by Salt he calls **Saline** and **Nitrous**. For Salt, through four methods of intensification, harms health and produces serious diseases: by **Resolution** <note>Dissolving into liquid.</note>, **Calcination** (through the loss of the liquid and moist temperament), **Reverberation**, and **Alkalization**. These result in **ulcers**, **scabies**, **shingles**, **skin eruptions**, **itching**, and the like, all of which are diseases of dissolved Salt. The cause of the destruction of Salt is excessive eating, which destroys digestion; immoderate lust is a cause of the "Resolution" of Salt within the microcosm <note>The human body.</note>. The Stars also disturb Salt from its proper state. This Salt can be transmuted into all kinds of Salts, and whatever the nature of the transformation, such is the nature of the disease.

He says, therefore, that ignited Sulphur in the body of the microcosm must be cured by the harmonically corresponding Sulphur of the macrocosm. However, if one looks at his intended goal, such a remedy will act as a *contrary* to the disease. For instance, to extinguish such Sulphur ignited in the body (suppose a fever, if the fire becomes universal and has the source of its spring in the heart), he wants an "appropriate" Sulphur to be taken—not a Mercurial liquor nor a Salt. Many such are found in the Garden of Nature and the families of herbs and minerals, such as the Sulphur of **Vitriol** <note>Iron or copper sulfates.</note>, of **Nitre**, of **Common Salt**, and similar things.

Similarly, he teaches that ulcers (provoked by Salts) ought to be cured by Salts. But if his purpose is observed, such Salts are contrary to the one that provoked the evil and are opposed to the evil itself. For they are **incarnative** <note>Promoting the growth of new flesh.</note> and **consolidative** <note>Healing or closing a wound.</note>, such as **Frankincense**, **Mastic**, **Myrrh**, and **Aloes**. From this, it is clear that he sometimes also names Salt as...

## V. THE DUTY OF THE PHYSICIAN AS THE SERVANT OF NATURE.

<margin>He said it himself. <note>original: "αὐτὸς ἔφα" (autos epha)</note></margin>
*Just as the boundary of common philosophy is not fixed in Aristotle, as Petrus Ramus <note>A 16th-century French philosopher known for his critique of Aristotelian logic.</note> has soundly shown, so the light of all Nature, according to Paracelsus, is not exhausted in Galen <note>An ancient Greek physician whose theories dominated Western medicine for over 1,000 years.</note> alone. Men should not snatch away from other men the freedom of human intellect, the light of Nature, and the faculty of discerning and judging, for the intellectual monarchy of the Greeks has ended. Therefore, whoever desires to excel in the medical art (since no one can emerge truly learned who swears only by the rudiments of a single faculty) must be a stranger to every kind of sect, nor swear by the opinion of any author, but follow only the naked Truth and subscribe to it, always mindful of that line from Horace:*

> ->*Wherever the storm carries me, I am carried as a guest,*<-
> ->*bound to swear by the words of no master.*<-

<margin>All hidden things must be made manifest by divine decree.</margin>
*Nor should the discoveries of others be rejected as a whole by adhering to one sect, but all sects, however many there are, should be acknowledged as familiar. For according to the most noble and wise phoenix of philosophers, Pico della Mirandola—that inimitable example of profound intellect and multifaceted learning—there is in every single school <note>original: "familia"</note> something remarkable that is not shared with the others. No book is so bad or lowly that it does not contain some good often neglected by the most excellent authors. A later age, says Fabius <note>Likely referring to Quintilian, the Roman rhetorician.</note>, has worked to educate the previous one more fully, and while science itself grows along with human intellects, a wiser progeny has later wiped away many of the most shameful errors of the pagans like a second sponge. Nor is it doubtful that more things still lie hidden, locked in the treasuries of Wisdom and Nature...*

<margin>
Daily experience, which has not yet reached its end, reveals many errors of the ancients.

*...destined by an immutable law for various times and nations until the end of the age, [these things] must be unearthed by the efforts of wise men, rather than those things that are obvious to our senses. Since Nature is circular, it can hardly be fully comprehended by any mortal due to the shortness of life. Since this is the case, the medicine of neither the ancients nor of Theophrastus <note>Theophrastus von Hohenheim, famously known as Paracelsus (1493–1541).</note> should be rejected entirely; nor should it be embraced in such a way that if something better is found, we leave no room for it. For day teaches day, and the second is the teacher of the first; both are to be compared, and whatever is better in both should be retained. Since they are men, they also suffer human failings; they err in places, they write contradictory and clashing things, sometimes disagreeing with themselves, and they are deluded in many matters, for not everyone sees everything. Only the Holy Spirit has the full knowledge of all things, who distributes to everyone according to a certain measure, and breathing where he wills, reserves much for himself, so that he may always have us as his disciples.*

<margin>
Paracelsus in *The Great Surgery*.
</margin>

*Let the true physician be a servant of Nature, not its master, and according to the opinion of Hippocrates and Galen, a philosopher skilled in healing. And because there are two kinds of those practicing philosophy—some inquire into the elementary natures of things beneath the sphere of the Moon in the common way; some, philosophers by a far more splendid and truer name, track the secrets and more hidden things of Nature—these men enter the inner chambers and the sanctuary of Nature, and they have true knowledge and experience of the Light of Nature, from which true physicians arise. For the innate natural power of things growing from the Earth, joined through Chemistry <term>Chymia: A term then encompassing both chemistry and alchemy, specifically the extraction of medicinal "essences."</term> with the constellation of the Firmament, mediated by the skill of the physician caused by celestial influence—these three finally bring forth a genuine physician. But according to Paracelsus, he should first be a legitimate INTERPRETER OF NATURE, whose Economy <note>original: "Oeconomiam"; referring to the organized system or management of the natural world.</note> he alone scrutinizes: its universal breadth, all the species and kinds of all creatures known by themselves, which he finally observes even in Man.*

<margin>
The true philosopher has his origin in the knowledge of Heaven and Earth, and he knows their nature and property exactly. Philosophy began from wonder <note>A classic philosophical proverb: "Ex admirari cœptum est Philosophari."</note>.
</margin>

*Philosophy teaches the powers and properties of Earth and Water, just as Astronomy teaches those of the Firmament and the Air. Philosophy and Astronomy make a perfect philosopher, not only in the macrocosm <term>Macrocosm: The "great world" or the universe as a whole.</term>, but also in the microcosm <term>Microcosm: The "little world," specifically the human being, viewed as a reflection of the universe.</term>. Let the physician have knowledge of Philosophy and Astronomy: for Chiromancy <note>Palmistry or hand-reading.</note>, Pyromancy <note>Divination or study involving fire.</note>, and Geomancy <note>Interpretation of patterns in the earth.</note> are the elements of Astronomy and Philosophy. For in the judgment of Theophrastus and Plato, only those are to be considered true philosophers who contemplate and admire this stupendous handiwork of Nature through this massive machinery of the whole Creation; who study the qualities and affections of the Heavens and the burning bodies...*

<margin>The Philosopher arises from the physician, and the physician from the Philosopher; each is the root of the other, and both together are one Alchemical **Spagyrist** <note>original: "Spagyrus"; a practitioner who separates and recombines substances.</note> of all things. He was the true **Monarch of Medicine** and the first physician of the **Microcosm**, who alone since the time of Noah wrote of the **Internal Astral Man** and his office created by God, as well as the origin of great incurable diseases—both Natural and Metaphysical. This never entered the minds of physicians of previous ages, even in their dreams; much less our followers of **Pagan Philosophy**, from which Gentile Philosophy every error has flowed, because (as said above) it passed over the twofold body of Creatures in silence and unknown.

Following Paracelsus, others of blessed and honored memory, most pious and innocent...*

<meta>This page continues the introductory defense of Hermetic philosophy. # PREFACE

*He would act against the oath of Hippocrates <note>The ancient Greek physician often credited with the "Hippocratic Oath," which originally included a vow to keep medical teachings within a specific circle.</note>, who also did not wish to teach medicine to everyone. Indeed, a secret must be hidden which is granted by God alone to be revealed; for if it were made public, it would usually bring about death, imprisonment, or disgrace—or at the very least, constant fear and voluntary exile (unless one is willing to burn a permanent stain into their own name through lying and fraud to cover themselves) far from one's homeland and family for the sake of safety. This is testified by the examples of Raymond Lull, Arnaldus de Villa Nova, Nicholas Zacharias of Paris, and others, in addition to more recent figures. The true Hermetic Philosophers <note>Followers of the "Hermetic" tradition, a blend of alchemy, philosophy, and spiritualism attributed to the legendary Hermes Trismegistus.</note> have taken a sacred vow that they will follow in the footsteps of their fathers and teachers, and will not, through any recklessness, profane the virginity of Nature that has been preserved since the beginning of the ages. However, they have given instructions to disciples who are bound by oaths and perpetual gratitude and faith—those deemed worthy by Nature or education—though these secrets must still be extracted with much sweat and effort.*

<margin>Without labor, no one should possess the art.</margin>

*Those who are weak in judgment think that if Paracelsus <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), a revolutionary physician who rejected traditional medical authority in favor of "Chymia" (alchemy) and observation.</note> attacks the "Methodics" <note>A school of medical thought that followed rigid, established rules based on ancient texts like Galen.</note> for their lack of Experience, or the "Empirics" <note>Those who relied solely on observation without a theoretical or scientific basis.</note> for their lack of Science, that he spares no kind of doctor and professes himself to be the one and only physician in the whole world. In truth, he only condemns the common crowd of doctors who are ignorant of both Theory and Practice. Surely those are not to be considered doctors who, while achieving nothing in the way of healing, merely fight over medical matters with wordiness and logic; this is a sign of foolish ambition. These men claim the "Method" of medicine for themselves, but they are a class of men swollen with conceit and pride, born to suppress the truth of the Medical Art. Some of them (since the shame of admitting they were wrong is so deeply offensive to the proud and inexperienced) are so biased against Theophrastus <note>Theophrastus is Paracelsus's given name.</note> himself that they would rather a patient die than use the medicines prescribed by him. Many even despise his medicines for this reason: they fear that if those remedies were used openly and their wonderful effects seen, their own authority would diminish. Thus, the better the remedies are, the more they despise them. And although these deceptive "Methodic" critics of Theophrastus (who prolong illnesses for their own profit by delaying remedies) charge the genuine "Chymists" <note>Alchemists or chemical physicians.</note> with having abandoned the true Method, it is for nothing; for the method Paracelsus follows is consistent with both Reason and Experience, as is clear to those endowed with the Light of Understanding. We should not be so devoted to anyone's authority that we do not put Truth itself first, since without Truth, all authority is harmful and should be considered of no importance by the wise. We should attend not to *who* says a thing, but *what* is said; and no one should be so bound to the judgment of others that they are completely robbed of their own.*

# ADMONITIONS

The True Method <note>Original: *Vera Methodus*. In this context, the "method" refers to the systematic approach to medical practice and diagnosis.</note> consists of the knowledge of a Disease and its Cure—namely, that which, through a rational diet and suitable Medicines, expels the disease and introduces health. Therefore, **Wimpinaeus** <note>Johannes Albertus Wimpinaeus, a 16th-century physician and author of *De concordia Hippocraticorum et Paracelsistarum*, who sought to reconcile traditional medicine with Paracelsus's new ideas.</note> learnedly discusses how the most serious diseases are cured today by the Paracelsists for three reasons.

**FIRST**, because diseases are understood more perfectly. In the past, when all diseases were attributed to the four humors <note>The traditional Galenic system which held that health was governed by the balance of four fluids: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.</note>, those illnesses caused by Tartar <note>A central Paracelsian concept. Just as tartar forms a hard crust inside a wine barrel, Paracelsus believed that minerals in food and drink could precipitate as "stones" or "sand" inside the body, causing gout, stones, and blockages.</note> clinging to a particular organ could not be cured, for Tartar cannot be attributed to any of those four humors. Since we have happened upon the subject of Tartar here, a more detailed mention of it should be made in this convenient place.

<margin>
Every organ has its own specific digestion and separation within itself, as well as its own "emunctorium" or waste-clearing passage.
</margin>
From the ultimate matter of food—namely, through the digestion of the stomach's Archeus <note>The "Archeus" is the internal "alchemist" or vital force that Paracelsians believed directed the functions of the body, specifically the separation of nutrients from waste.</note>, the process of separation, and the generation of that separation—there emerges the first Essence of life, from which the body receives its nourishment and food. It is reduced into Sulphur, Mercury, and Salt <note>Known as the *Tria Prima* (Three Primes). To Paracelsians, these were the basic components of all matter: Sulphur (the principle of fire/combustibility), Mercury (the principle of liquidity/volatility), and Salt (the principle of solidity/permanence).</note>, as is seen in the three primary waste-channels: the excess of Salt is separated through the urine; the excess of Sulphur is secreted and expelled through the intestines; and the Mercury (or the liquid of the nourishment) takes its place, and if any excess occurs within it, it is driven out through the pores.

<margin>
The first digestion of the stomach is not a full digestion but a preparation for the specific digestions of the individual organs.
*This occurs when the spirits of Salt—namely of the flesh and the urine—are united.
The first separation of Tartar produces "usnea" <note>Usually referring to a lichen or mossy growth, here describing a type of filmy deposit</note> which belongs to the Liver; the second produces "grando" <note>Literally "hailstone," describing a specific granular deposit</note> which belongs to the Stomach; the third produces "lapillum" <note>A little stone</note> which belongs to the Kidneys and Bladder. Every human has the filmy deposit and the granule, but not everyone has the stone.
</margin>
Everything we eat and drink contains within it a mucilaginous, muddy, and sandy Tartar that is harmful to human health. Nature accepts nothing except that which is pure. The stomach—which is the instrument of the human Archeus, or the internal Chemist, innate and implanted by God—immediately separates the impure, dross-filled Tartar from the pure Nourishment as soon as it receives what has been eaten and ingested. If the stomach is strong, especially in its power of separation, the pure passes to the limbs for the sake of nourishment, while the impure exits through the bowels. If the stomach is weak, the impure is sent even through the mesenteric veins to the liver, where a second digestion and separation take place. The liver, therefore, in its turn, separates the pure from the impure out of those two substances—namely, the Ruby from the Crystal. The "Ruby" <note>Original: *Rubinus*. Here it refers to the nutrient-rich, red portion of the processed food that becomes blood.</note> is the nourishment for all the organs: the heart, the brain, and so on. The "Crystal" <note>Original: *Crystallum*. Referring to the clear, watery waste.</note> (or that which is not nourishment) it expels to the kidneys; this is the urine, which is nothing other than Salt pressed out from the Mercurial elements by the force of separation and forced into a liquid state, which is then resolved by the liver into water and expelled. If the liver, due to weakness, does not separate correctly, it sends the mucilaginous and stone-forming matter to the kidneys. There, in the absence of good separation and by the power of predestination, it is coagulated into Sand, Tartar, or a stony or mucilaginous mass by means of the spirit of Salt. Tartar, therefore, is the waste of food and drink which is coagulated in man by the spirit of Salt...

This kind is of the most powerful impression, namely when the Air is infected by the vapors of the Earth, Water, and Firmament, and subsequently infects us. The universal medicine powerfully expels these diseases which arise from the impressions of the stars.

...of the Sun and Moon existing within us as a microcosm. In such cases, the body must be comforted by its own likeness, that is, by the macrocosmic Heat of the Sun and Moon, if it can be obtained. This is found in that most simple matter generated by God the Best and Greatest from the **Spirit of the World** <note>original: *spiritu mundi*; the vitalizing essence that Paracelsians believed permeated the universe</note> (which is one and the same as the spirit of our own body) for the restoration and conservation of **Human Nature**. Alternatively, it can be found in those things in which the power of the Sun and Moon resides, brought into action through artifice—namely, converted into a simple spirit like the spirit of our own life, which is achieved through dissolution and conjunction with **Nourishment**. If, however, our **Internal Alchemist** <term>Archæus: the internal vital force or "chemist" that governs the body's organs and separates pure nutrients from impure waste</term>—which separates the pure from the impure in the stomach, liver, or kidneys—becomes infected, or if the separative power of the internal organs is hindered by external accidents, then the **Excrement** remains with the chyle. This results not only in diseases of the kidneys and intestines but also **Stomach Ailments** in the stomach, **Liver Ailments** in the liver, and **Arthritic Ailments** in the "glue" <note>original: *glutine*; a reference to the synovial fluids or humors of the joints</note>, nerves, limbs, and joints. From this arises **Gout of the foot**, **Gout of the hand**, and **Gout of the knee** <note>original: *Podagra, Chiragra, Genugra*</note>, namely from the freezing of that "glue" by the **Spirit of Salt** <note>original: *Spiritum Salis*; an acidic essence believed to cause coagulation and stone formation</note>. <margin>**Tartar** differs according to the locations of the passages: the mouth, the stomach, the base of the stomach, the intestines, the liver, the kidneys, the bladder, the flesh, the blood, and the marrow.</margin> Therefore, the **Tartar of the Elements** must be destroyed by the **Internal Alchemist** of the stomach so that it does not become the **Tartar of Man**. For if the Spirit of Salt—which is the hero and Master of Coagulation in various substances—encounters matter that has been dissolved or separated from nourishment and excrement, it generates the **Stone** <note>original: *Calculum*; a physical stone or blockage in the body</note>. *So much for Tartar.*

**SECONDLY**, we now possess more perfect medicines than in former times, specifically those derived from **Minerals**. Their preparations and proper administrations have become known to the **diligent sons of the furnace** <note>original: *Nigellis Cadmi filiis*; literally "darkened sons of Cadmus," a poetic reference to alchemists or chemists blackened by the soot of their work</note>. As the saying goes: *“For a hard knot, a hard wedge must be applied.”* Therefore, for an "iron-like" <note>meaning stubborn or unyielding</note> disease, **Paracelsus** orders the use of a suitable "steel-like" medicine, since extreme diseases demand extreme remedies.

**THIRDLY**, because in this time the **Harmony** of the Greater World <note>Macrocosm</note> with the Lesser World <note>Microcosm/Man</note> has been revealed and recognized, we know which of the most excellent medicines is familiar and friendly to this or that member: such as **Silver, Sapphire, Vitriol, and Emerald** for the Brain; **Gold, Pearls, and Saffron** for the Heart; **Sulfur** for the Lung; and so on.

Furthermore, as for the fact that **Paracelsus** gives offense to **Galen**, **Galen** did the same to others. Even **Hippocrates** wrote many things which are today rejected by most **Galenists**. Indeed, even the leaders of common Medicine do not agree among themselves. How many of them disagree regarding particular diseases with their own most combative opinions, and regarding the [nature] of diseases...

Let them occupy themselves in reading the works of this new philosopher and physician [Paracelsus]—not indeed superficially and perfunctorily, but with the greatest mental attention. For in this type of study, the experience and industry of bees must be followed, who pack and collect their honey from the most fragrant juice of flowers, separating all the best from the bad and handling only what is useful. 

And I would not wish to persuade them of this because everything belonging to **Paracelsus** (as he himself retracts certain of his early writings) should be venerated as **Evangelical oracles**, just as we see others do in adoring the *decrees of the heathens* <note>original: *Ethnicorum placitis*; referring to blind adherence to classical, non-Christian authors like Galen or Aristotle</note>, but because a diligent and accurate reading of him can provide us no small benefit and bring greater light to understanding the writings of **Hippocrates** more intimately and correctly. 

For those are not to be praised who, without judgment, condemn everything Paracelsus has written, when they have not even read a paragraph, or if they have read something, they have not totally understood even a third of it. Hear me, **Philosophasters** <term>Philosophaster: a pretentious or sham philosopher who possesses only superficial knowledge</term>, who, having despised the kernel, insist only on the shell of the philosophers; seek from God—not from paper books—the Spirit of Understanding the dead letter of **Theophrastus** <note>Theophrastus von Hohenheim, better known as Paracelsus</note> and the Philosophers.

...communicated for the public good, they gave the adversary a handle for declaring that they are involved in the most evident disagreement. This is because the Expert wrote in a magical style—not for the common crowd, but for himself and for those intelligent ones educated in the school of magic. These are the "Sons of Wisdom," not the Sophists or the gold-hungry Alchemists who are under a spell. He was moved by a just indignation toward certain most unfair and inhumane Physicians and Apothecaries of his time, who many times lay in wait for him with poison to shorten his life. If he had written more clearly, then those marketplace quacks and common Alchemists would have surpassed all physicians and debased the art to the great injury of Nature. 

He hid his mysteries under common and various names: therefore, metaphors are not to be taken as the literal truth itself. For the Secret <note>original: *Arcanum*; a hidden, potent medicinal virtue</note> of Medicine is the hidden Power of GOD, or the Magical WORDS in Paracelsus which few understand. Therefore, they have need of a "Delian swimmer" <note>An ancient idiom referring to a person who can dive deep into difficult texts without drowning; originally used by Socrates regarding the obscure writings of Heraclitus.</note> and the sharpest wit; they also require a magical Understanding—namely, a purified eye of the mind—which may examine their meanings and hidden mysteries. 

By "Magic" everywhere I mean the True and lawful kind (not that infamous and profane sorcery <note>original: *goeteia*; lower magic or witchcraft</note> worthy of the fire <note>original: *Vulcano*, referring to the god of fire/the forge</note>, which men of hopeless character and wicked curiosity pursue). I mean the absolute perfection of all most noble Philosophy, the greatest Wisdom of the works of GOD, and a full knowledge of hidden Nature. By observing the harmony and discord of things through the proper application of active and passive forces, this magic is accustomed to accomplish incredible things that exceed the common order of Nature. 

Intelligent readers will notice that Paracelsus, following the imitation and model of the Great **Hippocrates**, joined together the practice of both Medicine—namely Physics <note>In the 16th century, "Physics" referred to internal medicine and the study of natural causes, while "Surgery" was manual/external treatment.</note> and Surgery. For he established a two-fold medicine: Physics, which is the knowledge of all diseases; and Surgery, which is their healing—which, like the work of a carpenter, cannot be performed without hands. For neither can safely exist or be practiced without the other, except to the frequent loss and danger of the sick. Therefore every Surgeon must necessarily be a Physician, and vice-versa—so that, as it were, the whole bridegroom may have a whole bride. 

Furthermore, he constantly advised that the selection of remedies, and their preparations and compositions, should be performed by the physicians themselves, and not blindly entrusted to others. For he is truly the genuine physician who has learned to prepare medications with his own hand—not merely by Theory <note>original: *Ratione*; literally "by Reason" or "Rationalist" methods</note> as the "Rationalist Physicians" do—and knows how to separate them from their poison and dregs, to cleanse them, and to reduce them to pure simplicity, rather than entrusting them to an unskilled cook. For good things are mixed with bad; neither sugar is without dreggy impurity, nor honey without poisonous bit[terness...]

But the Great Doctors of our time, who have grown old in the common medical art, do not want to be disciples and beginners; they are ashamed to dig. And because a years-old tree is transplanted with difficulty, and it is hard to accustom old dogs to the leash and the hunt, they prefer to openly contradict the truth and stubbornly bark at it and bite it with a dog-like voice, rather than emending their errors by working, lest they seem not to have been wise enough, or to have learned something better from others. *Although they may cry out that a Chemist <note>original: Chymicus</note> is not a physician, even if he were the most skilled, but rather one who has learned to employ individual Remedies for diseases through Judgment and Reason (setting Chemistry <note>original: Chymia</note> aside), nevertheless those Rational physicians, standing at the bed of the sick, do not know where to turn; they are often stunned by great diseases and, because they are not healers, they become at least flatterers, since they have learned to prepare medicines by Reason and not by the Hand. Yet I do not wish in any way to undertake the patronage of those who, rejecting the writings of Hippocrates <note>The ancient Greek "Father of Medicine."</note> and the ancients without judgment or understanding, boast that they are indeed disciples of Paracelsus, but neither recognize the mind of the author in his Theory, nor execute anything worthy of praise in the works of the art.*

There are also certain *Pseudo-Theophrastians* <note>original: PseudoTheophrastai; false followers of Theophrastus Paracelsus.</note>, who by their greed and recklessness profane Divine medicine (which today is forced to be the plow for many who try to support themselves without honor) with a most effective impudence of brow for the sake of deceiving. These people boast that they employ the *Remedies of Theophrastus* under counterfeit names, while being utterly ignorant of both *Philosophical* and *Common medicine*; despising the writings of the ancients, they seize upon medicine with unwashed hands, trusting in I-know-not-what *Arcana* <note>original: Arcanis; hidden medicinal virtues or secret formulas.</note> and *Experiences*. With a foolish confidence, they undertake to cure any diseases immediately without *Reason* or *Judgment*: indeed, when they have scarcely learned how to properly apply *Fire* to a furnace, they do not hesitate to attempt the cures of the most serious diseases. And while with a greedy eye and *Thrasonic boasting* <note>original: Thrasonica jactantia; derived from Thraso, a character in Roman comedy known for extreme bragging. It refers to arrogant, empty vaunting.</note>, they show off and boast that they can thoroughly heal all diseases, and do not blush to lie with great audacity, they lead on the sick with the most charming and desired promises—and having accepted a most ample price, they offer a pleasant, but most false, promise of health...

With a most effective impudence of brow for the purpose of deceiving, they boast that they use the **Remedies of Theophrastus** under disguised names. These men are utterly ignorant of both **Philosophical** and **Common medicine**. Having despised the writings of the ancients, they seize upon medicine with those hands of theirs, trusting in I-know-not-what **Secrets** and **Experiences**. With foolish confidence, they undertake to immediately cure any diseases whatsoever without **Reason** and **Judgment**. They ignite the **Mummy** <note>term: Mumia; a vital balsamic force within the human body that can be corrupted or used for healing.</note> and the **Sulphur of Man** <note>One of the "Three Primes" of alchemy (Salt, Sulphur, Mercury); Sulphur represents the combustible, oily, and vital principle.</note> within the human **microcosm** <note>The idea that the human being is a "little world" mirroring the "macrocosm" or great world of the universe.</note>, which latently possesses all the innate poisons of the macrocosm. By their poisonous malice and sinister aspect, the stars set these alight, and no medicine, however powerful it may be, can resist or help. Such is the force of the **Sidereal spirit** <note>The spirit of the stars within the human body.</note> upon the body, that toward whatever it imagines and dreams, it simultaneously lifts and carries the body itself, as we see in **Sleepwalkers** <note>original: "Noctambulonibus"</note>. *To the believer, all things are possible*, because *Faith makes certain all uncertain things.* 

<margin>*The Will and Imagination of Man is the mother of the plague: Therefore, by imagining, a Man can infect an entire region with the plague.*</margin>

*God can in no way be conquered except through Faith; he therefore who believes in God works through God, and to God all things are possible. However, how that is done cannot be scrutinized. Faith is at least a work—namely the work of Him in whom one believes. Thoughts overcome the operations of the Stars and the Elements. For while we think, and have Faith in our thoughts, then Faith perfects the work, and without Faith nothing is done. Faith gives Imagination, Imagination gives the Star, the Star (by reason of its marriage with the Imagination) gives the effect or the work. To apply Faith to a medicine gives the spirit to the medicine, the spirit gives the thought to the medicine, and the medicine gives health.* From this it follows that the physician arises from Faith; as he has believed, the spirit promotes and assists him—namely the spirit of Nature, or the **Star of Medicine**.

<margin>Read Paracelsus on invisible diseases and on the efficacy of Natural Faith, which can do all things Naturally through God.</margin>

*Man, through the Faith of the Imagination, often does what the best physicians with their suitable medicines cannot achieve. Faith has its greatest and most powerful enemy in Unbelief, for **Imagination** joined with **Faith** can do all things. Matthew 21. Fates also cause incurable diseases, which we discover when the expected help from appropriate remedies is denied. Matthew 9, section 2. Job 33, section 19.
