And what should be diligently noted in this place: our Savior, as the Holy Page <note>A common historical term for the Bible.</note> teaches, *could not* <note>original Greek: οὐκ ἐδύνατο (*ouk edynato*)</note> perform miracles in Capernaum because they did not believe, and they resisted him with their **unbelief** and false faith. For just as Man can do nothing without God, so God in turn does not wish to act without Man as His instrument; God and Creature act both together, neither without the other. Therefore no one should wish to act without God, because no one can exist without God, in whom we are, live, and move.

**EIGHTH**, that the recovering patient should not commit greater sins against God, neighbor, and himself—to the ruin of his soul—since every disease is an expiation <term>Piaculum: An act of atonement or a punishment for a sin.</term>, or is called by the just judge as a divine innate penalty, vengeance, and scourge for the future amendment of life. Or, by this Fatherly visitation and the imposed cross to be borne patiently, it may be an example to himself and his neighbor toward a more burning Fear and worship of God. For God often permits many people to fall into great sicknesses because the joyful health of the flesh, coupled with the continuation of sins, would have brought about a great sickness of the mind, not without the loss of eternal salvation. For health without the forgiveness of sins is of no use, as it is rather a condemnation. Furthermore, sins weaken the powers of the Soul, so that it is powerless for the natural governance of the body: therefore the powers of the body are weakened and they hasten toward death. Or, by this yoke and bridle of infirmity—acting as a healthy purgatory—one is usually kept at least in the duty of piety (though few are improved by sickness) while the license to sin is cut off, which he would have abused had he been established in long-term health or life.

<margin>
The Physician begins when the wrath of God is calmed. Job 33, section 23.
</margin>

And in these diseases caused by the resistance of **Astral Impression** <note>The influence of the stars or heavens upon the human body.</note> and the **Wrath of those above**, no physical medicine is profitable (because the doors of Nature are closed by a Divine bolt), but only Celestial and Spiritual medicine. Specifically: serious Repentance to heartily weep over sins committed, to appease the stirred-up Wrath of God by the amendment of life and Reconciliation with one's neighbor, to be reconciled to God through the celestial physician of Souls, our Savior, and to submit one's own will to the most just pleasure of the Divine will, patiently in all things, devotedly and humbly, with the firmest participation in Divine Mercy. Paracelsus <note>The famous 16th-century Swiss-German physician and alchemist.</note> calls these diseases **Godly** <term>Deales: From the Latin 'Deus'; diseases considered to be sent directly by God's will.</term> from the **Entity of God** <term>Ente Dei: One of the five 'Entia' or fundamental causes of disease defined by Paracelsus, specifically the one stemming from God's sovereignty.</term> who inflicts all such diseases and works alone through both good and bad things. He says that healing happens by **Faith**, or, once the purgatory is finished, treatment through medicines should finally be attempted.

### VI. ON THE UNIQUE AND SUPREME MEDICINE OF THE MOST ANCIENT PHILOSOPHERS.

<margin>This philosophy is a **hidden Minerva** <note>Minerva was the Roman goddess of wisdom; here, the author refers to secret, divinely inspired knowledge.</note> and this unique, most precious **Pearl** exceeds all valuation.</margin>
<margin>See the *Monad* of **John Dee** of London <note>Referring to the *Monas Hieroglyphica* (1564), a famous cryptic work on alchemical geometry and mystical symbols.</note>, and **Roger Bacon**.</margin>
FURTHERMORE, regarding that supreme and universal **Philosophical Medicine**, as a way of adding a supplement, it is read that no greater **Gift of Wisdom** has emanated from Divine Munificence. Not even excepting the **Rational Soul**—than which nothing more wonderful can be pondered under Heaven and Earth after God—nothing more sublime, noble, or excellent has been given to men under Heaven than this most secret **Secret of Secret Mysteries** <term>Arcanum Arcanorum: Literally "the secret of secrets," referring to the ultimate alchemical goal, often called the Philosopher's Stone.</term>. In this [Medicine], miracles are performed: both concerning the **planets of lower astronomy** <note>In alchemy, the "planets" refer to the seven metals: Gold (Sun), Silver (Moon), Mercury (Mercury), Copper (Venus), Iron (Mars), Tin (Jupiter), and Lead (Saturn).</note>, whose imperfections and dross it causes to vanish by penetrating them with its strongest impression (for it separates all foreign sulfurousness and impure earthliness from metallic and human bodies), as well as regarding the suffering and lost health of the **Human body**, which is to be restored and preserved by its fiery vigor.

I shall remain silent for now, among infinite other things, regarding its **Magical** and **super-celestial** use. Once the generative influence <note>original: *Influentia Gonetica*</note> of the rays of the **Sun** and **Moon** is finished, and after the fourth revolution above its native Earth, it is most absolutely endowed with every created influential power, both in the Elemental world as well as the Celestial or super-celestial. It is the most wonderful of all wonders; since God is wonderful in His works, He is also accustomed to hide His wonderful **Gifts** in wonderful men. All antiquity, and the truth of the tradition of this doctrine among all nations and languages, and the consensus of all those most learned men who lived in every age with the greatest admiration and praise of many, testify that this is so. 

Moreover, besides the eyewitness inspection and certification of many in our own century, it is not difficult to establish this from their writings—woven with so many **Hieroglyphic, Magical, and Mathematical veils**, and with such a certain series of Philosophical Truth. Who then would not admire and embrace such a great **Gift** of the Most High God, an immortal reward for study, labor, and virtue? For it grants rejuvenation by driving away old age, perpetual health, and an honorable livelihood and clothing without harm to one's neighbor—not through usury and fraud, nor through false merchan[dise]... <meta>catchword: niis (completing the word *mercimoniis*, meaning merchandise or goods).</meta>

Therefore, far be it from me that, by neglecting the example of the Ancients, I should wish to obscure or deny such magnificent *Great Works* <note>original: "Magnalia." In Paracelsian thought, these are the "wonderful works" of God hidden within the natural world.</note> of God and the stupendous powers of *Nature*. For he who spurns knowledge, spurns Him who is, according to this most true art, the *Glorious and Sublime God*. Nor, what is worse, would I wish (as many do) to slander these things as the speculations of idle men, or the empty dreams and fabrications of an insane and delirious mind. Such critics, at least among the wise, betray the weakness of their own judgment and call forth public witnesses to their own ignorance. Therefore, these slanderers and the ignorant, whom the *Philosophers* also call *Fools*, are to be kept away from these most divine Banquets, and the delirious are to be left entirely to their own fantastical dreams.

Some here will prick up their ears, wondering if, relying on my own talent, I dare to boast in this place about the preparation [of the Medicine], or ambitiously claim for myself an absolute knowledge of this art for the sake of show—as the theatrical *Lovers of Wealth* <note>original: "Philopluti." From the Greek *philos* (lover) and *ploutos* (wealth).</note> and *Lovers of Money* <note>original: "Philochremati." From the Greek *chremata* (money or possessions).</note> *Pseudo-philosophers* do. But since a little earlier I promised the benevolent reader that I would hand down only those things I have experienced, I would not wish in this place to most wickedly lie to the public about the proven certainty of this matter (which is not the mark of a prudent man, but characteristic of impostors).

For this sacred and *Divine Art* and *Science*, belonging not to *Sophists* but to *Philosophers*, has been wrongly and incorrectly condemned as false by the ignorant. Indeed, among all arts, both *Liberal* <note>The academic arts such as grammar, logic, and music.</note> and *Mechanical* <note>The practical or manual arts.</note>, none teems with as many impostors as this one. Yet it is deservedly to be venerated for the admirable secrets it contains, and is to be preferred above all other earthly sciences by true physicians. These are the men who, enlightened by the spirit of *Divine Wisdom* and provided with and content with honorable food and clothing—for it is impossible for one who is needy or not free to *Philosophize* <note>The author argues that true scientific and spiritual inquiry requires a degree of financial independence and mental freedom.</note>—pray to God with religious veneration, following the example of Solomon: not for the granting of riches, but for the obtaining of wisdom, that the storehouse of *Divine* knowledge might be opened to them. 

These are the ones who measure their happiness by Heaven and by the love of *GOD*, the giver of all good things; whom, moreover, the love of secrets and of *Nature* (according to *Divine grace*) promotes and stimulates to investigate. Out of a desire to attain knowledge, without vain hope of profit or the affectation of empty glory, they refuse no manual labor that is honorable, long-lasting, and possible within the *Fear of GOD*. Finally, without malicious intent and neglecting the source of parched human thirst, they use such great gifts most humbly with fear and trembling for the End due to the Master of *Nature*: namely, for the Praise and Honor of *GOD*, and for their own [benefit] and that of their needy neighbor...

By the same Spirit of the world, and the same Heat of the Sun and Moon by which human bodies are cleansed of infirmities and accidents, imperfect and impure metals are also restored to **True Health**—which is **goldenness** <note>original: "aureitas." # ADMONITIONS
### N 2

<margin>
When the purified Elements are reduced to a pure and equal simplicity, then one possesses the Medicine for prolonging life, because in this state the Elements are balanced. For inequality and the dominance of one element over another generates disease. Health consists in a Balanced body. Let it seem a wonder to no one that, following the example of the celestial Sun which dries Mud but melts Wax, a single action of one Thing is diversified in various ways, not because of itself, but according to the Nature of the Recipient.
</margin>

Truly, the true origin of all bodily diseases, according to more sensible physicians, is the *distortion of the Natural proportion of the Three Primes* <note>original: "Naturalis proportionis Primorum Trium enormitas." In Paracelsian alchemy, the Three Primes—Sulfur, Mercury, and Salt—are the fundamental components of all matter. Their imbalance was thought to cause illness.</note> (*or, to speak with the common lot of physicians, the immoderation and imbalance of the four Elements or Humors* <term>Humors: The four bodily fluids—blood, phlegm, black bile, and yellow bile—which Greek and Medieval medicine held must remain in balance for health.</term>) from which the Human body is composed, whether it be sick or well. However, this aforementioned medicine—which is in itself the very matter of our Creation—is a congenial and uniform substance, consisting in equality. It is a most subtle *Soul* <note>original: "Anima"</note> separated from the dregs, like a *simple substance of the Elements; a Fifth Being or Quintessential Virtue resulting from the purer Essence of the four Elements*. Once purified and incorruptible, it is compared to heaven; it admits no malignant spirit, for they flee from it. And because it is *least liable to Temperate corruption or decay*, it expels, as far as is *Naturally* possible, all accidental corruptibility from which infirmity can arise. It restores interior vigor through all the members and cures diseases caused by the "exaltation" <note>In alchemy, an "exaltation" refers to an element becoming too dominant or potent, throwing the system out of alignment.</note> of the *Three Primes* by bringing them back into reconciliation.

*The Health of Man consists in the harmony and union of the Three Primary substances*: but where they are exalted and ignited by the *Stars*, internal wars follow. And because the *Three Primes of diseases are volatile, they yield to the Essence of Fire, which consumes the disease and separates the pure from the impure*. Furthermore, that *Fifth Virtue binds the Elements or Humors of the Human body in peace and a Harmonic treaty*, reducing unequal parts to a true *Balance* by making them equal. It strengthens the innate heat and the substantial moisture; it *preserves the oil and the little flame of Life in equality through its celestial vigor*. (For as long as the *Radical Moisture* <term>Radical Moisture: Also called "Radical Humor," this was imagined as a vital, oily fluid or "balm" within the body that acted as the fuel for life's flame; its exhaustion resulted in old age and death.</term>, the *Vital Balsam*, and the *most precious Nectar of our Life*—since the strengthening power of the Human and Animal body proceeds from the *spirit of Life*—remains in its proper quantity, no disease is felt.) It restores the sick to health and balance, keeps *Nature* herself in her proper being, and preserves the *Nectar of our Life* in a good and praiseworthy *Balance*.

In this way, until *Natural* death (that is, to that *Limit* of life which *Almighty God* established for Man because of the disobedience of both our first parent and each individual’s own sins), this medicine will preserve a predisposed person—one who uses it prudently and appropriately with a pious *invocation of the Divine Name*—safe and whole from disease, maintaining the radiance of *Youth* and the prime of life (which is the age of *Human Beauty and Strength*), provided that the constitution of the body and its temperament are not damaged beyond measure. Therefore, in this *Quintessence and Spiritual Medicine, which is of the Nature and Heat of Heaven, and not in our Mortal and corruptible nature,* [the power of healing resides]...

Therefore, so that the consumption and dissipation of the said spirit may be avoided (as far as Nature allows), this spirit and natural heat existing in Human bodies, thus diminished or hindered, must be increased and comforted, so that it may perform its duty more strongly and effectively.*

I add that it would be vain to wish to preserve a corruptible body through a putrid and corruptible thing, to heal the sick through a sick thing, or to shape a thing through something subject to deformity. One must make this heat similar to our own heat or spirit, which happens when it has been prepared into a medicine and most sweet food, so that when taken by mouth, it immediately penetrates the human body, and its power and spirit keep every thing—especially the flesh united to it—uncorrupted.

—especially if it is done with the greatest excess of the Mind's Imagination and will, directed toward that which it desires to attract, change, bind, or hinder. And whoever is patient for *Truth*, putting aside malice, and approaches the reading of these things with a clear mind, examining everything deeply with a diligent and considerate judgment of the MIND not corrupted by passions—he will at last confess with great gratitude that the doors and innermost sanctuaries of each *Light* <note>In the philosophy of Paracelsus and his followers, "each Light" refers to the "Light of Nature" (reason and observation) and the "Light of Grace" (divine revelation).</note> have been unlocked by the favor of the supreme *Creator's* power. From all these things properly understood, by **PRAYING and WORKING** <note>original: "ORANDO & LABORANDO." This is a variation of the famous alchemical and monastic motto "Ora et Labora," emphasizing that spiritual devotion and physical experimentation must go hand-in-hand.</note>, he will bring forth fruits far more abundant than his expectations. 

If by chance there are men of twisted opinion, ignorant of the *Truth* and of a peevish palate, who in their reckless ignorance ungratefully count a benefit against our talent as an injury—those who may not have use for this work, sincerely shared from the hand of God for His glory and the benefit of his neighbor to promote the needy Commonwealth—let them not unjustly attack with their proud and reckless censures, like *Aesop’s* little crow <note>A reference to the fable of the jackdaw/crow that dressed itself in the feathers of other birds to appear more beautiful, only to be stripped bare. The author is accusing critics of being "borrowed" intellects.</note>, or with the reproach of being a "patchwork of mixed grain." For indeed, to extract the grain from the chaff and to separate the true from the false is a task of no less skill and success than it is of most tedious labor. Let them not unjustly harass the diligent, laborious efforts and the "sweat of others" <note>An idiom for someone else's hard work</note> of certain *Experience* (let those who have sweated in similar matters be the judge). Nor, like Timon the <term>misanthrope: one who hates or avoids human society</term> seeing with a grim mind, let them confirm their bitterness to posterity, or publish to the whole world their cruel and detestable inhumanity or their most unjust hatred of the *Truth*—unless, instead of a response, they wish to be called what they already are: enemies of the human race and adversaries of the public health, who ought to be rightfully banished from the assembly of the learned. 

Let them not deter those studious of truth who will gratefully receive these labors of ours and our faithful diligence. Or, if they are able, while the opportunity is now offered to them to publish their own *Observations*, let them draw from their own springs and bring them outdoors. Lest the curse of the barren fig tree fall upon them, let them bring out their light lit "under a bushel" <note>A biblical reference (Matthew 5:15) to hiding one's light/talents.</note>. Leaving aside idle word-battles and useless scholastic questions and disputes—for it is easy for a versatile and litigious Sceptic Philosopher, whose purpose is not finding truth but arguing, to prove, defend, or dilute anything with a shouting match—let them instead be incited and provoked by my example, as becomes good and sincere citizens of the Medical and <term>Spagyric: alchemical medicine involving the separation and recombination of natural elements</term> Republic. Since Medicine has not yet reached the limit of its perfection, but many things remain to be revealed to future ages, let them bring forth better things than these from their own experience. Let them help the needy LAZARUS not with syllogistic or Levitical WORDS, but with Samaritan WORKS <note>The author contrasts "Levitical" words (referring to the priest who walked past the injured man in the parable) with "Samaritan" works (the one who actually helped).</note>. # THE UNIVERSAL DIGE-
## STIVE OR MATURA-
### TIVE. <note>In early modern medicine, a "Digestive" was a remedy intended to "cook" or prepare "crude" disease-causing matter so it could be easily expelled from the body. "Maturative" refers to bringing an illness or an abscess to its peak or "ripeness."</note>

In diseases that consist of mobile and superficial impurities, which have not driven deep roots nor are destined for difficult **coagulations** <term>Coagulations: In iatrochemistry, the thickening or hardening of bodily fluids into stones, obstructions, or "tartar" that causes disease.</term>—which is discerned from the signatures of pain and the inconsistent and swollen **effervescences** <term>Effervescences: The boiling or bubbling up of humors (bodily fluids) as the body attempts to fight off an illness.</term> of symptoms, such as most fevers, catarrhs, coughs, hoarseness, and similar affections—in those cases there is no need for a Digestive; they are safely and suddenly removed by the help of **Purgatives** and **Cleansers**. However, febrile and inflammatory impurities, which have more difficult **tinctures** <note>original: "tincturas"; here referring to the deep-seated qualities or "stains" of a disease that permeate the tissues.</note>, because they [must be] reso- <note>The text breaks off mid-word, likely "resolvi" (resolved).</note>

<header>CHEMICAL MATTERS.</header>
<sig>P 2</sig>
<meta>catchword: Chemical-</meta>

<margin>Preparation for an easy evacuation without harming Nature.</margin>
Those solutions and coagulations of vapors that take on a fixed form are difficult to resolve (such things are constantly found in vulnerable parts of the body and related minerals). They are most safely and conveniently cured through the **CONCOCTION** <term>Concoction: In early medicine, this is the process where the body "cooks" or ripens raw, diseased humors to prepare them for expulsion.</term> of Hippocrates, the **MITIGATION** of Paracelsus, or the **EPICRASIS** <term>Epicrasis: A Galenic method of treatment that involves a gradual tempering or evacuation of harmful humors rather than a violent purging.</term> of Galen—all of which are essentially equivalent curative approaches. These conditions do not obey the raw powers of common purgative medicines, which act upon the physical and crude spirits and only worsen the "boiling over" (effervescence) of diseased spirits. However, once the heat of the spirits has ceased and the matter has been resolved and reached a suitable coagulation—having been freed from the bonds of those spirits—it then permits easy purging.

<margin>Aphorism 22, section 1 <note>Referring to the Aphorisms of Hippocrates.</note></margin>
In chronic diseases—such as **Epilepsy**, **Quartan fevers** <note>A recurring fever, often associated with malaria, that peaks every fourth day.</note>, **Colic**, **Nephritis** <note>Kidney disease or stones.</note>, **Gout**, and all **Tartaric** <term>Tartaric: Referring to diseases caused by the buildup of stony, hard deposits in the body, likened to the tartar crust left in wine barrels.</term> affections, **Dropsy**, and **Leprous** conditions—the fundamental impurities are cured properly and primarily by **RESOLUTION**, not by Concoction. Indeed, one waits in vain for signs of "cooking" (concoction) in these cases. The cure must be established immediately through Resolution: by consumption, destruction, and removal. If **Mitigation** <term>Mitigation: The chemical process of softening or calming a substance or a bodily "spirit."</term> is also applied, we shall achieve our goal more happily. However, the "fruits," the fits (paroxysms), and the boiling over of these "fruits" in some types of the aforementioned diseases do require the indications for Concoction and Tempering. In those instances, the decree of Hippocrates holds place, asserting: *Only those things which are concocted should be treated, unless they are in a state of swelling.* <note>original: "Concocta solum medicanda, nisi turgeant." This is a fundamental rule of ancient medicine: do not interfere with the body's humors until they have "ripened" or become "concocted," unless the pressure of the fluid is dangerously high.</note>

## *Observations.*

<margin>If too small a quantity of oil of Vitriol is added, it will at least induce vomiting.</margin>
I. Care must be taken when adding the oil of Vitriol so that the taste of the resulting salt is not overly acidic, but rather somewhat nauseating. If too much oil of Vitriol is added, it will not purge effectively; otherwise, it operates through the four emunctories <term>Emunctories: The body’s natural waste-disposal channels, such as the skin, kidneys, and bowels.</term>: namely, through vomiting, bowel movements (if mixed with other purgatives), as well as through urine and sweat.

II. If it can be done using a funnel with a very narrow opening—so that by a certain skill the drops of Vitriol oil fall only gradually and one after another into the oil of Tartar—it will be more advisable. In this way, the "good spirits" that normally rise as vapors and vanish during the sudden bubbling <note>original: "effervescentiâ"</note> of the mixture will be retained.

III. The glass vessel becomes extremely hot from the joining of these two "Fires." <note>Alchemists often viewed the reaction between an acid and a base as a conflict or union of internal "fires" or spirits.</note> In this mutual bubbling, one can observe the very generation of **Epilepsy**; specifically, it shows how the Spirit of Life in the **Microcosm** <term>Microcosm: A central concept in Renaissance medicine where the human body is viewed as a "little world" that perfectly mirrors the laws and structures of the greater universe (the Macrocosm).</term>, when provoked by foreign elements, boils over in a similar fashion.

# CHEMICAL MATTERS.

Regarding purgatives, we first encounter **Mercury**, and although its impurities are deeply intertwined, they can nevertheless be removed through ingenious adaptation.

<margin>
This **Water of Wisdom** <note>original: "Aqua Sapientiae"</note> is known only to a few.
</margin>

**Hermetic philosophers** <term>Hermetic Philosophers: Followers of the teachings attributed to Hermes Trismegistus, a legendary figure who combined science, religion, and philosophy, often focusing on the transformation of matter.</term> have hitherto regarded this "common mercury" <note>original: "Mercurium vulgi"</note> as nothing more than a servant or a kind of fugitive slave. ### PRECIPITATED MERCURY.

**Take** [℞] half a pound of well-purified **Mercury**, to which should be poured 1 lb. of **Oil of Sulfur** made by the bell <term>Oil of Sulfur per campanam: Sulfuric acid produced by burning sulfur under a glass bell jar to capture the vapors; it was considered purer than oil of vitriol.</term> and rectified (for this oil, above all other corrosives, precipitates and coagulates it best, and much more powerfully than Oil of Vitriol, so that it may even endure a greater firing). Let the mixture be digested in a sand bath for two days; afterwards, distill it gradually through a glass retort protected with **luting** <term>Luting: A paste (often made of clay, lime, or glass) used to seal vessel joints and protect glassware from the direct heat of the fire.</term>. Pour the resulting liquid back in again, and repeat this a third time. On the fourth occasion, some fresh Oil of Sulfur can be poured on once more, and toward the end, with the fire increased during distillation, it should be drawn off until the retort glows red-hot. Thus, in the distillation itself, the Mercury is precipitated into a white mass. 

Afterward, the retort having been broken, remove the mass and grind it upon marble, and carefully wash away the **saltiness** <note>original: "falsedinem"; the acrid or acidic residue remaining from the oil of sulfur.</note> with warm distilled rainwater in a wide-mouthed glass. Let it be stirred well, and for four hours let the water always settle before it is poured off. You shall repeat this **edulcoration** <term>Edulcoration: From the Latin 'dulcis' (sweet); the process of washing a substance with water to remove "sharp" or acidic salts, making it 'sweet' or mild enough for medicinal use.</term> as many times as necessary until you detect no more saltiness in the poured-on water, and you see the remaining Mercury turned into a very yellow powder. Afterward, having first dried it, you shall place this powder into a vial with a long neck to be closed with **cotton** <note>original: "bombyce"; silk or cotton wadding used as a breathable stopper.</note>, and at the be-

In the second method, the corrosive spirits of Vitriol <term>Vitriol: A historical term for sulfates, particularly iron or copper sulfate, from which sulfuric acid was derived.</term> and Salt are mortified <note>original: "mortificantur"; in alchemy, "mortification" refers to the alteration or destruction of a substance's outward form to change its properties.</note> in sublimated Mercury, from which, by a wondrous and simple homogeneous artifice, a crystalline powder is produced that is plainly tasteless. This is one of the most excellent Cathartics <term>Cathartics: Medicines used to promote the evacuation of the bowels or "purge" the system.</term>, which, used either on its own or with other pills <note>original: "catapotiis"</note> in medical practice, radically expels all harmful things from the human body. This will not seem strange to those who know that Mercury is the Balsam of Nature, in which resides an Incarnative and Regenerative power, wonderfully renewing and clearing away all impurities.

## FLOWERS OF BUTTER
## OF ANTIMONY.

That powder...

# P A N C H Y M A G O G O N
<note>original: "Panchymagogon"; a Greek-derived term meaning "that which leads away all humors." It refers to a "universal purge" intended to cleanse the body of all four primary humors: blood, phlegm, yellow bile, and black bile.</note>

Among all purgative medicines, though I have spared neither labor nor expense, I have not yet been able to find one, despite many experiments, that performs the desired operations more successfully and with less discomfort when taken than the Panchymagogon.

If Antimony—which has become infamous and abominable among the common people due to the violence of the vomiting it causes—could be prepared in such a way that it performed its function at least through the lower parts <note>original: "per inferiora"; meaning it acts as a laxative rather than an emetic.</note> without that common violence (which, however, has been mostly removed from it in my previous assigned preparations), there would hardly be a more pleasant purgative in the nature of things. But such a preparation, though very often attempted, has not yet been obtained by the benefit of <term>Pyrotechny: The "art of fire," a traditional name for early chemistry and alchemy emphasizing the use of the furnace to refine substances.</term>, much less have I seen it in any Chemist's workshop, although many falsely boast about it for the sake of showing off, just as they do with <term>Potable Gold: "Aurum Potabile," a legendary alchemical remedy where gold is supposedly dissolved into a liquid state to act as a universal panacea.</term>.

Of the Species <term>Diarrhodon Abbatis: A cooling, rose-based herbal compound used to strengthen the internal organs.</term>
and of <term>Diambra: An aromatic medicinal powder made of ambergris, musk, and spices, used as a restorative tonic.</term>, one ounce of each.

From these, a Tincture is extracted using <term>Spirit of Wine: Distilled alcohol, used as a powerful solvent in pharmacy.</term> through <term>digestion: A process of soaking a substance in a solvent at a gentle, constant heat to extract its medicinal properties.</term> for fourteen days, stirring several times daily as is proper; it is then kept separately.

## THE TRUE PREPARATION OF
## SCAMMONY.
<note>Scammony is a resin obtained from the root of *Convolvulus scammonia*. In its raw state, it was notorious in early medicine for being a "drastic" purgative, often causing severe abdominal pain.</note>

Take: half a pound of selected, unadulterated <term>Scammony: A potent resin used as a laxative</term>; let it be ground and sifted. Afterwards, pour over it a little juice of pale roses, or—what is better—wild roses, which has been pressed and strained (having added one or two drops of <term>spirit of Vitriol: An early name for sulfuric acid, used here in tiny amounts to preserve the juice</term>. That juice should be kept in a cold place for use, so that it does not turn sour). Then, let the drying process be carried out in the Sun or behind a furnace. This soaking and drying should be repeated twenty or thirty times; for in this way the sluggish, viscous, and tenacious <term>malignity: The harmful or "poisonous" quality of a raw drug that causes side effects</term> of the Scammony is dissipated, which otherwise is accustomed to excite <term>griping: "tormina," or sharp, twisting pains in the bowels</term> and torments by sticking to the linings of the stomach. Whoever wishes may add to the first juice, at their discretion, half a part of pressed and purified juice of <term>Quinces: A fruit often used in old pharmacy to "comfort" the stomach and temper harsh medicines</term>; in this way, it will purge more effectively and with less distress. And with this prepared Scammony, you will be able to arouse and sharpen the purging power of all <term>Cathartics: Medicines used to evacuate the bowels</term>.

### *Usage.*

In many diseases requiring <term>Evacuation: The removal of waste or "humors" from the body</term>.

### *Dosage.*

Five grains: for a stronger person, from 12 to 15 and 20 grains can be offered.

Let pills be formed from it, or [kept] in powder after drying...

## THE TRUE PREPARATION 
## OF SCAMMONY.
<note>original: "SCAMMONII VERA PRÆPARATIO"</note>

Take half a pound of selected, unadulterated <term>Scammony: A potent and historically harsh resinous purgative derived from the root of the *Convolvulus scammonia* plant</term>. Let it be ground and sifted; afterward, pour over it a little juice of pale roses, or—what is better—wild roses, which has been pressed and strained (adding one or two drops of <term>spirit of Vitriol: An early chemical name for sulfuric acid</term>. That juice is kept in a cold place for use so that it does not turn sour). Then, let the drying be carried out in the sun or behind a furnace <note>The area "behind the furnace" provided a source of gentle, consistent dry heat necessary for evaporation without burning the medicine</note>. This soaking and drying should be repeated twenty or thirty times; for in this way, the sluggish, viscous, and sticky malignity <note>original: "malignitas"; referring here to the harsh chemical properties that cause severe side effects</note> of the Scammony is dissipated, which otherwise, by its sticking to the linings of the stomach, is accustomed to provoke griping pains and torments. # A SPECIFIC PURGATIVE
## OF PARACELSUS.
<note>Paracelsus (1493–1541) was a revolutionary Swiss physician and alchemist who advocated for the use of minerals and chemicals in medicine rather than just herbs.</note>

First, let the purification of <term>Vitriol: Traditionally, a metal sulfate; in this context, Hungarian Vitriol usually refers to copper sulfate</term> from its sulfur be performed in the following manner:

Take Hungarian Vitriol and dissolve it in common water in a copper cauldron. Into the solution, sprinkle common <term>Oil of Tartar: A concentrated solution of potassium carbonate</term>; about four ounces of Oil of Tartar are required for every three pounds of Vitriol. Allow the clear solution to evaporate little by little until a crust almost begins to form on the surface; afterwards, in the cold, the Vitriol crystallizes into small stones, which should be kept.

# 2. SPIRIT OF SALT.

Take 4 pounds of native <term>Salt of Kraków</term> <note>original: "Salis Cracoviensis"; likely referring to the famous rock salt from the Wieliczka mines</note>, or dried or <term>calcined: heated to a high temperature to remove volatile substances</term> sea salt. From this mixture, make round or oblong balls, which you should place behind the furnace to dry until hard. Put them into an earthenware <term>retort: a glassware or ceramic vessel used for distillation</term> coated with <term>lute: a clay or paste used to seal chemical apparatus</term> <note>original: "luto obductæ"</note>, filled barely to the half-way point. Let a sufficiently large <term>Receiver: a vessel designed to collect the products of distillation</term> be joined to it. After observing the proper stages of the fire until the <term>phlegm: the watery, initial distillate</term> has come out, finally drive it with a strong and unceasing open fire, continuing until all the white vapors have emerged. The distillation is the same as that which is usually employed in preparing <term>Aqua Fortis</term> <note>original: "aqua Forti"; literally "Strong Water," referring to nitric acid</note>.

Take care that the fire does not become too strong, because of the extreme penetration of the spirits. 

Water flows out first, then a foul-smelling oil: let them be separated by a <term>separatory funnel</term> <note>original: "tritorium"</note>. The water or spirit is first corrected and <term>rectified</term> <note>purified by re-distillation</note> in a cellar by placing it for eight days in cold or damp sand. ### *Observation*

That stench of the Spirit of Tartar is not to be entirely removed, nor should it be feared, since it possesses the **Signature of Stenches** <note>referring to the 'Doctrine of Signatures,' the belief that a substance's sensory qualities, like a foul smell, indicate its specific healing powers—in this case, treating "foul" diseases</note>. ### VI.

# STRENGTHENING REMEDY.

This remedy strengthens and corroborates the **Internal and Innate Balsam** <note>the body's natural self-healing essence, a concept popularized by Paracelsus</note> by clarifying and purifying the spirits and all the elements of the **microcosm** <note>the human body, viewed as a miniature version of the universe</note>. In this matter, according to **Paracelsus** <note>a famous Swiss physician and alchemist (1493–1541) who revolutionized medicine with chemical treatments</note>, one should not worry whether a thing is "hot" or "cold" in nature <note>a rejection of traditional Galenic medicine which focused on balancing these qualities</note>, but rather the power of the **arcanum** <note>the secret, essential medicinal power of a substance</note> must be considered.

Thus, cures that are completed through strengthening, calming, and soothing are safer, more excellent, and more profound, because they approach more closely the nature and properties of the **Innate Balsam**. As far as possible, these should be mixed and joined with the earlier indications for treatment—that is, with **Purgatives** <note>laxatives</note>, **Resolvents** <note>substances that "dissolve" tumors or inflammation</note>, **Cleansers**, **Diuretics** <note>to promote urine flow</note>, **Diaphoretics** <note>to induce sweating</note>, and **Purifiers**.

### SALT OF ORIENTAL PEARLS.

Various ways have been devised for dissolving Pearls: through spirit of vitriol <note>an early name for sulfuric acid</note>, or through rectified spirit of Guaiacum <note>a resinous wood from the Americas used as a "wonder drug" for various ailments</note>. ### *Dosage.*

The dose of the Salt ranges from 10, 12, or 15 grains up to 1 scruple <note>a traditional unit of weight equal to 20 grains, or roughly 1.3 grams</note>, administered in suitable waters such as Cinnamon or Bugloss <note>a plant, also known as oxtongue, often used in historical medicine to "comfort the heart" and treat melancholy</note>.

<margin>Herbs and flowers that emit yellow drops during distillation.</margin>
It is also offered in the water of **May Dew** <note>original: "Roris Majalis"; dew collected in the early morning during May was highly prized by alchemists as a "celestial" solvent</note> collected from wheat or grain.

Or it may be given in the water of **Sundew** <note>original: "Rorella" or "Roris Solis"</note>, which turns yellow during distillation. This is a marvelous thing, just as Saffron <note>original: "Crocus"</note> does, and as does the expressed juice of **Mullein** <note>original: "Verbasci"</note> flowers when it is set in the sun and distilled.

It should be noted that if pearls are dissolved by means of distilled vinegar, and the sweetened Salt is allowed to liquefy in a cellar during the appropriate months, then a few drops of this liquor—by a wonderful and pleasant spectacle—will coagulate the finest **Alcohol of Wine** <note>high-purity ethanol</note> into a **Spreadable Butter** <note>original: "Butyrum scissile"; a chemical state where the liquid alcohol thickens into a waxy or buttery consistency</note>.

## SALT OF CORALS.

In the same way, the **Salt of Corals** is prepared, as is the salt of pearl-bearing shells, "crab's eyes" <note>stony concretions found in the stomachs of crawfish, used as an antacid</note>, and other stones from crustaceans.

## PARACELSUS’S ELIXIR OF PROPERTY
### (ELIXIR PROPRIETATIS)

->℞ Alexandrian Myrrh<-
->Hepatic Aloes<- <note>original: "Aloës Epat."; Hepatic or "liver-colored" aloes were a common grade of aloe resin used in pharmacy.</note>

# CHYMICA.

...[might be discove]red, that which Paracelsus studiously concealed.

->*Powers & Uses*<-

It is the balsam of the ancients, as Paracelsus says, composed of entirely subtle parts, heating and drying, and thus preserving against putrefaction. It is a perfect Elixir; in it are all the virtues of Natural Balsam <note>Natural Balsam was often used to describe the "mummy" or innate life-force within the body that prevents decay.</note>, and the greatest preservative power, especially for the elderly.

1. It performs miracles in ailments of the Chest and Lungs.
2. It is wonderfully effective against the contagions of the pestilential scourge <note>original: "pestiferæ Luis"; referring to the plague or similar infectious diseases.</note> spreading among the people, and against corrupt air <note>During this period, "corrupt air" or miasma was believed to be the primary cause of disease outbreaks.</note>.
3. It draws out various humors <term>Humors|The four fluids—blood, phlegm, black bile, and yellow bile—which early medicine believed governed human health and temperament</term> from the stomach, strengthens the stomach and intestines, and preserves them from pains.
4. It aids those with **hectic fevers** <term>Hectic fever|A persistent, wasting fever often associated with chronic diseases like tuberculosis</term>, **catarrhs** <term>Catarrh|An excessive buildup of mucus in the nose or throat</term>, and coughs in general, and it cleanses the chest.
5. It is beneficial for the "chilling" of the head and stomach.
6. It cures **migraines** <note>original: "Hemicraniam"</note> and vertigo.
7. It dispels dimness of the eyes.
8. It strengthens the heart and the memory.
9. Gradually, it relieves itching <note>original: "Pruritum"</note>, as well as pain in the flanks and ribs.
10. It breaks up kidney stones.
11. It cures **quartan fever** <term>Quartan fever|A form of malaria where the fever recurs every fourth day</term>.
12. It preserves against **paralysis** and **gout** <note>original: "Podagra"; specifically gout of the foot.</note>.
13. It sharpens the intellect and all the senses.
14. It takes away **melancholy** <note>In the 17th century, melancholy was seen as both a physical excess of black bile and a state of deep sadness or depression.</note> and brings joy.
15. It keeps old age at bay through the strongest preservation of youth and delays the graying of hair.

<header>THE ROYAL PHARMACY</header>

...from the specifically prepared [substance], they extracted a colored essence, used for medical purposes with great benefit to the sick.

## PARACELSUS’S ELIXIR OF
## PROPERTY.

-> ℞ Alexandrian Myrrh <-
-> Hepatic Aloe <note>original: "Aloës Epat."; a variety of aloe named for its liver-like color, often used in purgative medicines.</note> <-
-> Oriental Saffron, 4 ounces of each. <-

Let all these be diligently powdered and placed in a glass vessel, moistening them with the best **alcoholized Spirit of Wine** <term>Spirit of Wine|Highly concentrated distilled alcohol, similar to modern ethanol</term>. Afterward, pour on **rectified Oil of Sulphur made by the bell** <term>Oil of Sulphur per campanam|A potent acid—essentially sulfuric acid—produced by burning sulfur under a glass bell jar to capture the condensation</term> (let that oil be prepared from yellow or grayish sulfur during rainy weather, for in this way you will obtain a greater quantity <note>Alchemists believed the humidity in the air during rain helped the sulfurous vapors condense into liquid acid.</note>) to a height of 4 fingers. Place it in **digestion and circulation** <term>Circulation|The process of heating a liquid so that it evaporates and then condenses back down into the vessel, constantly "cycling" the substance to refine it</term> for two months. Finally, separate that which has been tinted and extracted by decanting <note>original: "per inclinationem"; tilting the vessel to pour off the liquid without disturbing the sediment.</note>; pour good Spirit of Wine onto the material remaining at the bottom, and by circulating it again for two months, extract the color once more. Separate this, and mix it with the first colored liquid. The dregs at the bottom should be slowly distilled; that which comes out first should be added to the aforementioned Tincture, and thus let them circulate for one more month without further distillation. The taste is pleasant, not bitter, and lacks any flavor of **burnt matter** <term>Empyreuma|The scorched or acrid smell and taste resulting from over-heating organic substances during distillation</term>, as commonly happens in ordinary distillation.

It must be diligently observed that the material should first be sprinkled with the Spirit of Wine so that it becomes like a paste, and only then should the Oil of Sulphur be poured on; otherwise, the entire material will be burned into blackness.

<header>CHEMISTRY</header>

### *Powers and Uses*

It is the **Balsam of the Ancients**, as Paracelsus says, composed of entirely subtle parts; it is heating and drying, and thus preserves against decay <note>original: "putrefactione"; the process of rotting or decomposition, which alchemists believed could be prevented in the living body through such elixirs.</note>. It is a perfect Elixir, containing all virtues. It possesses the greatest natural balsamic and preservative power, especially for the elderly.

1. It performs wonders in afflictions of the **Chest** and **Lungs**.
2. It is wonderfully effective against the contagions of the **pestilential plague** <note>original: "pestiferæ Luis"; a general term for a devastating infectious disease or "the Great Pox."</note> spreading through the population, and against corrupt air <note>Before the germ theory of disease, "corrupt air" or miasma was believed to be the carrier of infection.</note>.
3. It draws out various humors of the **stomach**, strengthens the stomach and intestines, and preserves them from pain.
4. It assists those suffering from **wasting fevers** <term>Hectics|Chronic, debilitating fevers, often associated with the later stages of tuberculosis</term>, catarrhs <note>original: "Catharrosis"; an excessive buildup of phlegm or mucus.</note>, and coughs in general, and it cleanses the chest.
5. It is beneficial for the "cooling" of the **Head** and **Stomach** <note>In the humoral medical system, an organ becoming too "cold" led to sluggishness and poor digestion.</note>.
6. It cures **migraines** <note>original: "Hemicraniam"; literally pain affecting one side of the head.</note> and dizziness.
7. It dispels dimness of the eyes.
8. It strengthens the **Heart** and the **memory**.
9. It gradually relieves itching, as well as pain in the flanks and ribs.
10. It breaks up **kidney stones**.
11. It cures **quartan fever** <note>original: "Quartanam"; a form of malaria where the fever recurs every four days.</note>.
12. It protects against **Paralysis** and **Gout** <term>Podagra|A painful form of inflammatory arthritis, often associated with a wealthy lifestyle and rich food</term>.
13. It sharpens the intellect and all the senses.
14. It removes **melancholy** and brings about joy.
15. It wards off old age by the powerful preservation of youth and delays the turning of hair to gray.

From 6 to 10 or 12 drops in wine or an appropriate and specific water <note>A "specific water" refers to a medicinal distillate (like rose or lavender water) chosen to target the patient's specific ailment.</note>.

### STRENGTHENING BALMS THICKENED BY THE BENEFIT OF WAX.

Because Aromatic Oils in liquid form cannot be carried about suitably or conveniently due to the danger of spilling or the breaking of glass, Chemical Physicians <term>Chymiatrists|Medical practitioners who used chemical and alchemical methods to create medicines, largely following the school of Paracelsus</term> began to devise a method of thickening them. This was done so that various types of these balms could be carried more easily in tin or silver boxes (which must be well-gilded) and be ready at hand in case of urgent necessity.

To make these, it is enough for now to have at least suggested to the skillful that the preparation of each requires both an oil drawn out by distillation, and a Tincture extracted by Alcoholized Spirit of Wine <note>original: "S.v. Alcoholisatum"; highly rectified or pure ethanol.</note> and thickened by separating it from that same Spirit. Likewise, one needs the Salt drawn out from its **dead head** <term>Caput Mortuum|The useless solid residue remaining after a substance has been distilled or heated to exhaustion; literally "death's head."</term> after incineration, using the aid of Water. The medium which provides the proper consistency is shavings of white Wax, which has been boiled several times in Rose Water to remove its bitterness, so that it does not possess any foreign quality of taste <meta>The sentence continues on the next page; the catchword "litatem" is the suffix of "qualitatem" (quality).</meta>

<note>original vocabulary: Vitam (Life), Vulnera (Wounds), Dosis (Dosage), Olea Aromatica (Aromatic Oils), Chymiatri (Chemical Physicians), Balsama (Balms), Cera (Wax), Alcoholisatum (Alcoholized), Salem (Salt), Spiritu (Spirit).</note>

### VII.

# PAIN-RELIEVING, MITIGATING, SLEEP-INDUCING,
## S E D A T I N G.

There are many diseases that cannot be cured without Pain-relievers <note>original: "Anodynis"</note>. Therefore, in the treatments of all diseases, where sleeplessness—the companion of pain—and the loss of strength are present, appropriate internal Pain-relievers can be administered, so that once the very roots of the destructive torturous symptoms are removed, a friendly rest may be restored to Nature <note>To early modern doctors, "Nature" referred to the body's internal healing force which required rest to function.</note>.

For sleep is a secret remedy <note>original: "arcanum" – a term used by Paracelsus to describe a powerful, hidden medicinal virtue that acts directly on the body's essence.</note> in medicine, above all gems and precious stones. And he who can conveniently apply a sleep-inducing secret remedy taken from the true Essence to a needy Nature (especially when the sleeping enemy-diseases have been untimely awakened from sleep), that physician is to be greatly honored by the patient.

---

## OBSERVATIONS on the preparation
## of Laudanum.

<margin>For then the greatest power of the spirit, or the First Being <note>original: "primum Ens" — in alchemy, this refers to the primordial essence or the most purified "first state" of a substance.</note> of the plant, is still concentrated in the root.</margin>
1. The younger, fresh, succulent roots and outer barks of Henbane <note>original: "Hyoscyami"</note> are to be collected—throwing away the internal woody trunk—while the Sun and Moon are positioned in either Aries or Libra before the full moon. Others collect them, if possible, at the very hour when the Moon is renewed in the said Signs. The expressed juice, having been skimmed and passed through a filter, is thickened in a warm place to the consistency of honey, and afterwards hardens in the Sun; from this, a Tincture is extracted with Spirit of Wine <note>High-proof distilled alcohol.</note>.

2. Opium should first be purified in a liquor of Hyssop, or in distilled water, as is customary with Aloe; afterwards, it should also be extracted with Spirit of Wine.

3. The juice of Henbane and the opium (before they are mixed with the remaining ingredients) should first cast off their "sulphurs" <note>In the 17th century, "sulphur" often referred to the flammable or oily component of a substance, which was sometimes thought to contain its "toxic" heat.</note> and harmful poisons through digestion <note>The process of steeping a substance in gentle heat over time.</note>; this poison seeks the surface like a foam. It is from this "foam" that such various and calamitous symptoms arise in those sick patients who use Opium and Henbane that has not been properly purified. Because this has been noticed by very few until now, I did not wish to hide it from the Chemical Republic <note>original: "Rempubl. Chymicam" — the international community of alchemists and physicians.</note>.

4. The things to be extracted should be extracted with rectified Spirit of Wine; the longer they are afterwards digested together, the more powerful the operation will be.

5. For women and those suffering from hysteria <note>original: "hystericis" — historically, this referred to a wide range of symptoms believed to be caused by the "suffocation of the womb."</note>, Ambergris and Musk should be omitted from the composition because of the "suffocation of the womb" <note>Early modern doctors believed the uterus was sensitive to strong smells, and that pungent aromas like musk could cause it to move upward, "suffocating" the patient.</note>; or, to suppress the odor, a few grains of Castoreum <note>A yellowish secretion from the scent glands of beavers, used frequently in medicine to treat "vapors" and uterine issues.</note> should be added.

# OBSERVATIONS on the preparation *of Laudanum.*

---

<margin>For then the greatest power of the spirit, or the "First Essence" <note>original: "primum Ens" — in alchemy, the most fundamental, purified form of a substance.</note> of the herb, is still concentrated in the root.</margin>
1. The young, fresh, succulent, and outer parts of the roots and bark of *Henbane* <note>original: "Hyoscyamus" — a potent sedative plant.</note> (throwing away the inner woody core) should be gathered when the Sun and Moon are in either Aries or Libra before the full moon; others gather them, if possible, at the very hour when the Moon is renewed in those same Signs. The pressed juice, cleared of foam and passed through a filter, is thickened in a warm place to the consistency of honey, and afterward hardens in the Sun; from this, a Tincture is extracted with *Spirit of Wine* <note>original: "Spiritu vini" — high-proof distilled alcohol.</note>.

2. *Opium* should first be purified in a liquid of *Hyssop* <note>An aromatic herb used here as a purifying solvent.</note>, or in distilled water, as is usually done with *Aloe*, and afterward it should also be extracted with *Spirit of Wine*.

3. The juice of *Henbane* and the *opium* (before being mixed with the rest) should first cast off their "sulfurs" and harmful poisons during digestion (this material rises to the surface like foam). It is from these impurities that such various and disastrous symptoms arise in those sick patients who use *Opium* and *Henbane* that has not been properly purified. Because very few people have noticed this until now, I did not want to hide this fact from the *Chemical Republic* <note>original: "Rempubl. Chymicam" — the international community of alchemists and scholars.</note> here as well.

4. Those things requiring extraction should be extracted with rectified *Spirit of Wine*; the longer they are afterward digested together, the more powerful the medicine's operation will be.

5. For women and those suffering from hysteria, because of the "suffocation of the womb" <note>original: "suffocationem matricis" — a historical medical belief that the uterus could move within the body, causing respiratory distress or anxiety.</note>, *Ambergris* <note>original: "Ambra"</note> and *Musk* <note>original: "Moschus"</note> should be omitted from the recipe; or, to suppress the scent, a few grains of *Castoreum* <note>original: "Castorei" — a pungent substance from beavers used to treat nervous conditions.</note> should be added instead.

<header>B A S I L I C A</header>

# OBSERVATIONS on the prepara-
## *tion of Laudanum.*

---

<margin>
For then the greatest power of the spirit, or the *First Being* <note>original: "primum Ens" — in Paracelsian alchemy, the "First Being" refers to the fundamental, primordial essence of a substance before it is altered by nature or art.</note> of the plant, is still concentrated in the root.
</margin>

1. The younger, fresh, succulent outer roots and barks of *Henbane* <note>original: "Hyoscyami."</note> (discarding the internal woody trunk) are to be collected when the Sun and Moon are positioned in either Aries or Libra before the full moon; others collect them, if it can be done, at the very hour when the Moon is renewed in the said Signs. The pressed-out juice, having been skimmed and passed through a filter, is thickened in a warm place to the consistency of honey, and afterwards it hardens in the Sun; from this, a Tincture is extracted using *Spirit of Wine* <note>original: "Spiritu vini" — high-proof alcohol or brandy used as a solvent.</note>.

2. The *Opium* should first be purified in a liquor of Hyssop, or in distilled water, as is usually done with Aloe; afterwards, it should also be extracted with *Spirit of Wine*.

3. The juice of Henbane and the opium (before they are mixed with the remaining ingredients) should first cast off their "sulphurs" <note>In this context, "sulphurs" refers to the volatile, oily, or impure components thought to carry the plant's toxicity.</note> and harmful poisons through *digestion* <note>A process of slow heating to encourage chemical change.</note> (which seeks the surface like foam); for it is from these that such varied and disastrous symptoms arise in those sick people who use Opium and Henbane that has not been properly purified. Because this has been noticed by very few until now, I did not wish to hide it from the *Chemical Republic* <note>original: "Rempubl. Chymicam" — the international community of alchemists, physicians, and chemists.</note> here.

4. The substances to be extracted should be extracted with rectified *Spirit of Wine*; the longer they are afterwards digested together, the more powerful the operation will be.

5. For women and those suffering from *hysteria* <note>original: "hystericis."</note>, on account of *suffocation of the womb* <note>original: "suffocationem matricis" — a historical medical condition where the uterus was believed to move within the body, causing respiratory distress; strong perfumes were thought to aggravate or treat it.</note>, the Ambergris and Musk should be omitted from the composition; or, to suppress the odor, a few grains of *Castoreum* <note>A yellowish secretion from the scent glands of the North American or European beaver, used as a medicinal sedative.</note> should be added.

This can finally be fermented in a very slow digestion of ashes in a *blind alembic* <note>original: "alembiaco cæco" — a distillation vessel without a spout, where the vapors are forced to circulate and fall back into the base, intensifying the mixture.</note> for a month, for the sake of greater efficacy and operation.

<header>B A S I L I C A</header>

[This remedy surpasses the preparations of] Nicholas, the Thrice-Delicate <note>original: Triphera — a category of ancient electuaries</note>, Theriac, the Mithridatium of Andromachus, Lozenges of Winter Cherry <note>original: Alkekengi</note>, Pills of Hound's-tongue <note>original: Cynoglossa</note>, and so on.

This specific anodyne <note>pain-relieving medicine</note> is <term>a bulwark against all the pains of ailments</term> <note>original Greek: ἔρυμα πρὸς πάσας παθῶν ὀδυνάς</note>. It is the final refuge.

1. In all acute pains, whether cold or hot, external as well as internal, where men are almost exhausted by the intensity [of the suffering]; especially in **Colic** pain taken with *Mint water* (provided the bowels are free and open), in **Kidney pain** <note>original: Nephritico</note>, **Pleurisy**, and **Gout** <note>original: Arthritico</note>.

2. In halting all "down-flows" <note>original: defluxionibus — the movement of harmful humors</note> of every humor and thin Catarrhs, especially at the beginning. 
Likewise in all flows of the Intestines, whether by reason of "sinning" and biting humors <note>referring to corrosive or imbalanced bodily fluids</note>, or by reason of [excessive] purging humors; it is then given with *Mastic* <note>a resin from the pistachio tree</note> and *Sealed Earth* <note>original: Terra sigillata — a medicinal clay</note>.

3. In excessive sleeplessness and restlessness, both internal and external. If you wish to apply it externally, then take 4 or 6 grains with three drops of *Oil of Nutmeg*, or with a very small amount of pressed oil, and make a linen plug <note>original: turunda</note>. By placing this in the nostrils, it wonderfully induces sleep; once they are sleeping deeply, the plug can be removed. In this way, even a desperate nosebleed <note>original: Hemorrhagia Narium</note> was cured: by forming two pills from 16 grains and blocking each nostril with one pill.

4. In every kind of Fever, taken with *Wormwood water* <note>original: aqua Absinthij</note> and *Rue water* (which are specific **fever-fighters** <note>original: Febrifugæ</note>). If the heat lasts a long time, the dose should be repeated after the fourth hour. In the most burning Fevers, it extinguishes thirst and brings sleep, especially when Fevers cause a sleep that is mixed with labored wakefulness.

5. Those suffering from Asthma and Consumption <note>original: Phthisici</note>, if they use it in *Hyssop water*, can be supported by it for a long time. In cases of Coughing, caution is needed so that it is not administered when the patient's strength is very weak or when there is a great abundance of waste matter <note>original: recrementorum — phlegm or secretions</note>.

[...and the medicine] is contained in the Chest: For although it soothes a **Cough** and brings on sleep, it increases the tightness of the Chest. Therefore, it is better always to give less of it during a Cough, and furthermore to mix it with thinning and cleansing agents, such as **Oxymel** <note>a medicinal syrup of honey and vinegar</note> or what is made from **Horehound** <note>original: Marrubio — a bitter herb used for respiratory issues</note>. ### *Dosage.*

From 2 to 3 or 4 grains. If the bowels are free <note>meaning the patient is not constipated</note>, then it works effectively. It is also offered in specific and appropriate medicinal waters and is remixed into them according to the 7 members <note>referring to the seven principal organs of the body</note> and diseases. If the disease is severe, one pill can be given around nightfall, long after dinner.

## VIII.

# FRAGRANT REMEDIES.

Human Nature is assisted by scents, and the spirits <note>the "vital spirits" or subtle fluids believed to carry life and sensation through the body</note> are aided by them. Therefore Philagrius <note>an ancient Greek physician</note>, according to Aëtius <note>Aëtius of Amida, a 6th-century medical writer</note>, says quite skillfully: Nature gladly embraces pleasant odors, and being refreshed and as if reviving from them, she calls back her strength which had been suppressed by the ferocity of disease. For a scent drawn in through the nostrils is pulled toward the heart and the brain; it awakens the compressed and suffocated spirit, and holds back that which is breathing its last and fleeing. Indeed, there are even hot regions where Pliny <note>Pliny the Elder, Roman naturalist</note> suggests the Mouthless People <note>original: Astomos — a legendary race described by Pliny as having no mouths and surviving solely by smelling fruits and flowers</note> live on scents alone.

In terms of health, the air is of the greatest importance; for one who falls ill from a foul stench is cured with difficulty, because an unpleasant odor permeates all parts of the body along with the spirit, especially the brain and the chest. By the scent of the Elixir of Life <note>original: Elixiris vitæ</note> composed of various aromatics, Giambattista della Porta <note>an influential Italian scholar and polymath</note> says that through multiple experiences, he has held back the exhaling soul of many who were near death. In many diseases, therefore, the spirits of life must be rectified and corrected. For the principal organs and the vital spirits (both of which are the first of all to be troubled and infected by any poison) are wonderfully refreshed by fragrant things, and the poisonous...

<meta>The text cuts off here at the catchword "nati," which completes the word "venenati" (poisonous) on the following page.</meta>

# SPECIFIC MEDICINE
## FOR THE HEAD.

Paracelsus attributes many virtues to the volatility of the **Spirit of Vitriol** <note>original: "spiritus Vitrioli"; a powerful acid distilled from mineral sulfates, used extensively in alchemical medicine</note> in curing **Epilepsy** <note>often referred to as the "falling sickness" in early modern texts</note>. I have found the following Spirit to be most effective in medical use.

### SPIRIT OF VITRIOL.

℞ Take **Hungarian Vitriol** <note>a mineral sulfate, usually of copper or iron</note>, or Cyprian, or Roman—it is all the same (though Huferus always highly valued that found in Silesia in the mines **at the Zigmantell** <note>original: "auff dem Zigmantell"; refers to a specific mining district near Zuckmantel, modern Zlaté Hory</note>, for it is produced from the ore of gold, silver, iron, and **copper** <note>original: "Veneris"; Venus is the alchemical name for copper</note>). Dissolve it in distilled water or **May dew** <note>moisture collected from plants in early morning during May, believed by alchemists to contain special "vital spirits" from the air</note>, and strain the solution. After this, let it be placed to **digest** <note>a process of slow heating to encourage chemical change</note> in the heat of ashes, sand, or dung, in a distilling vessel <note>original: "alembico"</note> that is only loosely sealed, because nothing evaporates. Let it stand for a month. Then, it will cast off dregs to the surface which must be separated. Let it be placed in digestion again until it no longer casts off any dregs. Afterwards, let the clear liquid be strained and distilled over a slow fire of a water bath or sand bath. In the space of two or three hours, a **phlegm** <note>a watery, inactive byproduct of distillation</note> comes out, which must be removed. ## OIL OF AMBER <note>original: "OLEUM SUCCINI"</note>

In preparing this, no ordinary diligence is required, for it demands a suitable and proper fire. We use **White Amber** <note>Succinite, a fossilized resin</note>—formed from the purest and unmixed **bitumen** <note>The author follows the ancient belief that amber was a form of solidified petroleum or "sea-pitch" generated in the ocean.</note> generated in the sea—for medicine, not the yellow variety.

<term>℞: Take</term> therefore fragments of white amber (for example, two or three pounds) and pound them into a coarse state; do not grind them into a fine powder. If necessary, first wash away any impurities with common water. Place the amber in a **cucurbit** <term>cucurbit: the gourd-shaped lower part of a distilling apparatus</term> or an **alembic** <term>alembic: a distilling vessel</term> that is not too tall. Pour in a good quantity of **Rose water** and **Betony water** (this is done so that the oil is not burned, and so that it may begin to drip more easily by the medium of these waters). Fit a spacious **head** <note>original: "capitellum," the top part of the still</note> with a sufficiently wide spout, and attach a receiving vessel. Seal the joints of the glassware on both sides in the customary manner. The distillation should be carried out in a **sand bath** <note>original: "in arena"; a method of heating a vessel evenly by nesting it in hot sand</note>, maintaining a suitable and steady degree of fire so it does not cool down (otherwise, it turns black like pitch and breaks the glass). Also beware that the fire does not become too intense, otherwise the receiving vessel is endangered.

First, the water and a white oil emerge with spirits like clouds. Then, the visible spirit no longer emerges, but streaks appear in the head, as can be seen in the distillation of **Spirit of Wine** <note>Alcohol</note>. Finally, the yellow oil comes; at this point, the distillation must be stopped, or, having changed the receiving vessel, collect separately the reddish-black oil that will follow. Lastly, the **Salt** rises by **sublimation** <term>sublimation: a process where a solid substance is heated into a vapor and then condenses directly back into a solid on a cool surface, used to purify chemical salts.</term>.

<header>CHEMISTRY.</header>

The **dead head** <note>original: "Caput mortuum"; the useless chemical residue remaining after distillation</note> remains at the bottom, crumbly, black, and light. 

Before the **Oil of white Amber** is **rectified** <term>rectified: purified by repeated distillation</term>, let it first be well washed in common water, swirling it frequently; afterwards, let it be rectified slowly in a **water bath** <note>original: "B. M." or "Balneum Mariae"</note> through Rose or Marjoram water. After rectification, it can also be mixed several more times with new Rose or Marjoram water—always renewing the water after the oil has settled and separated from it. In this way, the stench is accustomed to vanish. <note>Distilled amber oil has a notoriously pungent, burnt smell that the author seeks to mask with aromatic floral waters.</note> 

From one pound of Amber, after rectification, scarcely three or four **loths** <note>original: "lotones"; a pre-metric unit of weight roughly equal to half an ounce</note> of true white oil can be obtained.

## SALT OF AMBER <note>original: "SAL SUCCINI"</note>

Collect the salt raised by the force of fire through **sublimation** <term>sublimation: the process where a solid turns into gas and back to solid, leaving impurities behind</term> and dissolve it in Marjoram water; filter the water and in a water bath gradually draw it off [by evaporation]. Dissolve, filter, and **coagulate** <term>coagulate: here, to solidify crystals out of a liquid</term> it again; let this be repeated several times. Then the most effective **DIURETIC SALT** is obtained, of which mention was made above.

### *Powers of the oil of amber.*

It can deservedly be called the most effective **European Balm** <note>original: "Opobalsamum Europæum"; an attempt to frame a local substance as being as potent as the rare and expensive "Balm of Mecca" from the East</note>, because by its own faculty it surpasses all other remedies in curing **Stroke** <note>original: "Apoplexia"</note> and **Epilepsy**: formerly it was called "Sacred," no doubt on account of its admirable and secret powers.

1. In **PLAGUE**, one drop is rubbed on the nostrils morning and evening; thus no poison can take effect. To one who has been seized [by the disease], a dose is given from one **scruple** <term>scruple: a small unit of weight, approx. 1.3 grams</term> to two in **Blessed Thistle** <note>original: "Cardui benedicti"</note> water.

2. It is vehemently beneficial to those who [suffer from] dangerous [diseases] of the head—

### *Virtues & Uses.*

1. It wonderfully assists those suffering from **Apoplexy** <note>original: "Apoplecticis"; a historical term for a stroke or sudden loss of consciousness</note>, **Epilepsy**, and **Vertigo**, if the edges of the nostrils, the temples, the crown of the head, and even the internal palate [the roof of the mouth] are anointed as necessity requires, by intervals during the night and day.

For prevention, let the edges of the nostrils and the crown of the head be anointed once or twice every week with a tiny amount, using the thumb to apply the balsam moderately.

2. Against **malignant and pestilential air** <note>original: "malignam & pestiferam auram"; referring to the "miasma" theory where diseases like the plague were thought to be spread by foul-smelling, poisonous air</note>.
3. It restores all **Animal and Vital spirits** <note>In early modern medicine, these were subtle substances believed to circulate through the body to facilitate movement, sensation, and life itself</note>.
4. A **secret remedy** <note>original: "Arcanum"</note> for **Colic** <note>severe abdominal pain</note>, if the navel is anointed with it.
5. It wonderfully assists with **ailments of the womb** <note>original: "Matricis"</note>, if the stomach and navel are anointed; also the private parts of a woman suffering from **suffocation** <note>original: "suffocationem"; likely referring to "suffocation of the mother," a condition where the womb was believed to move upward and cause breathing difficulties</note>, for then she is immediately restored. However, at that time, foul-smelling things should be applied to their nostrils, such as **Castoreum** <note>a secretion from the scent glands of beavers</note> or **Asafoetida** <note>a pungent resin from the Ferula plant, known for its strong, sulfuric odor</note>.

The use is for external application only: a tiny amount is applied to the edges of the nostrils as desired; that sweet scent will scarcely fade away for a day or two.

# PECTORAL REMEDY
## MILK OF SULPHUR

Take 1 part of yellow Sulphur, ground or sifted—or alternatively, Flowers of Sulphur <term>Flowers of Sulphur: Flores Sulphuris; a fine powder produced by sublimation</term>—and three parts of Salt of Tartar <term>Salt of Tartar: Salis Tartari; potassium carbonate, used here as an alkali to help dissolve the sulphur</term>. Place these in a wide-mouthed glass vessel, and having coated the glass with clay <note>original: "luto obducto"; a common practice to protect the glass from breaking in direct heat</note>, place it in a sand bath <note>original: "arenam"</note>. Pour in distilled rainwater to a height of 6 fingers. Let a fourth part of the glass remain empty, protruding out of the sand. Apply the fire gradually so that it boils. Let it be stirred diligently with a wooden spatula until almost all the Sulphur is dissolved during these boilings, which should happen within the space of 5 or 6 hours. At that time, the liquid will turn red, or at least moderately so, thickening like a lye. If the water vanishes during the boiling, let more hot water be poured in. Finally, when almost all the Sulphur is dissolved and the red liquid remains at a height of three transverse fingers, it is then filtered while still hot through blotting paper <note>original: "chartam Emporeticam"</note>. A little of the hot, filtered solution is placed in another glass, and immediately, while it is still warm, wine is poured in (there are some who...

And although many try to dissolve Gold as a metallic root—which they undeservedly exclude from the province of Animals and Vegetables—using common **Spirit of Salt** <term>Spiritum Salis: an early name for hydrochloric acid</term>, some by **Alcoholized Spirit of Wine** <term>Spiritum Vini Alcoolisatum: concentrated ethanol</term>, others by **Radical Vinegar** <term>Acetum radicatum: a highly concentrated acetic acid</term>, others first by corrosive salts and later by **Spirit of Turpentine** <term>Spiritum Terebinthinæ</term> or aromatic oils and similar delusions, Experience itself testifies that they all labor in vain. The **Water of Wisdom of the Philosophers** <note>original: *Aqua Sapientiæ Philosophorum*</note> is the only one which philosophically and naturally liberates all metals and stones from the impure bond of the **Quaternary Point of coagulation** <note>A reference to the four elements being "locked" together in a solid, impure state.</note>. Nor is there any other way under Heaven to physically dissolve the **Body of the Sun** <note>original: *Corpus Solis*; here meaning physical gold.</note> except through the **Universal Mercurial Solvent of the Philosophers** <term>Universale Menstruum Mercuriale Philosophorum: the legendary "Alkahest" or supreme solvent</term>, the most secret thing in all of Nature. While we lack this solvent through ignorance and the difficulty of acquiring it, men have become accustomed to satisfying their hunger with beef when partridges are lacking—just as a cook, in the absence of oak wood to cook food, uses beech or birch. Furthermore, Gold, in which there is a perfect balance of the Elements, is the Universal Subject for Animals, Vegetables, and Minerals, and the Life of all things. And just as it has a singular concordance with the Celestial Sun, so too does it possess a great affinity and harmony with the human body through its internal form. Just as—

For Gold is the purest of metals, within which dwells the splendor of the Sun and the ray of Celestial Fire, and in whose most perfect body the four Elements meet in harmony. The Ruby contains within itself the effects of all precious gems; in the same way, Gold (the most noble stone of all precious things) possesses the virtue of all "ductile stones"—that is, the metals—because it contains within itself every metal, and it tinges and brings them to life.

And just as the higher celestial planets receive their splendor and light from the Celestial Sun, in exactly the same and similar way do the "Terrestrial Planets"—or metallic bodies—receive their splendor, light, power, and rays from Gold, as if from a Philosophical and Terrestrial Sun. The nature of things can never be hidden from the one who possesses a perfect knowledge of it.
