### C H Y M I C A.
Dd 3

I will set forth my reasons here until more probable ones are brought forward by others. For just as **saltpeter** <note>original: *Sal nitrum*</note> and **sulfur** are enemies and cannot tolerate one another—as we see in the ignition of prepared **gunpowder** <note>original: *Pulveris Tormentarii*</note>—in the same way, **sal ammoniac** and **tartar** are opposed to each other. Therefore, when **sal ammoniac** is joined with its enemy, the **oil of tartar**, they cause the **gold** (which was previously dissolved in **aqua regia** <note>original: *Aqua Regis*; literally "Royal Water," a mixture of nitric and hydrochloric acids</note>) to fall out <note>This describes the process of precipitation, where a dissolved solid settles out of a liquid solution.</note> as a result of that mutual struggle. The **oil of tartar** strikes the highly purified **spirit of nitre** <note>Nitric acid.</note>, which in that conflict joins with its adversary, the **sulfur of the sun** <note>original: *Sulphur Solis*; In alchemy, Gold is associated with the Sun (Sol). The "sulfur" of a metal refers to its combustible or "soul" principle.</note>. And because that **sulfur of the sun** is highly purified by nature and far more subtle than our common combustible **sulfur**, it is therefore more powerful, and in a smaller quantity it effectively achieves its astounding operations—in exactly the same way that we observe common **sulfur** and **saltpeter** joined and ignited in **gunpowder** <note>original: *Pyrio Pulvere*</note> making a great noise and crash.

This **calx** <note>A fine powder or metallic ash.</note> liquefies in **oil of salt** <note>Hydrochloric acid.</note> just like butter; this occurs because of the remaining dry spirits of **saltpeter**. However, it is not a true and radical solution, because it can be reduced back into a [metallic] body.

This has been my experience thus far, which I also once communicated to our most august Emperor **RUDOLF** <note>Rudolf II (1552–1612), Holy Roman Emperor and a famous patron of alchemists like Tycho Brahe and Johannes Kepler.</note> at his request, along with certain other medical secrets.

Now follows the further process for **Potable Gold** <note>original: *Auri Potabilis*; "Drinkable Gold," a legendary alchemical life-extension medicine.</note>, which I freely and faithfully offer to students of chemistry (as I do the rest) as a unique gift received—though not without having tested it.

Take the **urine** of a healthy man who drinks wine, about 20 measures...

### C H Y M I C A.

The aforementioned spirit, before use, must first be rectified <note>Purified by repeated distillation.</note> several times over fresh fused Salt, so that it might be stronger; for on its own, it is too weak for this operation.

Afterward, take the previously mentioned **calx of Gold** <note>original: *calce Solis*; "Sun" is the alchemical symbol for Gold. "Calx" refers to the powder resulting from heating a metal.</note> and pour over it **Oil of Salt** <term>Hydrochloric acid</term>; and so that it may be better dissolved, draw off the Oil of Salt again until it reaches an oily consistency, and pour on fresh Oil of Salt once more, repeating this labor of **cohobation** <note>The process of repeatedly pouring a distillate back onto its residue and re-distilling it.</note> several times until the calx is well dissolved.

Then take 1 part of this solution and another part of the prepared **Spirit of Urine** <term>A solution of ammonia</term>; drop the Spirit of Urine in at least drop by drop, always blocking the opening of a large glass vessel until the noise <note>The effervescence or "stridor" caused by the chemical reaction between the acid and the ammonia.</note> ceases. Let it stand in **putrefaction** <note>A term for long-term digestion or fermentation in gentle heat.</note> in the gentle heat of a Water Bath for 4 weeks; afterward, let it be driven through a **retort** in a sand bath, observing the degrees of fire: first gentle, and finally stronger so that the retort glows red. Then the Gold for the most part ascends; carefully save this **sublimated powder**, for the Oil of Salt has come out by itself and should be set aside. Finally, take this sublimate of Gold, pour on **Spirit of Wine** <term>Ethanol or high-proof alcohol</term>, and it will be colored with a gentle hue. Pour on more Spirit after removing the first by decanting <note>original: *per inclinationem*; tilting the vessel to pour off liquid without disturbing the sediment.</note>, continuing until the fresh Spirit being poured on is no longer colored. This Spirit of Wine can be drawn off until an oily residue remains, or it can be kept as a tincture with the **Essence of Gold** for medical use.

The calx of Gold remaining in the retort should be dissolved again with Oil of Salt and **digested** with the Spirit of Urine as just described, repeating the labor until nothing of the Gold remains. If, however, the Spirit of Wine stays in digestion with the extracted Tincture of Gold for several weeks, then the whole becomes **Volatile Gold** and ascends through the **alembic**.

### *The Powers and Uses of this Oil of Vitriol.*

**Paracelsus** calls this the "fourth part of the pharmacy" and recommends it to every pharmacist such that it should be like a cornerstone in his workshop.

1. We use 6 to 8 drops in wine, or in water of **Spearmint** <note>original: *Mentæ crispæ*</note>, or better yet, in warm meat broth, for weak and "cold" stomachs because it promotes digestion.
2. For the **Stone and Sand** <note>original: *Calculo & Arena*; refers to kidney or bladder stones</note> in water of **Rest-harrow** <note>original: *Ononidis*; a plant traditionally used for urinary issues</note>.
3. For **Suffocation of the Womb** <term>Suffocatione matricis: a historical medical diagnosis (related to "hysteria") where physical symptoms were blamed on the movement or "strangulation" of the uterus</term> in water of **Mugwort** <note>original: *Artemisiæ*</note>.
4. For fevers of the stomach, heat, and thirst: 12 or 15 drops.

### Dosage.

The method of administration is a change of flavor toward the acidic. It is given in Sorrel water or other specific drinks, adding as many drops as will not set the teeth on edge <note>original: *dentes stupidos*; literally "stupid teeth," a phrase describing the sensitive, "fuzzy" feeling in teeth after exposure to strong acid</note>, yet still providing a clear acidity to the taste. It should never be used by itself, but always with a vehicle <note>a liquid medium used to carry a medicine</note>, and used sparingly. ## FLOWERS OF SULFUR.

The fire must be increased gradually with large coals, so that finally the pan in which the sand sits glows red. If the fire is continuous, so that the **Sulfur** flows as it were in the Alembic, then it is sublimated more quickly; yet let it not be excessive, otherwise it would ascend not with a yellow color, but black.

The Flowers raised into the Alembic should be removed quickly, specifically by always holding a round and square piece of paper underneath, lest by lifting the cap the Flowers fall into the sand. Meanwhile, if the **Cucurbit** <term>Cucurbit: the gourd-shaped flask or "bottom" of the still where the raw material is placed</term> is then extremely hot, its opening should be covered without delay, lest the Sulfur be ignited by the entering air—as often tends to happen—and the Alembic should be replaced and the fire continued for ten hours.

After the **sublimation** <note>the process of turning a solid into vapor and then back to a solid to purify it</note> is finished, let everything be cooled; once the Alembic is removed, the Flowers should be collected and mixed with the previous ones. The **dead head** <term>Caput mortuum: literally "dead head"; the useless residue or dross remaining at the bottom of a vessel after all the volatile or "spirituous" parts have been driven off</term> in each sublimation becomes porous and brittle; when sprinkled on coals, it should no longer burn. This is indeed the sign of the loss of all its goodness.

Mix these Flowers again with new Salt and **Vitriol** <term>Vitriol: a group of sulfate minerals used here as a chemical agent to aid in the refinement of the sulfur</term>, observing the previous proportion, and proceed exactly as you did the first time, which

### *The Powers, Uses, and Dosage of Flowers of Sulfur.*

1. Against the plague, it is a supreme curative and preventative; for they <note>referring to the sulfur "flowers"</note> resist the impression of the disease and protect against putrefaction. When taken with Extract of **Elecampane** <note>original: *Enulæ Campanæ*; a root used since antiquity for respiratory and digestive health</note>, they work miraculously in times of infection.
The dose is one drachm in **Holy Thistle** <note>original: *Cardui benedicti*; a plant once considered a "cure-all" for the plague</note> water, or in **Theriac** <term>Theriac: an ancient, complex medical concoction of many ingredients used as a universal antidote</term>. This draught serves as a **multipurpose remedy** <note>original: *πολύχρηστον* (polychreston); a Greek term for a medicine with many uses</note> which prevents and cures—without any other medicine—the Plague, Pleurisy, all manner of Putrefactions, and **Abscesses** <note>original: *Apostemata*</note>.
2. Daily use is a **preventative** <note>original: *προφυλακτικὸν* (prophylacticon)</note> against all diseases and their symptoms, preserving both one's Nature and health.
3. It is offered in all diseases that require effective drying out <note>original: *exiccatione*; a common goal in early modern medicine to balance "moist" humors</note>.
4. They promote sweating in the **Venereal Pox** <note>original: *Lue Venerea*; an early term for syphilis</note>.
5. In all ailments of the lungs, asthma, and both old and recent coughs; also in phlegmatic catarrhs of the chest.
6. In **Pleurisy** <note>an inflammation of the membranes surrounding the lungs</note>.
7. In **Colic**.
8. In abscesses and putrefactions of the body.
9. As a preventative in all fevers: for they safely and suddenly remove all impurities from fevers and milder cases of **lung inflammation** <note>original: *peripneumonicas*</note>.
10. It is also a preventative in **epilepsy**.

### A Mass for the Shaping of Amulets or Constellated Pentacles.

# REMEDIES FOR GOUT.

Incipient and mild Gout <note>original: "Podagra"; a form of inflammatory arthritis characterized by recurrent attacks of a red, tender, hot, and swollen joint.</note>, according to Severinus <note>Petrus Severinus (1542–1602) was a Danish physician and an influential follower of Paracelsus.</note>, is cured by a single ointment or balsam that allows for a mixture of Resolvents <note>substances used to dissolve or "resolve" morbid humors</note>, Mitigants <note>pain relievers</note>, and Corroborants <note>strengthening agents</note>.

Confirmed Gout—which has established roots that are difficult to dissolve, whether in the blood, the flesh, or in the synovial fluid <note>original: "Synovia"; the lubricating fluid found in the cavities of synovial joints.</note> itself—cannot be cured solely by external resolvent, mitigating, and corroborating balsams. Therefore, Gouty Purgations must be added, and Cleansings, Diaphoretics <note>medicines that induce sweating</note>, and Diuretics <note>medicines that promote the production of urine</note> must be established through sweats, insensible perspiration, the consumption of fluids, and complete removals of the offending matter. Let us, however, call upon Gouty evacuants that are suitable and agreeable to the body.

Paracelsus states that three things are required for the cure of Gout: Resolvents, Mitigants, and Corroborants.

Among the Resolvents, Paracelsus recommends the Coral Secret <note>original: "Arcanum Corallinum"; likely a preparation of red coral or a mercurial compound with a coral color used in alchemy.</note>: Likewise, the following Arthritic Powder <note>original: "Pulverem Artheticum"; a powder intended to treat joint pain or arthritis.</note>:

> ℞ <note>Recipe</note> Hermodactyl <note>The root of a plant, likely Meadow Saffron, historically used for joint pain.</note>
> Best Turpeth <note>A medicinal root from the East Indies used as a purgative.</note>
> Diagridium <note>A preparation of scammony resin used as a potent laxative.</note>
> Senna leaves
> Shavings of a human skull <note>original: "Rasuræ Cranii"; a common, albeit macabre, ingredient in early modern medicine believed to contain "vital spirits."</note>
> Sugar: one dram each. Mix and let a fine powder be made.

The dose is half a dram in the morning, taken with Ground-pine water <note>original: "aqua Ivæ Artheticę"; *Ajuga chamaepitys*, commonly used for gout and known as "ground-pine."</note> for 3 or 4 days. It safely and gently purges all Gouty discharges <note>original: "defluxiones"; the flowing of morbid humors to a specific part of the body.</note>.
In place of Mitigants, the two following balsams may be used.

# REMEDIES FOR GOUT

Early and mild **gout** <note>Latin: *podagra*, specifically referring to gout of the foot.</note>, according to <note>Petrus Severinus (1542–1602) was a Danish physician and a major proponent of Paracelsian "chemical" medicine.</note> Severinus, is cured with a single ointment or balsam. It allows for a mixture of **Resolvents** (to dissolve blockages), **Mitigators** (to soothe pain), and **Strengtheners** (to fortify the body).

Established gout, which has set down roots that are difficult to dissolve—whether in the blood, the flesh, or in the <term>synovial fluid</term> <note>The lubricating fluid found in the joints.</note> itself—cannot be cured by external balsams alone. Therefore, gout-specific purgations must be added. Cleansing treatments, <term>diaphoretics</term> (to induce sweating), and <term>diuretics</term> (to increase urination) should be established to remove the illness through sweating, invisible perspiration, and complete elimination. We must call for gout-cleansing agents that are appropriate for the task.

<note>Paracelsus (c. 1493–1541) was a Swiss physician and alchemist who believed that diseases were caused by chemical imbalances and should be treated with mineral remedies.</note> Paracelsus says that three things are required for the treatment of gout: **Resolvents**, **Mitigators**, and **Strengtheners**.

Among the Resolvents, Paracelsus recommends the **Coral Secret** <note>Latin: *Arcanum Corallinum*. This was a high-level chemical remedy, typically a red mercurial preparation named for its coral color.</note>. He also recommends the following **Arthritic Powder**:

## GOUT BALSAM I

| Ingredient | Amount |
| :--- | :--- |
| **Vitriol**, calcined until yellow <note>Vitriol (metal sulfates) was heated (calcined) to remove moisture and change its chemical properties.</note> | 2 pounds |
| **Virgin honey** with the comb | 1 pound |
| **Spirit of wine** <note>Alcohol/Ethanol. The text notes that if you use the spirit left over from making **Opiate Laudanum**, it is even better.</note> | 1 pound |

| **Vervain** | 6 ounces |
| **Rosemary** | 6 ounces |

Let all the ingredients be ground and mixed together, and placed in a glass **alembic** <note>A chemical vessel used for distillation, consisting of a boiling flask and a cooling cap.</note> of appropriate size, well-covered with **lute** <note>A clay or paste used to seal the joints of chemical apparatus to prevent the escape of vapors.</note>. Attach a sufficiently large **head** <note>original: "capitello"; the upper part of the still where vapors collect.</note> with a capacious receiver, ensuring the joints are well-sealed with lute. Let them be placed for three days in the slow heat of a **sand bath** <note>original: "arenæ calore"; a method of even heating where the vessel is nestled in warm sand.</note> to **digest** <note>A process of slow, gentle heating to extract active principles.</note>. 

Afterward, let them be distilled little by little; finally, let the fire be strengthened as long as you see drops or "spirits" emerging. Then, let it cool. The **caput mortuum** <note>Literally "dead head"; the solid, useless residue remaining in the flask after distillation.</note> or spongy black dregs should be **reverberated** <note>Heated intensely in a furnace so the flames "echo" or reflect onto the substance.</note> until they turn white. Pour the previously distilled liquid back onto these white ashes and distill a second time.

This Balsam is most effective. It frustrates no one’s expectations if it is properly prepared and applied; for it quickly and suddenly calms **Gouty pain**, if the affected area is anoint- <note>The text cuts off here at the catchword "unga-", likely continuing with "ungatur" (is anointed).</note>

# THE KIDNEY REMEDY <note>original: "NEPHRITICUM"</note>

There are various types of **stone** <note>original: "Calculi"; referring to kidney or bladder stones, a common and painful ailment in the 17th century.</note>, differing in degrees and in the number of their parts. All are produced from the more impure, refined portion of nourishment destined for coagulation; after the separation of the more benign nourishment has occurred, they are brought to completion by the benefit of the spirit or heat of the surrounding parts. They are adorned with various shapes according to the variety of the material from which they come, and the diversity of the parts in which they stick.

<margin>If the expulsive force is weak, then the coagulative power of Salt creates Tartar.</margin>
A strong digestion results in a swift operation regarding the **Stone** <note>original: "Calculum"; refers to kidney or bladder stones.</note>. No weak digestion ever produced a stone: unless, by a weak digestion, it is expelled by a strong expulsive force and not separated, it is impossible for a human to be found without **Tartar** <note>original: "Tartaro"; in Paracelsian medicine, this refers to stony precipitates formed in the body from food and drink, named after the crust found in wine barrels.</note>, which the **Spirit of Salt** <note>Hydrochloric acid, or more generally, the acidic principle of salts.</note> usually coagulates, and which Purgations do not remove.

### SALT AGAINST THE STONE.

Paracelsus says that regarding the **Stone**, nothing is achieved by the length <note>The complexity or duration</note> of remedies, but rather in their true preparation.

℞ <note>Take</note> therefore:
**Crab’s Eyes** <note>original: "Oculorum Cancri"; these are not actual eyes but calcium carbonate stones found in the stomachs of crayfish, used as antacids.</note>
**Stones of the Microcosm** <note>original: "Calculi microcosmi"; stones taken from the human body, specifically bladder or kidney stones.</note>

# ON DYSENTERY:

If digestion is good, but there is no separation <note>The author refers to the body's ability to separate nutrients from waste.</note>, then **Dysentery** <note>original: *Dysenteria*; an inflammatory disorder of the lower intestinal tract.</note> is present.

If there is separation, but no digestion, then it is **Lientery** <note>original: *Lienteria*; a form of diarrhea where food passes through the body in an undigested state.</note>.

If there is neither separation nor digestion, then it is **Diarrhea**.

If there is a putrefaction of the matter in the stomach, then it is a **Flux of the belly** <note>original: *Fluxus ventris*; a general term for severe or chronic discharge from the bowels.</note> with various colors.

## ESSENCE OF SATYRION.

<note>Satyrion refers to various species of orchids, which were famously used in early modern medicine as aphrodisiacs and treatments for reproductive health due to their testicle-shaped roots.</note>

Just as **Rhubarb** <note>original: *Rhabarbarum*</note> loses its purging power through even a short boiling, so too does **Satyrion** through drying. For although the dry root may be extracted with **Spirit of Wine** <note>original: *Spiritu vini*; a high-proof alcohol or ethanol.</note>, no effective operation is observed from its use. Experience demonstrates that water distilled from the green <note>meaning fresh or succulent</note> root accomplishes more than the powder of the dried root. Therefore, its virtue should be drawn out through separation from the root while it is still imbued with its own moisture, according to the following method.

<margin>Bread and Wine are the primary pillars of sustenance and singular means of procreation, for without **Ceres** <note>The goddess of grain; here meaning bread.</note> and **Bacchus** <note>The god of wine.</note>, **Venus** <note>The goddess of love; here meaning sexual desire.</note> grows cold. Zachariah chapter 9, section 17.</margin>

℞ <note>Take</note> In early Spring, take selected juicy and full roots of all species of **Dog-orchis** <note>original: *Cynosorchidum*; a specific variety of orchid.</note> as desired, and crush them in a marble mortar. **Note:** One of the two <term>testicles</term> <note>The orchid bulbs were often called "testicles" due to their shape. Following the "Doctrine of Signatures," physicians believed the shape of a plant indicated the organ it could treat.</note> is always flabby, soft, and wrinkled; this must be cast away because it possesses a contrary power (which **Paracelsus** <note>A famous 16th-century Swiss physician and alchemist.</note> calls **Saturnine** <note>In alchemy, "Saturnine" qualities are cold, leaden, and suppressive, the opposite of the "hot" and vital qualities of Venus.</note>) that represses and extinguishes **Venus**. Add a crumb or two of the freshest, whitest wheat bread; let everything be mixed diligently in a stone mortar. To dilute the stickiness, pour in a sufficient quantity of **Malmsey Spirit of Wine** <note>original: *Spiritus vini Malviatici*; a spirit distilled from Malvasia, a sweet Greek wine.</note>. Afterward, place it in a <term>blind alembic</term> <note>original: *Alembico caeco*; a distillation vessel without a spout, used for "circulating" or "digesting" a substance so that the vapors return to the liquid without escaping.</note> in the very slow heat of a **Water-bath** <note>original: *Balnei*; a bain-marie.</note>. 

When one or two months of this digestion have finished, squeeze out the thick juice with a press. (Burn the dregs to ash and extract the white **Salt**, which will have a sweet flavor and not be urine-like, as other vegetable salts are.) Place the strained juice back into the blind alembic for another two months of digestion. Then, a very yellow liquid (sometimes even red) will separate itself onto the surface, leaving behind the impure dregs to be set aside, which reside at the bottom in the form of a <term>hypostasis</term> <note>A sediment or deposit found at the bottom of a liquid.</note> or dregs.

For those suffering from spleen ailments, it is given in water of **Spleenwort** <note>original: *Asplenii*</note>, **Maidenhair fern** <note>original: *Adianti*</note>, or **Tamarisk** <note>original: *Tamarísci*</note>. In affections of the **Liver** <note>original: *Hepatis*</note>, it is administered in water of **Endive** <note>original: *Intybi*</note>, **Chicory** <note>original: *Cichor.*</note>, or **Agrimony** <note>original: *Agrimon.*</note>; in such cases, it stops the spitting of blood.

## ESSENCE OF SATYRION.
<note>Satyrion refers to various species of orchids, particularly those of the genus *Orchis*. Historically, these were used as aphrodisiacs because their paired tubers resemble testicles.</note>

Just as **Rhubarb** <note>original: *Rhabarbarū*</note> loses its purgative power with a little boiling, so also does **Satyrion** by drying. For although the dry root may be extracted with **Spirit of Wine** <note>original: *Spiritu vini*; high-proof alcohol or brandy</note>, no effective action is observed from its use. Experience demonstrates that **Water distilled from the green root** works more effectively than the **Powder of the dry root**. Therefore, let the virtue be drawn out from the root while it is still imbued with its own moisture through separation, which is done according to this method.

<margin>Bread and Wine are the primary pillars of sustenance and singular means of procreation, because without **Ceres** <note>The goddess of grain/bread</note> and **Bacchus** <note>The god of wine</note>, **Venus** <note>The goddess of love and desire</note> grows cold. **Zechariah** chapter 9, Section 17. <note>A reference to the biblical verse "Grain shall make the young men flourish, and new wine the young women."</note></margin>

Take, in early Spring, selected succulent and full roots of all species of **Dog's Orchis** <note>original: *Cynosorchidum*; a common type of wild orchid</note> as much as you like; crush them in a marble mortar. Note: one of the two "testicles" <note>The orchid’s tubers often grow in pairs; one is firm and new, the other is older and shriveled.</note> is always flaccid, soft, and wrinkled; this must be thrown away because it possesses a contrary virtue (which **Paracelsus** <note>A famous 16th-century physician and alchemist who pioneered the use of minerals and chemicals in medicine.</note> calls **Saturnine** <note>In alchemy, Saturn is associated with coldness, restriction, and dampening of spirits.</note>) that represses and extinguishes **Venus** <note>Sexual desire or fertility</note>. Add a crumb or two of fresh, very white **fine wheat bread** <note>original: *panis similacei*</note>; let all be mixed carefully in a stone mortar, and to dilute the stickiness, pour on a sufficient quantity of **Spirit of Malmsey Wine** <note>original: *Spiritus vini Malviatici*; a sweet, potent Greek wine highly prized for extractions.</note>. 

Afterward, place it in a **Blind Alembic** <note>original: *Alembico cæco*; a distillation vessel without a spout, used for "circulating" a substance so that vapors condense and fall back into the liquid, ensuring a long, closed digestion.</note> for a very slow digestion in a **Water Bath** <note>original: *Balnei*; a Bain-marie</note>. When one or two months of this digestion are finished, express the tenacious juice through a press. (At this stage, burn the remaining dregs to ash to extract a white **Salt**, which should have a sweet taste and not a urine-like flavor like other vegetable salts). Put the strained liquid back into the Blind Alembic for another two months of digestion; then a very yellow liquor (sometimes even red) separates itself on the surface, while the impure dregs remain at the bottom to be set aside, which reside at the base in the form of a **sediment** <note>original: *hypostasis*</note>.

It emphasizes using fresh roots rather than dried ones and includes a specific instruction to discard the "Saturnine" withered tubers that supposedly suppress sexual desire.</summary>

<header>C H Y M I C A.</header>

# THE ESSENCE OF SATYRION.
<note>original: *Essentia Satyrionis*; Satyrion is a historical name for various species of orchids, long associated with fertility and the mythological satyrs due to the shape of their twin tubers.</note>

Just as <term>Rhubarb</term> <note>original: *Rhabarbarũ*; used here as a comparison for how heat affects medicinal potency</note> loses its purging power with only a little boiling, so too does **Satyrion** through drying. For although the dry root may be extracted with **spirit of wine**, no effective operation is found from its use. Experience demonstrates that a **water** distilled from the green, fresh root works more effectively than the powder of the dried root. Therefore, the "virtue" or medicinal power should be drawn out by separation from the root while it is still imbued with its own moisture, which is done according to this method:

<margin>Bread and Wine are the chief pillars of sustenance and the aids of procreation, because "without Ceres and Bacchus, Venus freezes." <note>A common Latin proverb meaning that without food and drink, desire grows cold. The author cites Zechariah chapter 9, section 17.</note></margin>
Take, in the early spring, select succulent and full roots of all species of **Dog-orchids** <note>original: *Cynosorchidum*</note> as much as you please, and crush them in a marble mortar. **Note:** one of the two "testicles" <note>The twin tubers of the orchid.</note> is always flaccid, soft, and wrinkled; this must be cast away because it possesses a contrary power (which **Paracelsus** <note>The famous 16th-century Swiss-German physician and alchemist.</note> calls "Saturnine") that suppresses and extinguishes **Venus** <note>In this context, Venus refers to sexual desire and reproductive health.</note>. Add a crumb or two of fresh, very white wheat bread; let everything be mixed diligently in a stone mortar, and to dilute the stickiness, pour on a sufficient quantity of **Malmsey spirit of wine** <note>original: *Spiritus vini Malviatici*; a high-quality spirit distilled from sweet Malvasia wine.</note>. Afterward, place it in a **blind alembic** <note>original: *Alembico cæco*; a distilling vessel without a spout, used to circulate vapors back into the liquid.</note> for a very slow digestion in a <term>Water Bath</term> <note>original: *Balnei*; a gentle heating method using hot water, also known as a Bain-marie.</note>. When a month or two of this digestion has passed, press out the thick juice through a press (calcine the dregs and extract a white **Salt**, sweet in taste and not smelling of urine like other vegetable salts). Place the strained juice back into the **blind alembic** for another two months of digestion. Then, a very yellow liquor (sometimes even red) separates itself on the surface, leaving the impure dregs to be set aside, which reside at the bottom in the form of a **sediment** <note>original: *hypostasis*</note>.

<summary>This page describes the alchemical preparation of the Essence of Satyrion (Orchid), emphasizing the use of fresh roots and the removal of the "Saturnine" tuber to preserve its aphrodisiac and restorative qualities. The process involves long digestion in a water bath using spirits and wheat bread to extract the essential medicinal oils.</summary>

<header>THE ROYAL PHARMACY</header>
<meta>catchword: VENE- (referring to Venus/Vitality)</meta>

The liquid, separated by decanting, should be kept for use. To this, you shall add its own **Salt** <note>The "proper salt" refers to the mineral salts extracted from the ashes of the plant's remains after burning (calcination), a standard alchemical practice to reunite the plant's "body" with its "spirit."</note>, as well as some **Salt of Pearls**, and also a drop or two of the oils of **Cinnamon**, **Mace**, and **Nutmeg**; in this way, the medicine will be more pleasant and effective. **Potable Gold** <note>original: *Aurum Potabile*; a legendary alchemical tonic made of liquid gold.</note> could also be added, provided that a true, genuine version can be obtained—one not defiled or corrupted by corrosive substances <note>Alchemists often used harsh acids like *aqua regia* to dissolve gold; if not properly neutralized, these "potable golds" were poisonous.</note>.

### Powers, Uses, and Dosage

A marvelous **signature** <note>The "Doctrine of Signatures" was the belief that a plant's physical appearance revealed its medicinal use. Because orchid tubers resemble testicles, they were used to treat the reproductive system.</note> of nearly all the external members of the whole body—of both sexes—is found in these roots of various species. Therefore, they are rightly believed to strengthen the entire human being. **Phaedro** <note>Georg Phaedro, a 16th-century Paracelsian physician.</note> calls this root the **"Red Mummy"** <note>original: *Mumiam rubram*; in alchemy, "mummy" refers to a vital, life-preserving force or substance extracted from a living thing.</note> and says it possesses a singular **sympathy** <note>original: *συμπάθειαν* (sympatheian); a Greek term meaning a natural resonance or connection.</note> with the **microcosm** <note>The human body, viewed as a miniature version of the entire universe.</note>.

This Extract, therefore, is one of the highest **restoratives** <note>original: *Confortativis*; medicines intended to "comfort" or strengthen the vital organs.</note> for the whole body. It is a most excellent medicine for strengthening **Venus** <note>The Roman goddess of love, here used as a euphemism for sexual health and reproductive vigor.</note>, and it is given with great benefit to those who are "cold" <note>Lacking in "vital heat" or libido.</note> or **bewitched** <note>original: *maleficiatis*; people believed to be suffering from "maleficia" or sorcery intended to cause impotence.</note>. Likewise, it powerfully restores lost virility to old men with weak loins.

The **Dose** is from one **scruple** <note>A scruple is an old apothecary weight, roughly 1.3 grams.</note> to two or three scruples, taken in sweet **Muscatel** or **Malmsey** wine when going to bed. Alternatively, it may be mixed with **Conserve of Roses**, of which a quantity the size of a hazelnut should be administered, followed by a draught of Malmsey or Muscatel wine.

# THE VENOMOUS
## THERIAC OF MUMMY
<note>Theriac was a famous "universal" medicine and antidote used since antiquity. This version uses "Mummy," a potent but controversial ingredient in Paracelsian medicine.</note>

It is Mummy alone that offers the most immediate remedy against all types of poisons.

->First, let the Tincture of Mummy be prepared in this manner:<-

Choose the corpse of a red-haired man <note>original: *ruffi*; red-haired individuals were often favored in alchemical recipes as they were thought to possess a higher concentration of "vital spirits."</note>, whole, fresh, and without blemish, approximately twenty-four years of age, who has died by hanging, being broken on the wheel, or pierced by a spear. The body should be collected during clear weather, whether by day or night.

Once this Mummy has been illuminated and influenced by the two luminaries <note>The Sun and the Moon.</note>, cut it into small pieces or shavings. Sprinkle these with powdered **Myrrh** and a very small amount of **Aloe** (otherwise it becomes far too bitter). Afterward, soak the pieces for several days in **Spirit of Wine** <note>Ethanol or high-proof alcohol.</note>; let it be hung up for a short time and then soaked again. Finally, let the pieces dry while suspended in the air. At this stage, the flesh will resemble meat preserved by smoke, without any foul odor. After this, a deep red **Tincture** should be extracted according to the art, using either Spirit of Wine or **Spirit of Elderberry**.

One may also soak olive oil separately with the dried, cut-up Mummy for a month (for any moisture causes an intolerable stench during the digestion process). Once the oil is thus colored, this infused olive oil can be added as desired to the Tincture of Mummy before it is mixed with the **Theriac**.

Take, therefore, half a pound of the Tincture or Extract of Mummy from which the Spirit has been drawn off.

Four ounces of **Andromachus’s Theriac** <note>A legendary "universal antidote" containing dozens of ingredients, including viper's flesh, used since the Roman era.</note>.

Two drachms each of **Salt of Pearls** and **Salt of Corals**.

Mix and digest by circulation <note>An alchemical process where a substance is heated so that its vapors condense and return to the liquid in a continuous cycle.</note> for a month.

->*Powers, Use, and Dosage*<-

Many diseases are perfectly cured by this **Theriac of Mummy**.

1. In the **Plague**, its power is so great that if it is administered before infection, the poison will cause no harm at all; he who uses one **scruple** <note>An apothecary unit of weight equal to about 1.3 grams.</note> in the morning hours will not be infected that same day.
One who is already infected should use half a drachm or one drachm in **Blessed Thistle water** <note>original: *aqua Cardui benedicti*; a common herbal remedy in the 17th century thought to cure almost any ailment.</note> or with Theriac.

2. In **Abscesses**, **Carbuncles**, **Anthrax**, and **Pleurisy**, one drachm is administered. Then, after six hours have passed, provide another drachm; he who lasts long enough to receive that second potion is certain of recovery.

3. Against any **Poisons**. The dose is from half a drachm to one or even two in cases of extreme necessity. If someone has swallowed poison, the stated dose is offered in one or two ounces of **oil of almonds**, so that the patient may vomit; the operation of the medicine should then be awaited while the patient remains in bed.

By this method, whatever **Animal** or **Mineral Poisons** exist are expelled.

# CHYMICA

after slow drying, either by itself or in a **Mary’s Bath** <note>original: *B. M.*, for *Balneum Mariae*; a double boiler used for gentle heating</note>, it is reduced to a **fine powder** <note>original: *Alcohol*; in early modern chemistry, this term referred to a substance ground to its most subtle, powdered state</note>. When taken internally for medical use, it drives **Poison** out through the skin, just like the **Theamedes Stone** <note>A legendary mineral mentioned by Pliny the Elder that supposedly repels iron, acting as the polar opposite of a magnet</note> which thrusts iron far away from itself. If anyone should refuse to agree with this testimony and experiment, let them not condemn the truth until they have first achieved what is here witnessed, or the contrary. <margin>Wheat is not had without tares, nor is honey found without its sting.</margin>
The efficacy of this medicine will not cause wonder to those who know that, in Nature, a **Medicine** often lies hidden right beside the greatest **Poison**. And because evils exist by nature coupled with a greater good, many peoples eat **Viper flesh**, claiming it brings long life; they do this with no preceding horror and no subsequent danger. Therefore, it is not without cause that **Baldus Angelus** <note>Baldus Angelus Abbatius, a 16th-century Italian physician who wrote a famous treatise on the nature of vipers</note> in his booklet on the *Admirable Nature of Vipers* breaks out into the following words: 
> One thing comes to my mind as being truly admirable: that by the cunning of a Serpent, death entered into the world; yet it is also a wonder that by the killing of the viper serpent and the use of its flesh, one is cured of all the most serious diseases and poisons and restored to a pristine state. But to be preserved from all diseases by the continuous eating of viper flesh—this surely surpasses and exceeds all wonder.

So much, kind Reader, may it suffice for the present to have discussed such...

-> B A S I L I C A <-

...concerning certain elemental, material, and internal diseases which are generated naturally from the **Entity of Nature** <note>original: *Ente Naturae*; in Paracelsian theory, this refers to the physical constitution and biological functions of the individual body</note>, and which draw the principles of their origin from **Obstruction** and **Tartar** <note>In early modern medicine, 'Tartar' referred to the stony or crystalline waste products that supposedly deposited in the body, causing conditions like gout, kidney stones, and hardening of the arteries</note>, as well as concerning several diseases arising from the **Entity of Poison** <note>original: *Ente Veneni*; diseases caused by toxins or the body’s inability to separate nutrients from waste</note>, and how these may be cured when the body is strengthened by the medicines properly assigned by Nature.

<margin>
The **Entities of diseases** according to **Paracelsus** are five. For he divides diseases into **Natural** ones, which are comprised of four Entities—namely the **Natural**, the **Astral**, the **Poisonous**, and the **Spiritual**—and into a fifth, the **Scourge**, which is the **Entity of God** <note>original: *Ens Deale*; diseases considered to be divine punishment or tests of faith, requiring prayer and repentance rather than just herbs</note>.
</margin>

Concerning **Astral**, **Spiritual**, **Imaginary**, and **Votive** diseases <note>diseases caused by the will or "vows," often related to curses or mental states</note>, as well as **Incantations** arising from the **Entity of the Stars** <note>original: *Ente Astrorum*</note> or of the **Spirit**, **Paracelsus** wrote specific books to which I refer the eager reader. For just as diseases arising from corrupted food and drink, or from animals, vegetables, and the fruits of the earth, are healed with the **Secrets** <note>original: *Arcanis*; the hidden, purified "essences" of a substance in alchemy</note> of herbs and roots, or as they are healed by minerals and metals with their own **Secrets** (provided they reject the Secrets of vegetables), in exactly the same way, the greatest part of diseases coming from **celestial influence** and from the **Astral Impression** of the **Firmament of the Macrocosm** <note>original: *maioris mundi*; the 'Greater World' or the universe, as opposed to the 'Microcosm' or man</note> does not wish to be cured with indiscriminate remedies, such as the Secrets of herbs, minerals, or metals. Instead, the cure must be established through **Astronomical Influence**, using at least those things which have an analogy to the Macrocosm and Microcosm. In these things, there is a true **Magnetic force** of the Firmament and a **Celestial Impression** capable of resisting diseases from the Firmament of the Macrocosm and the Microcosm, just as appears in **Persicaria** <note>Smartweed</note>, **Lesser Goldenrod**, **Dragonwort** <note>original: *Dracunculo*</note>, and **Greater Comfrey**.

<margin>
These **Sidereal and Firmamental infections** are known and cured **Firmamentally** by the **Adept Physician** <note>An 'Adept' is a master of alchemy and nature’s secrets</note>. For **Adept Medicine** is the Art which gives the knowledge to recognize and expel Firmamental infections.
</margin>

If a disease or pain has been brought on **Supernaturally** through incantation or the **Magical Impression** of the "Ascendants" <note>Astrological positions rising on the horizon</note>, then the healing efforts of the first three Entities are useless; but according to Paracelsus—

<margin>
The **Magnet of man** is a **Magical Cure**, in which there is a heavenly **Impression** <note>In alchemy, an "impression" is a celestial or spiritual influence stamped upon a physical substance</note> after contact with a plant; as the plant rots, it draws the medicine into the ulcer and thus heals it.
</margin>

One must proceed **Magically** and **Supernaturally**, and the evil must be repelled in the same manner by which it was brought. Otherwise, in the aforementioned **Simples** <note>term: Simples; individual medicinal herbs used on their own rather than in complex mixtures</note> there is an **Influential** attraction, and all things—by Divine ordinance—heal **Magically**, **Astronomically**, and **Magnetically**. This is because the medicine exists within the plants themselves, and within **Man**, there is a **Magnet**. For just as the Sun and the Stars possess the power of drawing moisture from the lower regions, so too does Man (by his own innate magnetic-attractive power, like a **Magnet** drawing iron, pulling the spirit of nourishment into himself). The lower things likewise have the same power of drawing from the Higher, as we see during a time of **Plague** <note>original: *Pestis*</note>. These attractions are **Natural**; they are not sorcery, incantations, or superstitions. 

The origin of diseases must therefore be sought from their own principle, and only then should the cure be established. Furthermore, the natures and properties of diseases are varied, as **Phaedro** <note>Likely referring to Georgius Phaedro, a 16th-century Paracelsian physician</note> most diligently noted when he said: Certain diseases allow for remedies applied both externally and internally. Certain external diseases and internal ulcers do not tolerate remedies. There are even certain internal diseases which tolerate no applied remedies at all, neither external nor internal. Furthermore, there are certain diseases, both internal and external, which are cured only by **Words** in which an **Influence** has been impressed according to the art. Some are cured by **Constellated Herbs** <note>term: Constellated Herbs; plants harvested at specific times when the stars and planets are in a favorable alignment to enhance their healing power</note>, and some refuse to be cured by remedies, constellated herbs, or the use of words. For example, someone might cure a wound or ulcer with **Sanicle** <note>original: *Diapensia*</note> or **Lady’s Mantle** <note>original: *Alchimilla*</note> by fixing a knife into the earth near the plant's location, being careful, however, that the root is not pricked by the knife; otherwise, the patient would be incurable. In this way, he relates how a certain old woman cured various **Cancers** <note>original: *Carcinomata*; referring here to malignant or "eating" ulcers</note> using only **Lady's Mantle** applied to the cancerous ulcer.

## MOST EFFECTIVE WOUND BALSAM
### FOR HEALING

> *By which all wounds and punctures of the limbs, joints, and nerves—even those strikes made by a weapon or a lead bullet—can be safely cured without any resulting infection or symptoms.*

Let the flowers be collected at the **Balsamic sunrise** <note>A specific astrological timing, likely referring to the moon's balsamic phase or a specific celestial alignment favorable for harvesting medicinal plants</note>.

Let all these things digest together again for fourteen days. At the last, let the spirit of wine be drawn off in a **Bain-Marie** <note>term: Balneum Mariae; a water bath used for gentle distillation</note>; then the **Balsam** will remain at the bottom, red as blood.

In winter, if the seeds of the aforementioned herbs are available, they may be ground and cast into the Balsam and placed in digestion; this will make the remedy operate far more powerfully.

## STICTIC PLASTER.

In the composition of every healing Stictic Plaster, according to **Paracelsus** <note>The famous Swiss-German physician and alchemist (1493–1541) who revolutionized medicine by using chemicals and minerals</note>, four ingredients of different kinds must be considered.
1. **Healing**, which is achieved by means of **Wax** and **Colophony** <note>term: Colophonia; a type of rosin or distilled resin from pine trees used to provide stickiness</note>.
1. <note>The original text repeats '1' here, though it is the second point</note> **Accidents** <note>original: Accidentia; in a medical context, these are complications or secondary symptoms like pain or swelling</note>, which are removed and prevented by the benefit of gums, namely **Opoponax**, **Galbanum**, **Sagapenum**, **Bdellium**, **Ammoniacum**, and **Elemi** <note>These are various aromatic resins and medicinal gums derived from plants, prized for their ability to soothe and protect</note>.
3. **Putrefaction** (for even a wound without complications is liable to rot, which generates worms and the growth of "bad flesh" <note>likely referring to gangrene or proud flesh/granulation tissue</note>), which is removed and guarded against by the help of the great **consolidatives** <note>substances believed to knit flesh back together</note>, namely **Mastic**, **Myrrh**, and similar items.

### *Mode of Use*

Let one ounce be dissolved in one pound of rain or river water—not spring water. After filtration and the removal of the dregs, we use the clear water.

# SALT, BUTTER, SUGAR
## OR HONEY OF SATURN <note>In alchemy, "Saturn" is the name given to the metal Lead.</note>

Let **Red Lead** <note>original: Minium</note> or **White Lead** <note>original: Cerussa</note>, and unadulterated **Chalk**, be moistened with distilled wine vinegar, mixed, and dried. Upon the ground material, pour distilled vinegar to a height of three or four finger-breadths. Let it stand in a warm place—but not in a **heated room** <note>original: hypocausto; a room heated by a furnace, often used as a living space</note> where people dwell, for the vapor of this vinegar infused over Lead is harmful—for two days, or in ashes, stirring it four times daily during digestion. The vinegar will change to a yellow color and a sweet taste. The vessels should be of glass, for earthenware ones leak. Pour it off and repeat the work by pouring on new vinegar, until it is no longer colored or becomes sweet. 

Draw off the vinegar in a **Water-bath** <note>original: Balneo [Mariae]; a gentle heating method using hot water</note>, and a gum will remain at the bottom. Pour distilled rain water upon this so that it may be dissolved again, and let the remaining dregs of the vinegar fall to the bottom. Continue to pour fresh water on the residue until it extracts nothing further. Evaporate the filtered water, and you will have a **Salt** <term>Lead Acetate; historically called "Sugar of Lead" because of its dangerously sweet taste</term> which, in a damp cellar, is resolved into an oil. The Salt prepared the first time can be slightly **calcined** <note>heated to a high temperature to remove volatile substances</note>—at least enough so that the finer spirits do not fly away—and ground on marble. Distilled vinegar is then poured on it again, so that it may be dissolved in turn in the ashes.

# THE COMPOUND OF SPERNIOLA.
<note>original: Sperniola; a term used in early modern medicine for preparations derived from frog spawn, valued for its cooling properties.</note>

In March, let the **Frog Spawn** <note>original: Sperma Ranarum</note> be distilled by itself in a **water bath** <note>original: Balneo; a gentle heating method using hot water</note>. It should be collected three days before the **New Moon**; for in this way, it does not smell foul. Once you have this Water:

Take of selected **Myrrh**.
Of **Frankincense**, two ounces of each.
Of ground **Saffron**, half an ounce.
Of **Camphor**, three drams.

Grind them all and mix: it is appropriate to let this powder soak in a glass vessel with the distilled **Frog Spawn Water** twenty or thirty times. However, it must always be allowed to dry naturally on its own before the next soaking; afterwards, it is to be kept for its intended uses. Internally, a quantity the size of half a **hazelnut** is given in **Plantain** water for **internal hemorrhaging** <note>internal bleeding</note>, specifically in cases where all other remedies have proved useless.

->*Uses & Powers.*<-

1. By its cooling nature, it coagulates the blood: for to stop internal bleeding from the nostrils and the throat, when all other hope is lost, three or four grains may be safely administered internally in **Shepherd's Purse** <note>original: Bursa Pastoris; a common herb used historically to stop bleeding</note> water.
2. If it is dissolved with **vinegar** and applied externally to **Erysipelas** <note>a bacterial skin infection, often called "St. Anthony’s Fire"</note> or to the hot pains of **Gout** <note>original: Podagra</note>, it is of great benefit.
3. It stops the external bleeding of wounds through direct application.
4. If it is applied to a **Felon** <note>original: Panaritio; a painful infection of the fingertip or nail bed</note> for two hours, it kills the infection; or one may apply a leather **finger-stall** that has been repeatedly soaked in the liquid and dried.

### A COSMETIC AGAINST FACIAL BLEMISHES.

Take a half-pound of the best **purified Mercury**, from which all blackness has been diligently washed away. Afterward, mix it in an unglazed earthenware bowl with an equal amount of powdered **Sublimate Mercury** <note>original: Mercurii sublimati; a highly toxic form of mercury used in early chemistry as a base for cosmetics and medicines</note>. Place everything into an **alembic** <note>a chemical vessel used for distillation</note> with a narrow opening, and pour **distilled vinegar** over it to the height of three or four fingers. Let it stand for three or four days, stirring it several times each day. This process extracts a **white powder**. Remove the whitish vinegar by tilting the vessel; save the white powder that naturally settles to the bottom after several days, once the vinegar is discarded. This labor should be repeated very frequently until you have a sufficient supply of that white powder. Dry the powder by itself and store it for use. It is not corrosive; therefore, unless you wish to, it requires no further washing.

-> *Usage.* <-

It is applied externally by mixing it with one's own **saliva** or with **Bean water** and smearing it on the skin. It is used against all **facial blemishes**, as well as **Ringworm** <note>original: Serpiginem; a term for spreading skin rashes or fungal infections</note>. Furthermore, it is a great **incarnative** <term>Incarnativum; a medicine that promotes the growth of new flesh to heal wounds</term> medicine.

# THE SYMPATHETIC OINTMENT, OR THE
## STELLAR OINTMENT OF PARACELSUS.

Take fat of a wild boar
->and of a bear, eight loth <note>original: lotones; a Germanic unit of weight equivalent to about half an ounce</note> each.<-
->The older the animals, the better the fat.<-

Let the fat of both animals first boil in **red wine** for half an hour over a slow fire; afterward, let it be poured over cold water and the floating fat gathered with a spoon; whatever sinks to the bottom should be discarded.

Afterward, take two pints <note>original: sextarios; an ancient unit of volume</note> of **earthworms** washed in wine or water; let them be roasted in a covered pot in a baker’s oven—care must be taken, however, that they are not scorched—then let them be ground into a powder.

->Take of this powder,<-
->dried boar’s brain,<-
->fragrant red sandalwood,<-
->mummy <note>original: Mumiae; in early modern medicine, "mummy" referred to the remains of embalmed human bodies, believed to possess great healing power</note>,<-
->and hematite <note>original: Haematit.; a reddish iron ore often called bloodstone</note>, one ounce of each:<-

Finally, take the **moss** <note>original: Usneæ; specifically the lichen *Usnea cranii humani*</note> scraped from the **skull of a man** who perished by a violent death, gathered while the **Moon is waxing** and situated in a "good house" <note>an astrological reference to the favorable position of the moon in the zodiac</note>—in **Venus** if possible, and not in **Mars** or **Saturn**—about the weight of two hazelnuts. From all these ingredients, ground and mixed together with the fat according to the art <note>original: secundum artem; a standard instruction for professional pharmaceutical preparation</note>, let an **ointment** be made, to be carefully reserved for its uses in a sealed glass or box.

If by chance the ointment should dry out over time, it can be moistened and softened anew with the aforementioned fat or with **virgin honey**.

# Let the Ointment be Prepared when the Sun is in Libra.

## *The Use and Powers of this Sympathetic Ointment.*

This cure is not accomplished through witchcraft <note>original: Veneficia; often implying sorcery or harmful magic</note>, as foolish and unskilled people believe, but through the magnetic, attractive power of this medicine, caused by the stars. This power is brought to and joined with the wound by means of the air, so that its spiritual <note>meaning "refined" or "incorporeal" rather than religious</note> operation might be brought into effect.

I say it occurs because of an astral and elemental conjunction: for just as the heat of the Sun corresponds with the Earth, so the smartweed <note>original: Persicaria; a plant commonly used in folk medicine, believed to draw out heat or disease</note> corresponds with the disease; when the Sun leaves, the heat leaves, and so it is here.

There are therefore three things that cause such a wonderful effect through this ointment:

1. The Sympathy of Nature.
2. The influence of the celestial bodies, completing their operations through the Elements.
3. The Balm <note>original: Balsamum; in Paracelsian thought, this refers to the "Internal Balm," the body's own natural healing force</note>, which is naturally endowed to every human, gifted with the power of healing.

With this ointment, all wounds are healed—regardless of the weapon, blow, or throw, and no matter the sex of the person—provided that neither the nerves, arteries, nor one of the three principal members <note>referring to the heart, brain, or liver</note> has been damaged. This holds true as long as the weapon can be obtained, even if the patient is many miles away from us. And because it is of a binding, purifying <note>original: suppurantis; here meaning the drawing out of waste to allow for healing</note>, and renewing nature, it does not allow any harmful symptoms to arise if applied in the proper way.

->Observations.<-

1. Let the weapon <note>original: telum; this refers to the physical object—sword, knife, or arrow—that caused the injury</note> by which the person was wounded be anointed once every day if necessity urges and the wound is huge; otherwise, it is sufficient to have anointed it on the second or third day. Let it be kept in a clean linen cloth and in a lukewarm place, not too hot, lest harm be brought to the patient. Care must also be taken that no dust falls upon the weapon, nor that the wind blows on it in a cold place; otherwise, the patient would be driven to insanity.

2. Before you anoint the weapon, consider whether the wound was made by a puncture; if it was, let that instrument be anointed from the top downwards (and not from the bottom up), otherwise harm would be brought to the sick person.

3. If indeed you cannot know how deeply or in what manner the weapon entered the flesh, you may anoint the whole thing; otherwise, it is sufficient to have anointed only the part of the weapon that caused the injury.

4. It is not necessary to sew up the wound in the manner of barber-surgeons <note>original: barbitonsorum; in the early modern period, barbers performed minor surgeries and wound care</note>, but at least to wrap it daily in a clean linen cloth that has first been moistened in the patient's urine.

5. On the day that one anoints the weapon, he should abstain from Venus <note>original: Venere; a common medical euphemism for sexual intercourse, believed to deplete the body's vital spirits</note>.

6. Before the anointing of the weapon, the bleeding must also be stopped very quickly in the wounded person.

7. In fractures and the breaking of bones, you may add some powder of Comfrey <note>original: Symphyti majoris; historically known as "knitbone" for its supposed ability to heal fractures</note> to the ointment, or some from the roots of Black Hellebore.

Once you have the weapon that caused the injury, and you desire to know whether the patient is going to die or survive, you shall test it thus:

If you sprinkle the finest powder of **Red Sandalwood** <note>original: Sandalo rubro; a fragrant wood often used in alchemy for its cooling properties</note> and **Hematite** <note>original: Haematit.; also known as bloodstone, used symbolically and medicinally to treat blood-related issues</note> upon that weapon <note>original: telo</note> after it has been heated over coals to such a degree that you can still hold your hand over it: if it then sweats drops of blood, the patient will die; if not, he will recover.
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;But if we wish to know whether the patient is conducting himself correctly regarding **drink** and other requirements <note>likely referring to dietary or behavioral restrictions mentioned on the previous page, such as abstaining from sexual intercourse</note>, 
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;this is recognized when spots of blood appear in the dressing; 
if not, then he is behaving well.

->It is further to be noted<-

I. Even if the arms or the weapon are not in your possession, any opening of the skin or violent injury from which blood flows can nonetheless be healed by this **Ointment**. This is done by moistening a small **willow splinter** <term>lignellum salicinetum; a small piece of willow wood used here as a biological bridge to carry the patient's blood to the salve</term> in the bloody wound; after the adhering blood has dried (not by the heat of the Sun or Fire, but spontaneously and by itself), it is finally thrust into the aforementioned **Ointment** kept in its **small box** <note>original: pixide</note>, leaving it inside.

II. If the wound should happen to be large and deep, it can be cleansed every morning and bound with a fresh linen cloth, without any other use of external oils, ointments, or similar things. Then this wound, in whatever way it was inflicted, heals by itself; it is sufficient for the splinter, having been first moistened once in the opening or the bloody wound, to remain thrust into the ointment box until full healing is achieved.

III. However, as often as any new wound is to be healed, a fresh splinter is always required.

IV. If indeed the wound will not emit blood, it must be <term>scarified</term> <note>original: scarificandum; the practice of making small, shallow cuts in the skin to induce bleeding</note> with the splinter until blood flows out: So also in do-

<page-num>282</page-num>
<header>B A S I L I C A</header>

To heal the pain of the teeth <note>original: lore dentium sanando</note>, let the aching tooth be scraped with a small scalpel until it bleeds; after the blood has dried upon the scalpel, let the tool be smeared with this **ointment**, and thus the pain is immediately calmed.

If a horse should be pierced in the foot by a nail, let the nail first be pulled out and smeared with the ointment, and the horse's foot will be cured quickly, without any formation of pus <note>original: suppuratione</note>.

In the same manner, all animals having flesh and bones can be cured.

<margin>Exodus 15:26; Wisdom of Solomon 16:12</margin>
May the **Supreme Physician** <note>original: Summus Medicus; referring to God</note>, by whose **WORD** <note>original: VERBO; referencing the biblical idea that God's word is the ultimate healing agent</note> the medicine created by Him is finally made effective, grant His grace and blessing for the legitimate use of these things to all who use them rightly and piously: to the Most High alone be praises and thanks, lasting and perpetual, **AMEN**.

# EPILOGUE.

From now on, let those arrogant, boastful Academic braggarts <term>Thrasones Academici; Thraso was a stock character of a boastful, puffed-up soldier in Roman comedy</term> cease their reviling of **Chemical Medicines**. These men, decreeing by their own perceived majesty with threats and violent rebukes, have until now foolishly mocked, condemned, and treated with a thousand insults the faithful Truth and divine science of our ancestors. Let them cease, I say, to brand the disciples of **Hermes** <note>referring to Hermes Trismegistus, the legendary founder of alchemy</note> with marks of infamy, envy, ignorance, and fraud, and to demand hereafter ocular demonstrations and manifest proofs of our operations: likewise, in their unusual and new way of learning, let them cease to imperiously demand from the "Coal-burners" <term>Carbonariis; a derogatory term used by university doctors to mock alchemists for the soot and fire of their laboratories</term>, whom they so call—

<header>C H Y M I C A.</header>

It behooves physicians to seek out **Spagyric Secrets** <term>Spagyrica; alchemical medicine involving the separation and recombination of natural substances</term>, which, inspired by divine power, I have candidly shared this time for the benefit of the Commonwealth from a full storehouse <note>original: "pleno horreo"; suggesting he is not holding back any knowledge</note>. Meanwhile, I ask this one thing of the most fierce Avenger of every falsehood and injustice <note>referring to God</note> with the highest prayers: that He grant and bestow grace and every blessing in the act of healing upon all who—with an ardent invocation of the help of Almighty **GOD**, and with a grateful heart—shall rightly use these prepared medicines for the praise and glory of the Creator, for the benefit of their needy neighbor, and for the sincere and rightful honor of the unfairly maligned **Chemical Art** <note>original: "arti Chymicæ immeritò proclamatæ"</note>. After recognizing the generosity of God, let them acknowledge these Spagyric gifts as received for the public good.

However, for those unworthy mockers and those who secretly use these gifts of God while maintaining a feigned contempt (as it is manifest that many idle **Galenists** <term>Galenicos; followers of the ancient physician Galen who typically opposed "chemical" or Paracelsian medicine</term> have done until now, secretly hunting for praise and esteem for themselves from the labors of others), and who meanwhile do not cease to attack their **Spagyric** benefactors with malicious treachery, whether by word or by writing—may everything turn out the opposite for them.

That this may be firm and settled, may that most Holy **TRINITY** grant it—He who gave me the will and the ability to consecrate to the memory of perpetual posterity these Chemical labors and these **Spagyric grains** plucked from the chaff <note>original: "grana Spagyrica è paleis eruta"; a metaphor for extracting truth from useless matter</note>, which have been examined most deeply and frequently with the greatest of studies. And let the entire **Spagyric Senate and People** <note>original: "Senatus Populusq; Spagyricus"; a playful reference to the Roman "SPQR," here meaning the whole community of chemical practitioners</note> say with me from the bottom of their hearts, **AMEN**.

<term>Signatures</term>
<note>The "Doctrine of Signatures" was a foundational concept in early modern medicine and botany. It proposed that God had marked every natural substance with a physical sign—a "signature"—that revealed its hidden healing properties. For example, a plant with heart-shaped leaves was believed to treat heart conditions, while a yellow flower might be used to treat jaundice.</note>

*...sed, presenting and representing a most delightful spectacle. *Because of this dignity of the Medical Art and the utility which it provides to the human race, those men deserve well of mortal affairs who strain every nerve of their intellect in increasing and illuminating it, sparing—as far as possible—neither expense nor labor. Indeed, nothing can be more excellent, and nothing more praiseworthy for a man, than to deserve well of the human race in any way possible, and to bind more closely to our own efforts that knowledge which we receive from Nature. Carefully weighing this, I have directed my focus there with every effort since my early youth, so that according to my ability, just as I was inclined toward all liberal arts and noble studies, so too by a certain peculiar inclination and propensity toward the most useful <term>stirpium cognitionem|knowledge of plants; specifically the study of stems and roots</term> and other natural things, I myself might also bring something for the common use of life, for the sake of aiding the <term>Reipubl.|Commonwealth</term> <note>The "Medical Commonwealth" (Respublica Medica) was a common Renaissance term for the international community of physicians and scholars.</note> and propagating Truth through my studies and labors, and thus be judged to have deserved well of it. ### DEDICATION.

This herbal medicine, which I discuss here, Most Illustrious Prince, discovered by Chiron <note>In Greek mythology, the centaur Chiron was the tutor of heroes and the originator of the medicinal arts.</note>, has always been held in great esteem and cultivated by the zeal and industry of great men. Indeed, the Roman Emperors and ancient Kings showed a wonderful devotion to the investigation of plants—in the cultivation and illustration, I say, of botanical matters. The fame of some among their number still flourishes, and will flourish as long as the herbs named after them remain green. Nor is so much praise, admiration, and glory owed to this study solely because its knowledge is pleasant and delightful, but also because it is exceedingly useful and exists as a necessity for all of human life. Therefore, if Your Highness is ever permitted to breathe from public business, may you apply yourself to this study and contemplation; in it, may you delight yourself through the remembrance of the Creator’s wonderful wisdom, and behold the manifest footprints of Divinity impressed upon the secrets of Nature, for:

->And every herb reflects the present God.<-
<note>original Latin: "Præsentemq; refert quælibet Herba Deum."</note>

I know Your Highness is accustomed to take the greatest pleasure from the reading of Natural Philosophy <term>Natural Philosophy|The study of nature and the physical universe that preceded the modern era of specialized science.</term>, and that even amidst your most grave and continuous cares and business for the glory of God and the safety of the Fatherland—in which you are engaged day and night—you do not neglect to devote certain spare hours to the various studies of the sciences. Since Your Highness is thus proclaimed by all, I have come forward boldly to you with the dedication of this book, especially because that most noble and distinguished man, **Theobaldus Hock of Zweibrücken**, Your Illustrious Highness's most worthy and intimate counselor; and furthermore those most renowned men, outstanding in their learning, **Matthias Timinus of Ottenfelt** and **Hermanus Bulderus**, who are present as medical counselors to Your Highness and who all most faithfully revere Your Highness, have very often praised your prudence, humanity,

# EPISTOLA

*...and Liberality <note>original: "Liberalitatem"</note> worthy of such a Heroic Prince and widely known, have wonderfully and with the best right commended themselves to me. I thought it would be worth the effort, therefore, if I dedicated these* **Correspondences of Signatures** <term>Signatures|The "Doctrine of Signatures" was the belief that a plant's physical appearance—its shape, color, or texture—provided a divine clue to its medicinal use (e.g., a walnut looking like a brain to treat head ailments).</term>*, like planks gathered from a shipwreck, contracted into one body to spare the reader the trouble of searching, and comprised in a clear brevity, elegant order, and proper sequence, to* **Your Name**, *which is not subject to any oblivion, through this publication,* **Most Praiseworthy Prince**. *I do this not only because of your aforementioned Excellent and Heroic gifts of mind—namely your remarkable Piety, exceptional Prudence, singular Erudition, and incredible Humanity—but also because* **Your Highness** *has deserved so well of literature and the professors of letters. You exclude no one from the assembly of the* **Muses** <note>The nine Greek goddesses who presided over the arts and sciences.</note>, *nor do you dismiss anyone in sadness as* **Augustus** *was known to do, but gladly bear them in your ears and eyes after the example of that best Emperor* **Trajan** <note>The Roman Emperor Trajan was famous for his accessibility and kindness toward his subjects, contrasting with the more distant Augustus.</note>. *You show yourself approachable, just as* **Cicero** *praises in* **Pompey**, *with a perennial and never-fading reputation for your Name, just as the following most learned Letter, written to me in* **Your Highness’s** *own hand, provides most abundant proof of your innate kindness, for the perpetual memory of the matter.*

*Therefore, I humbly ask* **Your Highness** *to allow these nighttime labors of mine, the first fruits of my efforts (an eternal monument of my study and humble devotion), to go forth into public protected under the most honored splendor and patronage of* **Your Highness’s Name**. *May you receive them with a kind face and a liberal hand, and not disdain to embrace me with the favor of your kindness in the future—as you have most mercifully done until now—and to keep me recommended to you.* **God, the Best and Greatest** <note>original: "Deus Optimus Maximus"</note>, *who governs the hearts of Princes, who alone can bring about successful governments, and who bestows the Wisdom by which Princes rule, keep* **Your Highness** *safe and unharmed in all most happy prosperity...*

# DEDICATION

...may He keep you safe for as long as possible. For by the peculiar favor of the **Divine Power**, while **Your Highness**, in this your venerable **graying age**, precedes all the **Princes of Europe** in longevity, nevertheless that old age is still seen to be so vigorous <note>original: *viridis*, literally "green" or "youthful"</note> that, although according to the course of **Nature** the powers of mind and body usually weaken and diminish as age grows heavy, in your case they are perceived to grow younger daily, like a miracle, and the sharpness of your **Intellect** is found to increase.

<margin>The Rosenberg Ursini family <note>The Rosenbergs claimed a prestigious, though likely fabricated, connection to the Roman Orsini family to bolster their status.</note> traces its lineage to the Roman Orsini Princes, who themselves originate from the Lords of Ascania and Ballenstedt in the Harz region (who were surnamed Beer and Beringer).</margin>
Just as that most ancient **Branch** of the Illustrious House of **Rosenberg**, born and descended from the first **Trunk** of its origin—namely the most ancient and most praised **Lineage** of the **Anhaltinians** and **Ascanians**—has continued to emerge and flourish through so many centuries by its heroic virtues and deeds in the company of Emperors and Kings: so also I pray to Almighty God with the highest petitions that, since in Your Highness the last sprout of the said branch now begins to fade and end by inevitable fate (for in this sublunary globe, where all things are subject to change, there is no constant permanence), nevertheless that **Ancestral** and **Heroic** implanted virtue may flourish, bloom, and put forth leaves in **Your Highness's Sons**, late grandsons, and great-grandsons, by the blessing of **GOD**, through an ever-new budding of offspring in the Trunk that shall endure (namely, the most virtuous leaders of the same illustrious **ANHALT** lineage), with the perennial glory and honor of the Name and of the one and kindred **FAMILY**, never dying in any age.

->for the benefit of the Christian Commonwealth and the Fatherland, under the unceasing Di-<-

# **Epigrams by Nicolaus Majus**, Councilor of Appeals to His Holy Imperial Majesty, on the Alchemical Works of **Oswald Croll**.

**I**t is no small thing to know the powers and mysteries of nature,
*And it is no small thing to have offered aid with a healer's hand.*
*But you, CROLL, provide something even greater, while you offer chemical*
*Remedies, which certain Reason teaches are more than sufficient.*
*And those things which long Experience has granted you*
*Through your knowledge, you now make manifest for the common Good.*
*Go forth, O glory of true medicine; go forth and continue to be worthy*
*In your devotion; you shall see worthy rewards for yourself from heaven.*

### Another by the Same Author.

**I**t is a work of great art, if one knows the innermost secrets of things,
*And from that knowledge has applied healing hands.*
*But it is a work of even greater merit to be able to teach the remedies*
*Which Reason and eyewitness Faith <note>original: *Fides oculata*; literally "eyed faith." This is a philosophical and legal term used in the Renaissance to emphasize empirical evidence—knowledge gained through seeing and direct experience rather than hearsay.</note> themselves provide.*
*Since you have achieved these things, CROLL, your glory is well-deserved.*
*Let others be envious, for they cannot imitate your deeds.*

# **Of Nicolaus Maius, Councilor to His Holy Imperial Majesty**
## **in the Court of Appeals, an Epigram on the death of**
## **Oswald Croll, the Alchemist.**

> Whatever flourishes in the lands, and whatever wise nature
> Might hide in her inner depths,
> I have found through you, Croll; provided in the chemical pledges,
> The medicines <note>original: *Pharmaca*; the Greek-derived term for drugs or remedies, which Croll famously synthesized through "Chymical" means.</note> which sound Reason and experience teach.
> And while long labor grants its trials to you,
> It gathers individual honeys into one for the common Good.
> Wipe away [sorrow] with the medicines given; though dogmas may perish,
> You see for yourself the long threads of fate.

### Another by the Same Author.

> This golden wisdom captured in these small pages,
> Croll, how it stands out, flourishing with art in so few words!
> But your works will hold greater inscribed monuments,
> Which the laws of fate’s old age <note>original: *fati... anus*; literally "the old woman of fate," a personification of time and decay as an elderly woman who eventually claims all things.</note> will never be strong enough to break.
> In this way, Croll inserts his own name and his teachings into fame,
> So that his day of glory shall never perish.
