# ON SIGNATURES, OR THE TRUE AND LIVING 
# ANATOMY OF THE GREATER AND 
# LESSER WORLD,
# BY OSWALD CROLL,
## HERMETIC PHYSICIAN AND PHILOSOPHER,
### PREFACE TO THE READER.

---

<margin>
The place in which God is said to have stood, and from the sign, God Himself or His essence is known: for all creatures, by their properties, demonstrate God as if present.
</margin>

<image-desc>Decorative woodcut initial 'V' depicting a person standing in a garden landscape with large, stylized plants.</image-desc>Would that the Botanists of our time—who, being ignorant of internal form, know only the matter, substance, and body of Herbs—would apply such diligent care in discerning the Signatures of Plants as they do in their accurate and often frivolous disputes over names. If they did, a far richer and more fruitful utility would overflow from there into the Medical Republic <note>original: *Respunlica Medica*; a common Renaissance term for the collective community and knowledge of the medical profession</note>. Since most people, however (as is usually the case in almost all arts), have abandoned the sweet and pithy kernel of the Sciences, and like commoners lacking internal eyes and considering only the external face of things, are busy only with the outer bitter bark, it follows that many "Nomenclators" <note>namers or catalogers</note> of herbs are found. These men magnificently describe only the lodgings, habitations, and external garments of Plants (in which their powers reside as if in houses). But as for the inhabitant—the trace of the invisible God in His creatures, the Shadow, the Image of the Creator impressed upon His creatures, or that internal force and secret power of operation, which is a gift of Nature to the plant like a Soul instilled and infused by the most high God—this they ignore. This inhabitant must be investigated by the wise physician: first through the signature and the mutual, analogical sympathy and "conspiracy" <note>original: *conspirationem*; literally a "breathing together," referring to the harmonious relationship between different parts of the universe</note> of the members of the Plant’s body, and then it is to be unearthed by the industrious work of Vulcan <term>Vulcan: a reference to the Roman god of fire, used here as a metaphor for the alchemical process of using heat to extract the essence of a substance</term> or the anatomical knife...

<summary>This page introduces Croll’s "Doctrine of Signatures," arguing that botanists should focus on the hidden "soul" and divine signs of plants rather than just their external names and shapes. He posits that God has left physical clues in nature that reveal the medicinal uses of plants to the "internal eyes" of a wise physician.</summary>

# PREFACE

*...ses <note>completing "houses" from the previous page</note> to be unearthed, they sluggishly and with harmful silence pass over. As for those many irregular <note>original: *Heteroclitas*; meaning unusual or deviating from the norm</note> powers which they ascribe to individual herbs—copied from the records of others without any personal effort and without a clear foundation or separation of truth from falsehood—experience alone, the one and only mistress of things, proves that these do not satisfy even a tenth part of the eager expectations of physicians and patients. We do not need a great deduction of reasons if Experience, the Mother of Truth, deserves trust.*

<margin>Diverse and manifold forms are the signs for investigating each and every mystery.</margin>

*Therefore, there is a need for sharper eyes, a higher intellect, and subtler investigators if we wish to grasp a full and intimate knowledge of plants (the kind of knowledge that Nature has left to be explored and carefully examined by studious lovers and admirers of natural things). This is better than being able to distinguish some hundreds of them at first glance in a common way by their names, without knowledge of their internal Virtue <note>In this context, "Virtue" refers to the specific medicinal power or "life force" of the plant</note>. For the names of herbs do not possess virtues; therefore the bodies themselves must be examined so that we may know what purges, what gives fragrance, and what heals fevers or wounds. Nor should we wish to explore their powers by the unjust and deceptive assessment of the "four qualities"—namely Heat, Coldness, Moisture, and Dryness <note>Croll is rejecting the traditional Galenic system of medicine, which classified all plants and diseases according to these four basic states</note>—when nevertheless those are—*

<margin>The qualities of "simples" <note>individual medicinal herbs</note> are not to be considered, but rather their secrets.</margin>

*merely the shadows of things; just as colors have neither roots nor powers. This will not be denied by those who—knowing the Virtue from the root of the Center and not from the surface—leave behind the subtlety of empty names and search out the intimate truth from the things themselves with profound speculation. They more exquisitely examine the manifest traces of Nature imprinted by God in hidden things, and they hunt for the hidden gifts of herbs by inspection of their external appearance. They know how great a difference there is between the bark and the kernel, between the house and the tenant—unless they foolishly wish to label wood and stones with the name of "statues," or, having abandoned the farmers, attempt to harvest only the huts. In all external things, the house is merely the dwelling of the internal inhabiting virtues, infused by God into the body like the Soul into a human body. That Philosopher <note>A reference to Socrates</note> more rightly sought the character and senses of men not from a name, but from speech (the true indication of the mind or the internal Man), when he addressed a boy standing by in silence: "Speak, that I may see you, O youth!"—since the secret movements of the mind are opened by the voice of the interpreter. In the same way, Herbs "magically" speak through their Signature to the physician who gazes deeply into them, and they manifest their interiors—hidden in the silent secrecy of Nature—to him through a likeness. For there is (to use the words of the most famous man, Giambattista della Porta <note>An Italian scholar (1535–1615) whose work "Phytognomonica" argued that plant shapes reveal their uses</note>) a method of demonstrating through likeness by which the supreme Architect of Things is very often accustomed to reveal divine and occult things, so that the supreme [beauty] of Ideas...*

### ON SIGNATURES

...might reflect a similarity: nor could it have been done in a more excellent or elegant way. For if we imagine a plant speaking, and wanting to bring forth the secret benefits of its Nature (in which it excels) in any spoken language or mode of speaking, it would not be understood by everyone, since both speech and written characters are proper and peculiar to individual nations. Thus, it would have been necessary to speak either to a single nation or in infinite languages. Instead, by its clever Nature and skill, through the similarities of things, it speaks to all people at once, both briefly and clearly enough. All herbs, flowers, trees, and other things coming from the Earth are magical books and signs communicated by the immense mercy of GOD—not because those signs themselves are our medicine, but because through the knowledge of them we can arrive at the true medicine, that is, the *signatum* <note>original: *signatum*; the internal essence or power "signified" by the outward appearance</note>. Therefore, he who desires to be an experienced physician and possesses knowledge of those things which pertain to him, let him learn through that art—which nature proposes externally through signs—what those things signify internally. For everything that is intrinsic bears the external Figure of that hidden thing, in both sensible and insensible Creatures. While we are silent, Nature speaks as if by certain notes, and reveals the character and habits of each thing, just as was shrewdly said by Adamantius, the translator of Polemon: <gloss>original Greek: "There is an outward appearance of those who are silent, but Nature speaks as if through signs, thus revealing the character of each thing."</gloss> And just as our innermost character can be investigated from the outermost marks of the body, so from the exterior signs of Plants, Man can be alerted to their interior powers. For the plant, as if with hidden words, reports its powers to sick mortals and reveals the treasures of hidden things, so that Man—the most miserable of all—might learn how to bring help to his own diseases. Just as external features lead us into a knowledge of the Internal Man and his diseases, so also the medicines necessary and conducive to Man are discovered from a similar Anatomy: for they are of the same Astronomy and Philosophy. Moreover, Magic <note>Natural Magic was considered the highest form of natural science in this period, focusing on the hidden "sympathies" between things</note> gives the knowledge of the secret Virtue <note>The specific medicinal power or "life force"</note>; Magic is the teacher in the Light of Nature, and the most perfect and consummate Science of all Natural Philosophy. And truly nothing increases Piety more, nothing (I say) promotes us more ardently toward the worship of GOD and His love, than the true Knowledge of Him, than the unceasing Contemplation of the immense works and wonders of GOD, than that Natural Magic (always declaring and suggesting the internal kernel or *signatum* to us through the external bark or sign), the offspring of Heaven and daughter of the arts and discoverer of secrets, by which we are compelled to sing: <margin>Palmistry <note>original: *Chiromantia*</note>, derived from the Kabbalistic art, is called the Discoverer of medicine.</margin> The Heavens are full, all the Earth is full of the Majesty of Your glory, Almighty Creator! <meta>This page continues Croll’s preface, shifting from the "language" of plants to the practical application of local mineral and botanical resources. ### PREFACE

<margin>
A physician, like a Virgin, ought to see those things which are before his feet, not ambitiously seek out things beyond the seas: the product of his own Region is sufficient.
</margin>
Let us see that it has been so arranged by Nature among men that they admire foreign and imported talents, while they despise their own domestic ones due to familiar use. Thus it also happens to these admirers of foreign plants that, in their zeal for novelty, they hold in contempt their own domestic products which our world brings forth. Yet these are far better, fresher, more select, and more healthful, because they were born under the influence of our sky and are more suited to each of our natures. Collected at the proper time at home, they can be obtained with less difficulty and expense, and were destined for our use by the Father of mercies in our time of need. What necessity is there, then, to use foreign things if our own Earth produces the same and similar efficacy? Thus medical use has taught that the medicated earth <note>original: *Terram medicatam*; likely referring to *Terra Sigillata*, a medicinal clay traditionally imported from Lemnos or Turkey</note>, which GOD has given us in many places in Germany, does not yield in efficacy, goodness, and virtue to the Turkish variety. I speak of the Silesian kind from Striga, which Johannes Montanus—an old man of deep experience—first discovered. After him, it was found in many places in Germany by Johannes Bartoldus of Oschatz, a Silesian and a curious and diligent searcher of underground things, in the district of Solms and several places in Hesse. Not far from Lake Acromius <note>likely Lake Ammersee</note> in the domain of the Illustrious Maximilian, Marshal of Pappenheim, near the Fortress which takes its name from a long stone <note>likely Langenstein</note>, a great abundance was once dug up from a certain scattered rock. It was enclosed by Nature in a covering or matrix like a highly purified nut, as the traces still testify there today, and I have used it in medical practice with success. Our most August Emperor RUDOLPH the Second took care to have dug up in his garden at Brandeis <note>original: *Brundusij*; likely Brandýs nad Labem in Bohemia, where Rudolph II had a castle and gardens</note>, besides the medicinal clay, two "fats" of the SUN and MOON <note>original: *SOLIS & LUNÆ axungias*; Paracelsian terms for refined mineral essences associated with gold/sun and silver/moon</note>, as Paracelsus calls them. Having received a part of these as a gift from His Majesty and used them in medicine, I have observed their proven goodness and found them to be a heap of true Lemnian earth, most effective, and not yielding to the Turkish Earth.

<margin>
We are ignorant of the power of many things only because of our negligence in experimenting.
</margin>
Thus GOD has bestowed resources upon us in various places. Although the true Unicorn <note>The horn of the narwhal or the mythical unicorn, highly prized as an anti-venom</note> is of great price due to its rarity, there is another <term>unfettered <note>original Greek: *ἀνεξαπόλυτον* (*anexapolytos*); here used to mean a mineral or fossilized version that is more readily available</note></term> variety which they call "Mineral" and is sometimes dug out of ponds or mountains. For example, once in Moravia, three miles from Brno (where I was practicing medicine at that time with the most distinguished man, Dr. Johannes Berger of Pannonia), not far from the territory of the Abbot of Obrowitz, the bones of two unknown animals of unusual magnitude, together with two younger ones, were dug up under a very high cliff. Without doubt, these perished in that solitude during the time of the Great Flood by the force of the waters. Coming to those places by chance several months later, I saw some remains of those bones and marvelous teeth, and admiring—

...the origin of that thing: I took care to dig it up: and in medical use I found nearly the same efficacy in it that can be attributed to the unicorn’s horn <note>original: *monocerotis Cornu*; often refers to fossilized mammoth tusks or narwhal horns used in early modern medicine to detect and neutralize poisons</note>. In the same region, not far off, is an amazing cave, not unlike the one excavated in a mountain in Italy at *Villa Costozza*, between Padua and Vicenza, in which various and wonderful works of *Nature at play* <note>original: *Naturæ ludentis*; a common Renaissance concept where nature creates shapes resembling art or other objects for "sport" or "whim"</note> are found, while dripping drops from the upper vault in that hollow mountain, entangled with many labyrinths, immediately congeal into stone (by means of the *spirit of salt* <term>spirit of salt: an alchemical term for an acidic principle thought to govern crystallization and the "fixing" of minerals</term>) of their own accord, and by their long fall, they form various stone statues and shapes. Furthermore, that stone, when reduced to dust at the weight of a dram, is accustomed to effectively induce sweat; and when mixed with suitable *Plasters* for broken and bruised bones, it is applied with the greatest benefit. If it is dissolved into salt by the benefit of distilled vinegar, it works effectively in cases of *the Stone* <note>kidney or bladder stones</note> and those knotty conditions of *Gout* <note>original: *Podagricis*</note> because of its signature. For Nature has provided for these two diseases—which are very common in *Moravia* along with Contractions <note>muscle or tendon stiffness</note> due to the "stony" wines <note>original: *cæmentosa vina*; wines thought to contain mineral impurities that caused stones and gout in the local population</note>—with suitable, innate, and domestic *Remedies*. Where some evil or disease exists, there Nature provides a timely Remedy nearby, so that we need not beg for it from far away. Therefore *Ruellius* <note>Jean Ruel, a French physician and botanist (1474–1537)</note> says not without merit: *No part of medicine is more uncertain than that which is sought from another world than our own.* And *Paracelsus*, that most diligent searcher of the *Light of Nature*, rightly laughing at the exotic curiosity of many physicians who desire to know *Plants* only by name (neglecting their internal powers to be sought from their signatures), affirms that any peasant has a True *Pharmacy* <note>original: *Pharmacopolium*</note> before his own house.

<margin>
The Earth is God’s pharmacy and there is nothing that cannot be achieved by the power of herbs if the powers of many were not unknown. When we can help with simple medicines, we should not work with compounds.
</margin>

Those who cure with the simplest herbs and roots cure most successfully of all, as *Carrichter* <note>Bartholomaeus Carrichter, 16th-century physician to Maximilian II, known for combining herbalism with astrology</note> testifies: *For the medical essence or Magic Gold <note>original: *Aurum magicum*; a term for the most refined, life-giving essence of a substance</note> is contained just as well in them as in other more precious things.* Just as the earth provides food and clothing for every Region—if not for superfluous luxury, then at least enough for necessity—so also Nature, the mother and parent of all things, who has provided abundantly for everyone, has distributed a necessary sufficiency of medicines. Each Fatherland contains within itself the matrices <term>matrices: in Paracelsian philosophy, the elemental "wombs" or environments that give birth to specific minerals or plants</term> of its own Element, and provides for itself what is necessary. Nature produces and tempers herbs for each of its lands and regions, for its people, its climate, its sky, and its era. Since the male and female gender are found in these, just as in stalks (for *Divine Providence* distinguished the anatomy into *Male* and *Female* in Created things not in vain), the sexes should not be rashly confused in their application and use. For as man and woman are distinct by Nature, so also are their *Remedies*, so that I may for now remain silent about

### ON SIGNATURES

...in a spiritual manner, which appear bodily in this visible world: and that all things flow from within into the composite whole, and nothing is taken from without, the *Light of Nature* <note>original: *Naturæ Lumen*. In the Renaissance, this referred to the innate intelligence or guiding force found within the physical world that reveals hidden truths.</note> itself proves and demonstrates this by ascending and descending, entering and stripping away. <margin>Whatever exists in all worlds simultaneously is also contained in each individual one; nor is there any one among them in which all things that are in the individuals do not exist, as witnessed by *Anaxagoras, Pythagoras, and Plato.*</margin> Three worlds are numbered, and these three are one universe, since one world is within another: **GOD**, namely, **ANGELS**, and the **VISIBLE MACHINE** <note>original: *Machina Visibilis*. This refers to the physical universe, viewed as a grand, divinely-ordered mechanism.</note>. Each lower world is ruled by a higher one and receives the influence of its powers, so that the *Archetype* <term>Archetype: The original divine pattern or "blueprint" in the mind of God from which all things are modeled.</term> and supreme craftsman may pour through the *Angels, Heavens, Stars, Elements, Animals, Planets, Metals, and Stones*—the virtues of omnipotence—and from there into us, for whose service He established and created all these things. 

<margin>*Genesis 28:12–13*</margin> Entry or ascent occurs when I am raised from the lowest to the highest via *Jacob’s Ladder*: from sensible things to things of the mind, ascending from the Creatures to the Creator himself. The *Hebrew Cabalists* <note>original: *Hebræorum Cabalistæ*. Mystics who studied the hidden symbolic meanings of the Hebrew scriptures.</note> call these the Fifty Gates of Understanding; they are the steps or boundaries of all things collected from the first chapter of Genesis, by which—as if by symbols and signs—we are led to the knowledge of all things, both *Visible* and *Invisible*.

# ON THE SIGNATURES OF
## PLANTS, WHICH BY SIMILARITY
### REPRESENT HUMAN MEMBERS:
### THE HEAD.

1. The POPPY <note>original: *Papaver*</note> with its crown represents the Head and the Brain: therefore, a decoction made from it is usefully administered for many afflictions of the Head.

2. WALNUTS <note>original: *Juglandes*</note> possess the complete signature of the Head:
The outer hull, or the green herbaceous covering, represents the Pericranium <term>Pericranium</term> <note>The dense membrane covering the outer surface of the skull.</note>; for this reason, a salt made from these hulls is singular for treating wounds of the Pericranium.
The harder inner hull, or the woody shell, represents the Skull.
The thin skin surrounding the kernel represents the Meninges <term>Meninges</term> <note>The membranes that envelope the brain.</note> and the membranes of the brain.
The kernel itself has the shape of the Brain: therefore, it is also beneficial for the brain and dulls poisons. Indeed, if the crushed kernel is moistened with the Quintessence of wine <term>Quintessence</term> <note>In early medicine, the "fifth essence" or purest distillation of a substance; here, it refers to highly rectified spirit or brandy.</note> and applied to the crown of the head, it powerfully strengthens the brain and the head.

3. The bud of the PEONY <note>original: *Pæoniæ*</note> flower, while still closed, has a signature and a certain analogy to the Head, complete with the sutures <term>Sutures</term> <note>The zig-zagging joints where the bones of the skull meet.</note> and the small veins surrounding the brain. The flowers, when they are about to bloom, break open the outer skin representing the Skull; in this way—and by the way the seed later leaps out like a lightning bolt—they expel Epilepsy or the "star-struck" disease <term>Syderatum morbum</term> <note>original: *Syderatum morbum*. A historical term for a sudden stroke or paralysis, once believed to be caused by a "blast" from the stars or planets.</note>.

4. AGARIC <term>Agaric</term> <note>Specifically *Laricifomes officinalis*, a wood-decay fungus that grows on larch trees, long used in traditional medicine as a potent purgative.</note> is an outgrowth of the Larch tree, much like a fungus, and it purges the head.

## OF THE HAIR.

2. Long **moss** adhering to trees looks like hair; its decoction is similarly recommended in cases of hair loss.

3. A certain herb grows in marshes which deeply resembles long hairs in its form; it floats on the water and is distinguished by a small white flower. Its decoction is also beneficial (just like the previous ones applied externally) for the shedding of hair.

4. **MAIDENHAIR FERN** <note>original: *Adiantum*</note>, **MAIDENHAIR SPLEENWORT** <note>original: *Trichomanes*</note>, and the **POLYTRICHUM** <note>original: *Politrychon*</note> of Apuleius <note>Referring to the author of an influential 4th-century herbal.</note> are also "hair-like" plants; with their somewhat stiff curls and slender fibers, they express the appearance of hair, and they make the locks thick, curly, and more beautiful.

5. **THAPSIA** <note>original: *Thapsia*; a plant in the carrot family often called "deadly carrot."</note> with its fennel-like or hair-like leaf: **Avicenna** <note>A famous Persian physician (980–1037) whose "Canon of Medicine" was a standard European text for centuries.</note> says it has no equal in covering the head with hair in cases of **alopecia** <term>alopecia</term> <note>A medical term for baldness or hair loss.</note>.

## OF THE TEETH.

1. In **Henbane** <note>original: *Hyoscyamus*</note>, the receptacle or the seed-pods have the shape of a molar tooth. Therefore, its oil or the liquid expressed from it, or a decoction of the root with the herb **Smartweed** <note>original: *Persicaria*</note> in vinegar, used as a warm wash, most effectively stops toothaches.
2. **Pomegranate seeds** <note>original: *Acini Mali Punici*</note> represent teeth; a decoction is effective for ailments of the gums and for the firmness of teeth.
3. **Pine nuts** <note>original: *Pinei Nuclei*</note> closely resemble incisor teeth; for this reason, pine leaves boiled with vinegar soothe the pains of the teeth.
4. **Toothwort** <note>original: *Dentaria Herba*</note>, whose root is seen to be formed by a wondrous artifice of Nature into a compact series of scales <note>The scaly, white rhizome of this plant looks remarkably like a row of human teeth.</note>.

## OF THE THROAT.

1. **Wintergreen** <note>original: *Pyrola*</note>, which is therefore used in gargles.
2. **Bellwort** <note>original: *Uvularia*; named for its resemblance to the uvula hanging in the back of the throat.</note>.
3. **Throatwort** <note>original: *Cervicaria*; derived from the Latin *cervix*, referring to the neck or throat.</note>.

## OF THE LIVER.

1. **Liverwort** <note>original: *Hepatica*</note> and **Lichen**.
2. **Birch Fungus** <note>original: *Fungus Betulinus*</note> and **Oak Fungus** <note>original: *Fungus Quercinus*</note> also possess the particular "signature" of the liver, the factory of the blood <note>In the medical theories of this era, the liver was believed to be the primary organ responsible for creating blood from digested food.</note>. For this reason, the powder of both, when sprinkled, miraculously stops blood bursting forth from the nostrils or from wounds.
3. **Liver-herb** <note>original: *Jecoraria*; likely referring to a species of Marchantia</note> which clings to the walls of springs, and is particularly effective against afflictions and hard tumors <term>scirrhos: a historical term for a hard, fibrous swelling or tumor, often associated with the liver or spleen</term> of the liver.
4. **Pears** <note>original: *Pira*</note> have, in a certain way, the signature of the liver; therefore, they are also beneficial for the liver.

->ON THE INTERNAL ORGANS.<-

### OF THE HEART.

1. **The Citron** <note>original: *Citrium*</note> represents the Heart by the shape of its fruit.
2. **Yellow Monkshood** <note>original: *Anthora*</note> possesses two roots that show themselves like little hearts.
3. **Wood Sorrel** <note>original: *Alleluya*; often called "Alleluia" because it blooms between Easter and Whitsun.</note> puts forth leaves at the top of its little stems in the shape of a Heart.
4. **Lemon Balm** <note>original: *Melissophyllon*</note> bears a leaf with the appearance of a Heart.
5. **Motherwort** <note>original: *Cardiaca*</note> or **Shellflower** <note>original: *Molucca*</note> produces leaves similar to balm.
6. **Spikenard**, **Myrobalan**, and **Quinces** <note>original: *Mala Cydonia*</note>.
The qualities of all these are outstanding for the Heart.

### OF THE LUNGS.

1. **Lungwort** <note>original: *Pulmonaria*</note> clinging to both rocks and trees.
2. Certain species of **Lungwort** reflect the whitish spots of the Lung: therefore, a decoction <note>A concentrated liquor resulting from heating or boiling a substance.</note> of them all is beneficial in various afflictions of the Lungs.

### OF THE BREASTS.

**The "Eyes" of Peacock Feathers** <note>original: *Specula pennarum pavonis*; the iridescent, eye-like spots on the tail.</note>: for they have the form of Breasts and udders: therefore, when consumed <note>original: *hausta*; likely ground into a medicinal drink.</note>, they heal the ill-affected breasts of women.

### OF THE BILE.

The green, herbal husk of the **Walnut** <note>original: *Juglandis*</note>: if its juice is pressed out while green, it is similar to the juice of the **Bile** <note>original: *Fellis*; referring to the gallbladder or yellowish bile.</note> in color and taste, and it is beneficial for the cleansing of the Bile.

### OF THE SPLEEN.

1. True **Spleenwort** <note>original: *Scolopendrium*</note>, **Asplenium**, and **Ceterach**.
2. **Hart’s-Tongue Fern** <note>original: *Lingua Cervina*</note> and common **Phyllitis**.

## OF THE TESTICLES or GENITALS.

1. ### THE WOMB AND UTERUS.

1. **True Round Birthwort** <note>original: *Aristolochia rotunda vera*; the name "Aristolochia" itself means "best delivery" or "best birth" in Greek.</note> imitates the shape of the female womb and provides the best help for women in childbirth.
2. **Peas**.

7. **Lion’s Leaf** <note>original: *Leontopetalon*; a plant in the barberry family.</note>, whose root skillfully demonstrates to the viewer a resemblance to the female pubes, appearing with a downy and soft flock. <term>Dioscorides</term> <note>A Greek physician and the author of the most influential herbal of antiquity.</note> records that when worn as an amulet, it is effective for love affairs.
8. **Mace** <note>The lacy, reddish outer covering of the nutmeg seed.</note> also reflects the signature of the womb: for the mace encloses the nutmeg (which bears the signature of the fetus in the womb), just as the womb encloses the embryo.

### THE KIDNEYS.

**PURSLANE** <note>original: *Portulaca*.</note> has its signature for the Kidneys. <note>In the "Doctrine of Signatures," the fleshy, succulent leaves of purslane were thought to resemble the shape or cooling nature of the kidneys.</note>

### THE AFTERBIRTH.

**WATER LILY** <note>original: *Nymphæa*.</note> has the signature of this. Therefore it also expels the Afterbirth <note>original: *Secundinam*; the placenta and membranes expelled after childbirth.</note>.

### THE SPINE.

1. **HORSETAIL** <note>original: *Equisetum*; its jointed, segmented stems were seen as a physical map of the vertebrae.</note>.
2. **Female Fern**: therefore its decoction (for sciatica and pains of the Spine) and a fomentation <note>A warm, medicinal soak or poultice.</note> made from wine and water applied over many days is a most excellent remedy according to the art of signatures: for it clearly represents the image of the backbone.

### THE SHINS AND BONES.

1. **GRACE OF GOD** <note>original: *Gratia Dei*; likely referring to the herb Hedge Hyssop or a species of Geranium.</note> or **GERANIUM** has the signature of the Shin Bone: therefore its powder is exceptional for broken bones.
2. **BONE-BINDER** <note>original: *Ossisana*; likely *Osteocolla*, a mineral deposit found in sandy soil that resembles bone.</note> or **Sandy Stone** found near Speyer and Darmstadt, is miraculous in bonding together broken bones, and that because of its <term>Magical signature</term> <note>Here, "magical" refers to the occult or hidden properties of nature that create a sympathetic link between a mineral and the human body.</note>.

### THE NERVES AND VEINS.

1. **PLANTAIN** has a complete signature, and indeed even the <term>chiromantic</term> <note>The art of palm reading (chiromancy); the author suggests the leaf veins resemble the lines on a human hand.</note> figure of the hands and feet, since the leaves are the hands of herbs.
2. **SAVIN** <note>original: *Savina*; a type of juniper.</note> also has the signature of the veins.

### THE PORES OF THE SKIN.

The perforated leaves of **ST. JOHN’S WORT** <note>original: *Hypericon*; the leaves of *Hypericum perforatum* appear to have tiny holes when held up to the light.</note> have a signature: they remove the blockage of the pores and drive out sweat.

# SIGNATURES OF DISEASES.

## FOR APOPLEXY.
1. **LILY OF THE VALLEY**: The flower has the signature of a **DROP** <note>original: *GUTTÆ*; in older medicine, "the drop" referred to gout or to a stroke/apoplexy, where humor was thought to drop into the brain.</note>, because the flower hangs like a drop: therefore its use in this disease is great.
2. The **STONE** of a Carp: existing in a crescent shape above the eyes, it is recommended for that type of Apoplexy which attacks with twitching and contraction of the muscles above the eyes.

## FOR STONES.
Everything that expels a Stone <note>original: *Calculum*; kidney or bladder stones.</note> is <term>Magically signed</term> <note>A "magical" signature refers to a hidden physical resemblance that connects a natural object to a specific healing property.</note> by resemblance, and these things signify the disease through their own images.
1. **CRYSTAL, FLINT, CITRINE STONE, JEWISH STONE, LYNX STONE**: The urine of the Lynx congeals into stone <note>original: *Lyncis*; referring to fossilized belemnites, which were historically believed to be the petrified urine of the lynx.</note>: therefore its substance is excellent for the dripping of the bladder.
2. **STONES OF THE MICROCOSM** <note>original: *Calculus Microcosmi*; refers to stones formed within the human body, which were sometimes prepared as medicines to treat the same condition.</note>.
3. Roots of **SAXIFRAGE** <note>meaning "Stone-breaker."</note>.
4. **LITHOSPERMUM** or **GROMWELL** <note>original: *Milium Solis*; literally "Seed of the Sun."</note> which bears stones with the whiteness and roundness of pearls; because of its stony hardness, along with other stony seeds, it is effective for crushing stones.

## FOR DYSENTERY.

The root of the **YELLOW WATER IRIS** <note>original: *Acori Aquatici Lutei*; commonly known as Yellow Flag Iris.</note> dug up and collected in May is a singular amulet against dysentery when hung near the region of the stomach: for it possesses the color and signature of excrement <note>The yellow-brown color of the root was thought to mirror the bile or waste associated with intestinal distress.</note>.

3. In Epilepsy, that **CROSS** or **LITTLE BONE** <note>original: *Crux seu Ossiculum*; likely referring to a "Wormian bone" or a specific shape found in the sutures of the human skull.</note> is a most excellent medicine. This is because almost anyone being strangled is seized by epilepsy in their death-agony, while the spirit of life, blocked and seeking an exit, is suffocated: then it is necessary for the joints of the head to be separated by this violence. It is administered at the beginning of a paroxysm <note>A seizure or fit.</note> under the **Exaltation of the Moon** <note>A specific astrological timing when the Moon is at its most powerful position in the sign of Taurus.</note>.

After the fetus has been delivered, it is removed immediately, lest the womb itself should follow <note>A warning against uterine prolapse, believing the stone’s "attractive" power might pull the womb out if left too long.</note>.

### FETUSES ATTACHED TO THE WOMB <note>original: *Foetus utero adnati*; referring to complications where the fetus or placenta is abnormally adhered to the uterine wall.</note>.

The **SEEDS OF LINDEN FLOWERS** <note>original: *Grana florum tiliae*.</note> are beneficial because of their resemblance, as they grow halfway attached to the leaf above the flower stalk. 8. From a magical signature, one should observe animals that extend and contract themselves. The elephant's trunk serves as a signature for the "extension" of a hernia.</note> is useful here.

5. **BURNT VITRIOL** <note>original: *Chalcanthum*; copper or iron sulfate.</note> turns a blood-red color when heated; it miraculously checks blood breaking out from a vein in the brain or from the chest.

2. **FIGWORT** <note>original: *Scrophularia*</note> has a root rough with tubercles and gifted with nipple-like heads, with a scrofulous sod extending beneath: it helps in softening scrofulous ulcers and tubercles hardened <note>original: *glaciatis*; literally "frozen" or solidified</note> by cold humors.

## TARTAR OF THE STOMACH <note>original: *Tartari Ventriculi*; in Paracelsian medicine, "tartar" refers to stony or hardened metabolic waste that deposits in the body, much like the scale in a wine barrel or a teakettle.</note>

**DODDER** <note>original: *Cassutha* or *Cuscuta*; a parasitic climbing plant that looks like a mass of tangled threads</note> possesses a signature: its decoction is most highly recommended <note>the tangled, thread-like appearance of dodder was thought to represent the intestines or the "internal threads" of the body.</note>.

->FOR RETAINED URINE<-

1. The **MARROW** <note>original: *Medulla*; likely referring to the soft internal pith or dried remains</note> contained within the hollow of a **Goose Quill** <note>original: *Calami Anserini*</note>: when dried and crushed, it marvelously expels delayed urine when taken in wine.
2. The **SOUL of the HERRING** <note>original: *Anima Halecis*; a common name for the fish's silvery swim bladder</note> (as the common folk call it): because of its silvery color and its shape, it represents the hollow duct of the penis <note>the urethra</note>. When powdered and administered, it is most effective at inducing the flow of urine.

->FOR POISON<-

1. **DRAGON ARUM** <note>original: *Syderica* or *Dracontium Majus*</note>: in every leaf it bears the image of a serpent. From this magical sign, we are confirmed in our belief that its decoction is most effective against the strikes of serpents.
2. **LESSER DRAGONWORT** <note>original: *Dracunculus Minor*; likely *Arum italicum* or a similar species</note>: a miracle of playful Nature <note>original: *ludentis Naturae*; a common phrase for unusual or mimicry-based natural phenomena</note>, it pushes itself out of the earth at the first spring awakening of serpents, and is hidden back in the earth along with them; nor does a serpent appear at all while the plant is hidden. By this dutiful gift, Nature demonstrates the remedy and forewarns of the season of fear <note>i.e., when snakes are active</note>.
3. **BISTORT** <note>original: *Bistorta*; literally "twice-twisted"</note>, also called **Snakeroot** <note>original: *Serpentaria*</note> or **Colubrina**, used for the bites of vipers and serpents.
4. **ADDER’S-TONGUE** <note>original: *Ophioglossum*</note>: like the preceding herb, it has the shape of a serpent's tongue poised to strike.
5. Among the types of **GARLIC**, **VIPER’S GARLIC** <note>original: *Ophioscorodon*</note> is marked for this purpose.

Indeed, all plants that mimic the spotted shed skin <note>original: *Exuvium*</note> of a serpent, or show the variegated spots of vipers—even those that render the likeness of a serpent visible in every part—are powerful against their bites.

## FOR WARTS.

The **Nodes of Stalks** <note>original: *Culmorum Nodi*; the joint-like swellings found on the stems of grasses or grains</note> bear the signature of **Warts**; for this reason, warts are removed by a magnetic cure <note>In 17th-century medicine, a "magnetic cure" referred to sympathetic magic or "action at a distance," where the disease was thought to be "drawn out" of the body and transferred into an object or plant.</note> performed through them.

## FOR WOUNDS.

1. **WATER-PEPPER** <note>original: *Sapena Riparum* or *Hydropiper*; likely *Persicaria hydropiper*, known for its acrid taste</note>, which grows in slow-moving waters, heals the symptoms arising from recent **Wounds** because of the blood-colored spots on its leaves. Indeed, the flow of blood is mirrored in the blood-red stem of the **Peach-wort** <note>original: *Persicaria*; a genus of plants often featuring reddish stems or spotted leaves</note> when it is held up to the Sun. This plant is called **Terrestrial Mercury** <note>original: *Mercurius Terrestris*</note> by **Paracelsus** <note>Philippus Aureolus Theophrastus Bombastus von Hohenheim (1493–1541), a Swiss physician and alchemist who popularized the Doctrine of Signatures.</note>, who says that within it resides a **Carnal Influence** or an **Influential Attraction**—no different than how the Sun and all the stars attract things from the lower realms, and the lower realms are in turn attracted by their superiors. The drops <note>referring to the dark spots</note> on the leaves bear this signature.

2. The leaves of **ST. JOHN’S WORT** <note>original: *Hypericonis*; specifically *Hypericum perforatum*</note> appear to be punctured with countless tiny holes, as if pierced by a needle; therefore, they are useful for all external and internal injuries to the skin. And because its flowers turn into the likeness of blood after they decay, they mark its specific use for **Wounds**. <note>The "holes" are actually translucent oil glands, and the "blood" is the red pigment hypericin released when the flowers are crushed.</note>

3. **YARROW** <note>original: *Millefolium*</note> and **BETONY** <note>original: *Betonica*</note>, because of their jagged and cut-shaped leaves. <note>The shredded appearance of the leaves was thought to resemble torn flesh or surgical incisions.</note>

4. **CROSS GENTIAN** <note>original: *Gentianella* or *Cruciata*</note>, the root of which is marked through in the fashion of a **Cross**.

5. **ST. PETER’S WORT** <note>original: *Ascyrum*</note>.

6. The **ELM** <note>original: *Ulmus*</note> also has perforated leaves; and thus, all plants with perforated leaves are effective for wounds of the body.

# MEDICINES THAT HELP
## THROUGH SIMILARITY.

It should also be noted that we have discovered certain medicines provide benefit through similarity, and liberate one from diseases in a marvelous way, because one possesses the "anatomy" <note>original: *Anatomiam*; in this context, it refers to the inner essence or spiritual structure of a substance rather than just physical dissection</note> of the other; for to what should a thing be more rightly compared than to its own likeness?

**Arsenic** <note>original: *Arsenicus*; used here in a homeopathic or alchemical sense where a refined version of a poison treats the symptoms it causes</note> assists **Arsenical ulcers**: among all the fruits of the Water, there is no greater **Poison** than that found in the matter of Resins, and all the poisonous nature of Resins—as **Paracelsus** confirms—flows together into Arsenic, as if into a single body.

**MONKSHOOD** <note>original: *ACONITUM*; a highly toxic flowering plant</note> given in warm wine has been found by several highly skilled physicians to be life-saving for those struck by a **Viper** or a **Scorpion**; thus, poisons are very often "poisons to the poisoned" <note>This reflects the ancient medical idea that a second poison can "neutralize" or combat a first poison already in the system.</note>.

**THE STAG MUSHROOM** <note>original: *BOLETUS CERRINUS*; likely referring to *Elaphomyces*, or "Stag Truffles," which were historically believed to grow where deer had mated or been in heat</note> is a fungus which is used for **matters of Venus** <note>referring to aphrodisiacs or the treatment of venereal diseases</note>; it arises from the genital seed of that animal.

**THE CRAB** <note>original: *CANCER*; the Latin word for both the animal and the disease of the same name (cancer/carcinoma)</note>, because its own body is swollen, therefore soothes **Carcinomas** and **Chilblains** <note>original: *Perniunculos*; painful, itchy swellings on the skin caused by poor circulation in the cold</note> when prepared with boiled honey: the ash of river crabs is also usefully sprinkled upon them.

Likewise, a living **CRAB**, with its claws bound, is placed upon a **CANCER** <note>referring here to the tumor or sore</note> until it dies: thus "Cancer kills Cancer." If the wound becomes ulcerated, it is afterwards cured with any **opodeldoch** <note><term>opodeldoch</term>: a soap-based liniment or plaster popularized by Paracelsus, used for bruises and external pains</note>.

The powder of a **PARTRIDGE HEART** removes **HEART AILMENTS** <note>original: *CARDIACAM*; can refer to heartburn, palpitations, or general distress of the heart</note>.

If **Human Hair** is distilled, a juice emerges which, when applied as an ointment, is beneficial for **lengthening the hair**.

The pains of **COLIC** are soothed by a small piece of a newborn infant's **UMBILICAL CORD**, when it is enclosed in a silver capsule or ring and worn in such a way that it touches the flesh; I have learned this from the most certain experience of many people.

A **Human SKULL** assists in cases of **EPILEPSY**. However, the front part of the skull should be used, not the back; and a female skull should be applied to a woman, and a male skull to a man.

The ripe fruits of the **wild CUCUMBER** <note>original: *Cucumeris sylvestris*; likely the "Squirting Cucumber"</note> stain anyone who handles them lightly, for they eject their juice at the mere touch. Thus, the use of this thickened juice—or **Elaterium** <term>a potent purgative drug derived from the juice of the squirting cucumber</term>—by this magical sign, powerfully purges the **watery Humors** from the human body.

In cases of **DYSENTERY**, the greatest help is found in that red marrow which is found and dug out from the joints of stone quarries; the common people call it **Stone Liver** <note>original: *Jecur Lapideum*; likely a reference to a type of red iron-ore or hematite found in rock crevices, resembling liver in color and shape</note>.

**EPILEPSY** also affects **ELK** and **SWALLOWS**: thus, against this same disease, the right hoof of an elk's hind foot is specifically useful when worn as an **Amulet**. It is said that when a seizure comes on, the elk puts this hoof into its left ear and is freed from the paroxysm by this means <note>This was a common folk belief; the elk’s "signature" behavior of scratching its ear was interpreted as a self-cure for epilepsy</note>. From **Swallows**, a singular **Anti-Epileptic Water** is prepared.

**ELKS** <note>original: *Alces*</note> and **SWALLOWS** <note>original: *Hirundines*</note> are seized by **EPILEPSY**. Therefore, the right **HOOF** of the elk’s hind foot is specifically useful against the same disease as an **AMULET**. It is said that elks thrust this hoof into their left ear when a seizure is coming on, and in this way, they free themselves from the fit. From swallows, a singular **ANTI-EPILEPTIC WATER** is prepared.

<margin>A Man is known by the nature of the animal whose primary essence dominates within him.</margin>
<margin>Hence that saying of the Chaldeans <note>ancient Babylonian sages often cited in Renaissance philosophy</note>: Man is a varied, multiform, and leaping animal of nature.</margin>
There is nothing in the world whose property is not also found in the Human Being, the Microcosm <term>the "lesser world," representing the idea that the human body reflects the entire universe</term>. For the Glorious God did not create any creature wiser or more noble than **MAN**, because the habit and primary essence of all animals is found within him; and since he is a bundle <note>original: *fasciculus*</note> of all creatures, he molds, builds, and transforms himself into the face of all flesh and the character of every creature, like some poetic **PROTEUS** <note>a Greek sea god capable of changing his shape at will</note>. For as **Pico della Mirandola** <note>a famous Renaissance philosopher known for his "Oration on the Dignity of Man"</note>, a man most learned in hidden literature, asserts: at Man's birth, the Celestial Father implanted within him seeds of every kind and the germs of every sort of life. Whichever of these each person cultivates will grow and bear their fruit in him: if vegetable, he will become a plant; if sensual, he will grow brutish; if rational, he will turn into a heavenly animal; if intellectual, he will be an angel and a son of **GOD**; and if, by chance, no creature...

-># ON SIGNATURES<-

...they adhere to so stable and certain a union through the height of chastity, that neither reaches for a stranger’s bed. Indeed, if seized by unchaste love, they cast their eyes upon another's wife, the rest of the birds sitting around tear them to pieces—and the females do the same to other females—as Aelian <note>Claudius Aelianus (c. 175–235 AD), a Roman author whose work *On the Nature of Animals* was a primary source for animal lore in the Renaissance.</note> bears witness. In a similar way, the same author relates that Doves do not allow mating with others' wives, nor do they ever desert a marriage entered into from their very first youth, unless they are single or widowed. Regarding adultery, they are the most chaste of creatures; for once a partnership is established, the male is never separated except by death itself, nor is the female ever divided from him unless she becomes a widow. During the birth of the young, the male is present and performs every duty and care. If the female is slow in going to the nest, the male strikes her with his wings and forces her to enter; when she has laid the eggs, he compels her to sit on them. They both take turns incubating the eggs: the male by day, and the female by night. If the husband dies, the female mourns for a long time, abstaining from all food and drink, and wastes away. Such is the mutual love of Doves that the female will not even admit the male unless he has first kissed her.

**THE SLEEPY:** from the **HEDGEHOG** and **DORMICE** <note>original: *Herinaceo & Gliribus*.</note>, who sleep through the entire winter; they pass away into sleep so deeply that they can scarcely be recalled even by fire. If dissected, they remain as motionless as if dead until they are cooked; then, for the first time in the boiling water, the dissected limbs show signs of life. These creatures—not to mention the stories related by fishermen of Storks and Swallows submerged in winter and reviving in the springtime—perhaps gave their signatures to the **People in Russia**, who are said to perish in the forests during the harshest cold of winter and rise again when summer approaches <note>A common early modern myth about northern lands, where "frozen" people were said to thaw out and return to life.</note>. Furthermore, those animals that live through the winter in caves without food live off their own substance, just as we see in trees that remain green with a perpetual canopy, where the sap is the cause, which by its own thickness allows it to suffice for itself.

...they coordinate with their voice. When they descend to the earth, the Leader cries out loudly so that all may assemble and feed together; if he becomes hoarse from excessive crying, another is substituted in his place. When they journey, due to the sharpness of their senses, they form the shape of a **Triangle**, so they may more easily cut through the opposing air. Then, they gradually lift the course of their wings from both sides as if using them like oars. If the sky grows harsh and wind arises, they do not fly head-on (though they fly in a crescent-shaped cluster <note>original: "lunato globi situ" — literally a moon-shaped or crescent arrangement of the mass.</note> when it is calm), but shift themselves into a wedge formation in an instant. If they foresee an attack by an **Eagle**, they stand in a circle; drawn up in ranks like a crescent moon <note>original: "falcatae" — sickle-shaped or crescent-shaped, a term often used for curved battle lines.</note>, they present the appearance of a battle line, which causes the Eagle to retreat. In flight, they rest their necks upon the backs of those flying ahead (a behavior also seen in **Stags** when swimming across rivers), making the labor easy; when the leader tires, it moves to the back of the line to become the last. When they come to rest, the others sleep while the Leader stays awake, signaling whatever he perceives with his voice. In a similar way, the **GOOSE** performs its nightly sentry duties, constantly announcing its watch with its song <note>This likely refers to the historical legend of the sacred geese of Juno, who saved Rome from a night attack by the Gauls in 390 BCE by alertly cackling.</note>.

<margin>**SINGLE COMBAT** was taught to soldiers by...</margin> **ROOSTERS**, who are most warlike when fighting among themselves, being spirited and stubborn in their contests. Nature has granted them a certain privilege, for alone among birds they wear a crest like a helmet and spurs on their feet. When they enter a doorway, even if it is very high and lofty, they nevertheless bow their heads; pride causes this, as they are careful not to strike their crest against anything. When they are the victors in a contest, they act insolently with a boastful song, their eyes prominent, their necks proud and tall, and their sickle-shaped tails erect. The defeated bird, however, hides in silence and finds it difficult to endure his servitude.

# ON THE SIGNATURES OF NATURE #

<page-num>68</page-num>

The design of **WAGONS** was learned from **MARMOTS** <note>original: "Murmentis" — referring to the Alpine marmot. A popular piece of natural folklore claimed that marmots used one of their colony members as a living sled to transport hay.</note>, who, by lying on their backs and extending their four legs, create a cart. This is loaded by others with provisions for their future needs, and is afterwards dragged into the granary of their cave using the tail in place of a wagon-pole. For this reason, their backs are always hairless and smooth in the Autumn. The same skillful foresight is observed in the **BEAVER** (an amphibious animal), which builds itself houses on the banks of rivers with several levels and multiple floors, so that it may move upward as the river water rises and downward as it recedes. Once it has chosen a tree to be cut, whether for the building of its home or for food, it does not leave until it has completely severed it with its most fierce and sharp teeth. Just as the tree is about to fall, the beaver looks up at every stroke, lest it be crushed by lack of caution. When it goes out to gather wood, it selects one of its own kind that is a stranger or too old for active life; it places the wood upon the belly of this creature as it lies on its back. To ensure the wood does not fall, and so that the animal may serve as a vehicle, the beaver skillfully arranges the load between the legs, and thus drags the burdened animal back to its house.

Likewise, **DEER** <note>original: "Cervi"</note> taught how to remove a thorn <note>original: "Clavium," referring here to a sharp object like a nail or splinter, or a painful callus</note> stuck deep in the sole of the foot; for if they are struck by a poisoned arrow, they can eject and shake it out by eating a specific herb.

**WILD GOATS** <note>original: "Capreæ Sylvestres," likely referring to roe deer or chamois</note> that wander the mountains and feed on fragrant herbs—especially **Nard** <note>Spikenard, a valued aromatic plant in ancient medicine</note>—demonstrated the cure for **ABSCESSES** <note>original: "Vomicæ," a localized collection of pus or infection</note> to Surgeons. In these animals, blood decays beneath the skin and flesh; this gathered infection, before the abscess bursts, naturally progresses toward "ripening" <note>the process where an infection becomes localized and ready to drain</note>. Once it reaches this point, the beast—disturbed by the painful stinging of the irritating fluid—rubs itself with great pleasure against rocks and stones that are glowing white from long exposure to the sun. This continues until an opening is made for the abscess, and the entire force of the infection is poured out from its sac onto the stones, much like a ripe boil filled with "cooked" matter bursts open. Afterward, the ulcer forms a scar, and the rushing force of the blood returns to that spot, filling the area until it swells into a similar abscess once more by receding.

The **SERPENT** taught that **EYES** in poor condition should be cured with **FENNEL**. Likewise, it showed that wounds can be healed with **Adder's-tongue**, **Snakeweed**, and **Comfrey** <note>original: "Serpentinâ, Colubrinâ & Conſolidâ" — these plants were historically associated with treating snakebites or wounds due to their appearance or "signatures."</note>.

Similarly, **CATS** demonstrated the remarkable use of **VALERIAN** for strengthening the sight. In the same way, **SWALLOWS** showed that **CELANDINE** <note>original: "Chelidonia," derived from the Greek word for swallow, *chelidōn*; legend held that swallows used the juice of this plant to restore the sight of their young</note> is a herb healthy for vision, as they use it to heal the eyes of their chicks.

The **HIPPOPOTAMUS** (or "River Horse") showed the practice of **BLOODLETTING** <note>term: Venae Sectionem — the surgical opening of a vein to withdraw blood</note> and **SCARIFICATION** <note>term: Scarificationem — the practice of making shallow incisions in the skin for medical purposes</note>. When it feels weighed down by constant over-eating, it enters a reed-bed and rubs itself against the sharp stump of a reed until it breaks its veins and a sufficient amount of blood is released. Afterward, it stops the flow and heals the opening by covering it with mud or silt.

</margin>

*The most ancient wise men, whom we call Philosophers in the Greek tongue, if they discovered any Secrets <term>Arcana</term> <note>Hidden or mysterious knowledge, often pertaining to the secrets of nature or alchemy</note> of either Nature or Art, they hid them by various means and figures so that they would not become known to the wicked. In the same way, the Hermetic Philosophers <term>Philosophi Hermetici</term> <note>Followers of the mystical and alchemical tradition attributed to Hermes Trismegistus</note> were accustomed to mark the terrestrial planets <note>original: "Planetas terrestres"; in alchemy, the seven metals were believed to correspond to and be influenced by the seven celestial planets</note> with certain Hieroglyphic signs. They did this so that they might set out the metals' hidden powers or virtues to be looked upon, as if before the eyes of the understanding and observing "sons of art" <note>original: "filiis artis"; a traditional term for practitioners of alchemy</note>. However, so that such signs might be rescued from destruction or burial, I have judged that I would be doing something worthwhile if—along with the Characters of other Minerals devised by a foresighted Antiquity to keep the Profane and unworthy Commoners <term>Vulgus</term> away from this study—they are now communicated by me in a single work for the sake of Hermetic disciples and the Republic of Chemistry <term>Reipubl. Chymicæ</term> <note>The "Republic of Chemistry" refers to the international community of alchemists and early chemists who shared knowledge through symbols and texts</note>.*

### SIGNS OF THE METALS <note>original: "NOTÆ METALLORUM"</note>

| | | |
|---|---|---|
| Saturn | Lead | ♄ |
| Jupiter | Tin | ♃ |
| Mars | Iron | ♂ |
| Sun <note>original: "Sol"</note> | Gold | ☉ |
| Venus | Bronze, Copper | ♀ |

# ON THE TRUE AN-
# TIENT PHILOSOPHICAL
## MEDICINE,
<note>original: "philosophica medicina." In the 17th century, this referred to a spiritual and chemical approach to healing, often associated with alchemy and the teachings of Paracelsus, rather than just herbal remedies.</note>

### MASTER ULRICH BOLLINGER
<note>original: "M. Ulrico Bollingero." The "M." stands for Magister, an academic title indicating he was a master of arts or a teacher.</note>

## LORD OSWALD CROLL,

->*The most successful physician-chemist, etc.*<-

<meta>This page serves as a celebratory introductory poem (elegy) dedicated to Oswald Croll by Ulrich Bollinger. It establishes the spiritual and philosophical framework of the book, linking the study of nature and medicine to divine revelation.</meta>

<page-num>3</page-num>

<image-desc>A rectangular decorative headpiece featuring a symmetrical woodcut design with swirling acanthus leaves, floral blossoms, and scrolling vine motifs.</image-desc>

# ON THE TRUE ANCIENT
## PHILOSOPHICAL MEDICINE

### ELEGY,

->To OSWALD CROLL, *Philosopher & Physician*<-
->*most expert, his dearest friend,*<-

->by MASTER ULRICH BOLLINGER,<-
->*Poet Laureate.* <note>The title "Poeta Laureatus" was a prestigious honor bestowed upon distinguished poets by the Holy Roman Emperor or universities.</note><-

Oswald, my Muses <note>original: *Camœnis*; the Roman goddesses of song and inspiration, often used as a metaphor for poetic talent</note> do not possess such great power—
O Croll, great glory of the medical choir <note>original: *chori*; likely referring to the community or guild of physicians</note>—
To sing the highest praises in my humble verse,
And what hope true medicine brings to the wretched.
This is what raises our minds to the heavens,
And proclaims that the Creator is God.
Every herb proves that there is a divine power,
Which established every kind of thing for us.
Behold what nature encloses in her fertile recess,
You who believe in your heart that there are no gods.
This is what reminds us that we are gods and the descendants of gods <note>The author alludes to the Hermetic and Neoplatonic idea that the human soul shares a divine nature with the Creator.</note>,
Yet alas, it lies hidden in the shadows.

<summary>A dedicatory poem by Ulrich Bollinger praising Oswald Croll and the divine nature of "true" philosophical medicine, which sees the hand of God in every herb and natural secret.</summary>
<keywords>Oswald Croll, Ulrich Bollinger, philosophical medicine, divinity in nature, iatrochemistry, Paracelsianism, Neo-Platonism</keywords>

--- Page 552 ---
<meta>This page continues the introductory elegy by Ulrich Bollinger, shifting from the praise of Oswald Croll to a philosophical defense of "Chymistry" (Alchemy) and the Paracelsian theory of the three kingdoms of nature and the three primary substances.</meta>

<page-num>4</page-num>

<header>ELEGY</header>

Ah, how such great ignorance holds blind minds,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;And a fleeting shadow fascinates our eyes.
The traces of the ancient work do not survive today;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;The names remain scarcely known in our time.
Who knows <term>Chemistry</term><note>original: *Chymicam*; here referring to the alchemical art of extracting medicinal essences</note>, which rightly teaches how to remove
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Mute corpses from substances with the flames of <term>Vulcan</term><note>original: *Vulcani*; the Roman god of fire and the forge, used here as a metaphor for the alchemist's furnace</note>?
This is the labor, this is the task: to learn the powers of Vulcan,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;You who desire to prepare certain medicines for disease.
That <term>Lemnian God</term><note>A poetic title for Vulcan, who was famously cast down from heaven and landed on the island of Lemnos</note> perfects the whole art for you;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Let it not trouble you to have set your hands to the coals.
Take these <term>Balsams</term> which are enclosed in the triple order of things <note>The "triple order" refers to the three kingdoms of nature: vegetable, animal, and mineral</note>,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;If you have a heart for true healing.
Animals can bring health along with Plants,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;And Mineral power will also provide you with aid.
Lest the dead surface of things deceive you,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Seek for yourself the inner essences beneath the external appearances.
They speak of <term>Mercury</term>, as well as <term>Salt</term> and <term>Sulphur</term><note>These are the *Tria Prima* (Three Primaries) of Paracelsian alchemy, believed to be the fundamental spiritual and material components of all matter</note>; in these
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;You will find whatever is effective in the medical art.
There is a greater world and a lesser world <note>The Macrocosm (the universe) and the Microcosm (the human being), a central concept in Hermetic philosophy suggesting that man is a mirror of the universe</note>;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Look, how they always move in harmony through a fixed covenant?
The greater serves the lesser through pleasing medicines,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;And brings forth help for health from the triple class.
But the iron chains of a <term>Tartarean</term> God bind the human race
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;In the middle of the nights of <term>Orcus</term><note>Orcus and Tartarus refer to the dark underworld of Roman and Greek mythology; Bollinger uses this to describe the spiritual and intellectual darkness of those who reject true medicine</note>.
The hidden covenants of the world are known to few,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;As is the Medicine which is fit for its own disease.

<summary>In this poem, Bollinger argues that true medicine requires "Chymistry" (Alchemy) to extract healing essences from the three kingdoms of nature (animal, vegetable, and mineral) using the fire of the furnace. He introduces the Paracelsian concepts of the Three Primaries (Mercury, Salt, and Sulphur) and the harmony between the Macrocosm and Microcosm.</summary>
<keywords>Alchemy, Vulcan, Tria Prima, Mercury, Salt, Sulphur, Macrocosm, Microcosm, Paracelsian medicine, Three Kingdoms of Nature</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the introductory elegy by Ulrich Bollinger, transitioning from the theoretical "Chemistry" (alchemy) and the three kingdoms of nature to the divine and ancient origins of medicine, arguing that medical knowledge is a gift from God evidenced in nature and the Bible.</meta>

<page-num>5</page-num>

<header>ON ANCIENT MEDICINE</header>

<sig>aa 3</sig>

Oh, what a shame! Even those creatures lacking reason know this;
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Brute beasts themselves prepare their own cures.
When arrows stick in the backs of wild goats,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;They seek out <term>Dittany</term><note>original: *Dictamnum*; a herb famous in antiquity for its supposed ability to expel arrows and heal wounds</note>, a plant well known to them.
Nor does the hawk’s own medicinal practice remain hidden from it,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;By which it is able to sharpen its eyesight.
<term>Snake-weed</term><note>original: *Serpentina*; likely referring to bistort or another herb believed to cure venomous bites</note> is not unknown to the serpents themselves,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;And the blind bear seeks out stinging bees <note>A reference to the folk belief that bears ate honey or bees to restore their health or sight</note>.
But as for those who bear the image of the heavenly Father above,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Did God wish such things to be hidden from us?
I certainly would not believe it; rather, a wicked error has led us astray,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;While we despise these gifts in most ungrateful ways.
Woe is me! What a most perverse state of the world this is:
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;It attributes the holy gifts of God to Satan.
O grievous impiety, which rejects the holy breath of life,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;And loves darkness more than the blessings of light!
Was it then an evil Demon who bestowed these arts upon us—
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Arts which the primeval Fathers knew so well?
O happy are they to whom the Spirit of God, sent down from heaven,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Reveals these <term>secrets</term><note>original: *arcana*; the hidden mysteries or inner workings of nature</note>!
<margin>Adam</margin>
Did not the first man, ADAM, teach the names of all the plants
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;And their medicinal powers, with God as his instructor?
<margin>Jacob</margin>
From where else could JACOB have known the power of his rods <note>A reference to the Biblical story in Genesis 30, where Jacob uses peeled branches to influence the breeding of livestock</note>,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;If he had not learned well the workings of nature?
<margin>Joseph</margin>
And how could JOSEPH have kept the body of his father uncorrupted <note>A reference to the embalming of Jacob in Genesis 50</note>,
&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;&nbsp;Though it was already deprived of the light of life?

<header>ON ANCIENT MEDICINE.</header>

<margin>Hiller</margin>
The learned **HILLER** <note>Johann Hiller (1550–1599), a physician in Ansbach.</note> also knew how to drive away various diseases,
And gave healthy medicines to Ansbach <note>original: "Onoldæ"; the Latin name for the city of Ansbach in Bavaria.</note>.
<margin>Cretschmer</margin>
**CRETSCHMER** <note>Probably referring to a physician or mining expert from the mining regions of Bohemia or Saxony, skilled in mineralogy.</note> is learned in searching the mines of the earth,
Where the metals lie hidden, filling their veins.
<margin>Hessus</margin>
And **HESSUS** <note>Eutychius Hessus, a jurist who became a follower of Paracelsian medicine.</note> is truly not the last among dear friends,
He is indeed worthy of the Medical choir <note>original: "Medico choro"; a poetic way of describing the community or guild of physicians.</note>.
He previously studied the complex volumes of rigid law,
But now, **KING PARACELSUS**, he unrolls your work:
He consults for the common good if your health suffers,
Or if a heavy plague has invaded your limbs.
<margin>Maius</margin>
**MAIUS** <note>Lucas Maius (c. 1522–1598), a physician and editor of Paracelsus’s works.</note> follows him, born under a lucky star <note>original: "felici fydere"; literally "happy star."</note>,
Who translates Paracelsian books everywhere:
**MAIUS** proceeds, learned from the order of Apollo <note>Apollo was the Greek god of healing and medicine.</note>,
Now the prefect of your valley, **Joachim** <note>Referring to Joachimsthal (St. Joachim’s Valley), a famous silver mining town and center for alchemy and medicine.</note>.
<margin>Ruland</margin>

The court of our **EMPEROR** <note>original: "CÆSARIS"; referring to the Holy Roman Emperor, likely Rudolf II, who was a great patron of alchemy.</note> deservedly honors you.
Nor would I pass you by in my Muses and my song,
You who have sung of the hidden riches of Nature.
<margin>Toxites.
Suchten.</margin>
Our **TOXITES** <note>Michael Toxites (1514–1581), a famous poet and physician who edited many of Paracelsus’s manuscripts.</note>, and our **ALEXIS VON SUCHTEN** <note>Alexander von Suchten (c. 1520–1575), a chemist famous for his works on the secrets of antimony.</note>,
The one is famous for his talent, and the other for his own.
<margin>Croll</margin>
Now I return to you, **CROLL** <note>Oswald Croll (c. 1560–1609), author of the "Basilica Chymica," a definitive textbook on chemical medicine.</note>, whom great **APOLLO**
And **Mercury** gave as a distinguished physician.
The mysteries of ancient doctrine are known to you:
I have seen your **MERCURY**, your **SALT**, and your **OIL** <note>The "Tria Prima" or three primary principles of Paracelsian alchemy: Mercury (spirit), Salt (body), and Sulfur/Oil (soul).</note>.
You know what **PHOEBUS** <note>Apollo/The Sun.</note> can do, and also the **WINGED ONE OF CYLLENE** <note>original: "CYLLENIVS ALES"; a poetic title for Mercury, who was said to be born on Mount Cyllene.</note>,
And you know what that **GOD OF LEMNOS** <note>original: "LEMNIVS ille DEVS"; referring to Vulcan/Hephaestus, the god of fire and smithing, symbolizing the alchemist's furnace.</note> can achieve.

# ELEGY ON ANCIENT MEDICINE.

<meta>catchword: ENCO-</meta>

From this, the harmony of the triple world <note>The "triple world" in Paracelsian philosophy refers to the three realms: the terrestrial (elemental), the celestial (sidereal), and the spiritual (archetypal), all of which a physician must understand.</note> obeys you,
In which that ancient medicine of things lies hidden.
Yet you do not wish to hide this so great a talent <note>original: "talentum"; here referring to the biblical "Parable of the Talents," suggesting that knowledge is a gift from God that must be invested rather than buried.</note>,
As do those whom the bitter malice of envy possesses.
For this present little book will be able to show many things,
Which you allow to be shared with all other men.
You also; what you prepared for yourself with great toil <note>original: "magno tibi cum sudore"; literally "with much sweat."</note>
While traveling through the regions of Italy and France <note>original: "Latias Franciacasq́; plagas"; Latium (the region around Rome) and Francia. The author highlights the scholar's extensive travels to gather medical wisdom.</note>,
You now release into the clear air for the common good
The remedies <term>pharmaca</term> <note>original: "pharmaca"; Greek-derived term for medicines or chemical preparations.</note> hitherto enclosed in your secret breast.
Because of this, posterity will deservedly owe you thanks;
Future generations will be more learned because of your writings.
Be honored in your gift, and despise the remaining profane ones <note>The "profane" refers to those who practice medicine without spiritual or chemical understanding.</note>,
For great rewards await you in heaven.

Most distinguished and *wise men: so that an outstanding and memorable example of the singular and special Mercy and Goodness of God, the Best and Greatest, toward our most beloved homeland might remain for all posterity, I wished to insert in this place an **Encomium** <note>A formal literary tribute or work of praise.</note> of that land, written some time ago in verse by a friend. This poem was printed in **Strasbourg** <note>original: "Argentoratum"; a major European center for printing and intellectual life.</note> in the year [15]95, and now, by means of this second publication, it is dedicated by me to you as an appendix to my book, as a mark of my gratitude and respect. I do this for the specific purpose that you, along with distant future generations, may always be mindful of these blessings and ceaselessly join me in giving thanks to God. For by His favorable blessing, He has raised up from our land many learned men, all at nearly the same time—more, perhaps (if I may be forgiven for speaking the truth), than have come forth from almost any other city in all Europe, however famous. Thus, what the **Ithacan** <note>original: "Ithacus"; a reference to Odysseus, the hero of Homer’s Odyssey.</note> says of his own country might deservedly be applied to ours: although it may be barren and rugged, it is nevertheless a **nurser of youth** <note>original: "κουροτρόφον" (*kourotrophon*); a Greek epithet used by Homer to describe a land that, despite its harsh terrain, produces excellent men.</note>. Beyond the aforementioned abundance of learned men, I can furthermore assert this: scarcely*

# ENCOMIUM OF WETTERAU
## THE ATHENS OF HESSE.

*Others will praise Jerusalem <note>original: "Solymam", a poetic name for Jerusalem.</note>, or Persian Susa,*
*Or the city of Cecrops <note>original: "Cecropis vrbem"; referring to Athens, founded by the mythical king Cecrops.</note>, which in ages past produced*
*Men outstanding in the learned arts, famous throughout the world:*
*Yet you, **WETTERAU**, recently surrounded by high walls,*
*You who rejoice to be called by that ancient name,*
*Where the soldier of Drusus <note>Nero Claudius Drusus (38–9 BC), a Roman general who campaigned in Germania and established forts in the Wetterau region.</note> used to place his ancient camps,*
*You shall be deservedly praised by the Muses of Bollinger <note>original: "Bollingeri"; referring to Nikolaus Bollinger, a contemporary poet and scholar.</note>.*
  *It is not only because nature has gifted you with rich goods,*
*And abundance enriches your fields with a fertile horn of plenty,*
*And Aeolus <note>The Greek god of the winds.</note> tempers the breezes to be both mild and healthy,*
*From which vigorous strength grows in hard-working limbs.*
  *It is not only because the Nymphs prepare wreaths for you in various patterns,*
*And clapping they lead the dances, and the Oreades <note>Mountain nymphs.</note> play*
*With the hairy Satyrs, and the Dryads <note>Tree nymphs.</note> there, clothed in high foliage,*
*Hold their kingdoms and frequent the forest coverts.*
  *It is not only because you have no small offspring of wild beasts*
*In the forest, and the leafy vales <note>original: "tempe"; a reference to the Vale of Tempe in Greece, used here to mean any beautiful valley.</note> smile all around:*
*Every kind of bird is both around and above,*
*Soothing the air with song as they fly through the light.*
  *It is not only because large rivers flow down for you from springs*
*And fish-bearing lakes (from which pleasing dishes are prepared),*
*And because in your lap is a great quantity of various metals*

### OF WETTERAU.

He reveals the path to the stars: born from noble blood,
That famous **Johann Croll**, <note>original: *Ioannes Crollius*; Johann Croll (1530–1582) was a Reformed theologian from the Wetterau who served as a pastor and teacher.</note> interpreter of Christ,
Whom the German youth admired while he was teaching—
Youth who were then ignorant of the language of the **Allobroges** <note>The *Allobroges* were an ancient Gallic tribe near Geneva; the author uses this term poetically to refer to the French language spoken in Geneva.</note>—at the time when he
Showed the sacred rites by the well-known waters of **Lake Geneva**. <note>original: *Lemanni*; referring to Lake Geneva (Lacus Lemanus) where Croll worked alongside other Reformers.</note>
Who could count those learned in the Law and skilled in the codes
Whom **WETTERAU** has sired: look upon the **Vulteius** brothers,
**Hermann** along with **Christopher**, who in managing affairs
Excel equally; both are most reliable authors
For providing benefit through good counsel: the Abbot of **Hersfeld**
Consults the former; Prince **Ludwig** honors the latter. <note>Hermann Vultejus (1555–1634) was a renowned professor of law at the University of Marburg. Prince Ludwig refers to Landgrave Ludwig IV of Hesse-Marburg.</note>
Look upon the **Pincier** family, joined by kindred blood,
From among them **Ludwig** traveled far to the **Elbe** [River]
And to the bay of the **Kattegat**, <note>original: *Codani*; the *Sinus Codanus* was a classical name for the waters around Denmark and the Baltic Sea.</note> rendering his laws to the people of **Lübeck**.
**Johann**, good in eloquence while life remained,
Served not rarely as an ambassador to the court of the **Emperor**
And the **Austrian** Duke: now, deprived of his light, <note>A poetic idiom for being dead.</note> he is mourned by
The Arbiter of the Empire, and by **Belgium**, <note>In this period, *Belgia* referred broadly to the Seventeen Provinces of the Netherlands, then suffering through the Eighty Years' War.</note> bristling with mournful wars,
To which he took care to restore a gentle peace.
Now behold for me the three **Gernandus** brothers in order,
Whom **Themis** and the sisters of **Themis**, **Charis** and **Suadela**, <note>Themis (Justice), Charis (Grace), and Suadela (Persuasion) are personifications of the qualities required for a great lawyer and orator.</note>
Adorn with rivalry: add **Calvinus** to these besides. <note>Likely Justus Calvinus (c. 1550–1606), a scholar and jurist from the Wetterau region, rather than the more famous French reformer John Calvin.</note>
What is fitting, what is shameful, what the rule of conduct is,
He will tell you better than **Chrysippus** or **Crantor**. <note>Chrysippus and Crantor were famous ancient Greek philosophers; the author claims Calvinus is a superior teacher of ethics.</note>
Nor shall you depart unmentioned by our songs,
**Porphyry Croll**, who by the exact standard of the law...
